reviewText:
Its power and toughness are equal to the number of creatures you control. Note that it's not on your side of the field; anybody trying to swipe your monsters won't bring its beat-status down. So build up a field, whether keen tokens or speedy cheap drops, and beef it up.

Whenever it hits a player for combat damage, it populates. (If you don't know what populate means, it lists it on this card.)
That's great for building up any tokens you've made, especially since you have token options in every color! So besides just doing a populate on something in Selesnya (8/8 GW vigilant Elemental tokens from "Grove of the Guardian" 's ability, for example), you can do that with Vraska's black Assassin tokens in Standard, or any token allies from the Zendikar block (blue/white in the case of a friend of mine) in Modern. Bant decks, Naya decks, any multi-color shenanigans that have some focus on creature-based damage.

Note too that it says when it deals combat damage to a "player", not "opponent". This means if you have some creative way of hitting yourself and not regretting it (or just get its damage redirected to your face instead of their's), you still populate.

It's a wonderful beater later-game for three anyways, whether you populate with it or not. But with that ability, why wouldn't you?

I got this for my 6-month old daughter.  I think it is overrated and way over-priced for what it is.  This is not a $50 toy, maybe a $25 toy.  The best parts about it are that it has a mirror (all babies love mirrors) and the height is good so that the baby can see in the mirror while sitting up.  But the musical aspects are not good.  The worst part is that the thing never really shuts off.  The music will continue to come on randomly long after the baby has stopped playing with it.  I have searched and cannot find an OFF button anywhere.  It's enough to drive a mother crazy!  Also the tunes are not pleasant - very electronic sounding and too loud.  It is also not very interactive at all.

We received the LeapFrog Learn & Groove Musical Table as a gift at the same time, and it is a far superior toy for a better price. It is more interactive, the tunes are pleasant to listen to, and it has an OFF button.  I would recommend buying that instead, and just make sure the baby has another mirror somewhere to look in, because that is the only strong point for this toy.

reviewText:
Ive got three kids, 9, 5 & 2, all of whom are at least as iPad fluent as I am, probably more so for the oldest. They were all interested, to varying degrees, in this app-connected toy, even if the boys didn't love that it was pink, and my youngest mostly just wanted to play with the actual, physical Furby. (And be careful, because the electronic elements, make this a delicate physical toy.)

The large-eyed, big-eared plush sings and mumbles cutely, and even snores as it goes to sleep when you apply its adorable, but kind of futzy, sleep mask. (Which, when the kids inevitably lose the tiny thing, can be activated by just pushing the clear button it attaches to instead.)

My sons enjoyed the poop and fart humor  which seems to be EVERY joke  waaaayyy more than I did (distasteful), and liked the video elements, but it seems like an awfully expensive way  to let your kids watch a few random, rather boring YouTube videos.

Some of the signature elements, like feeding via the "food cannon in the app, worked only haphazardly, and my boys gave up, just finding it frustrating. The Furby would often lose connection even when immediately next to the iPad and the app, and the Furby itself, just eat batteries  the 4 AAs had to be replaced after less than an hour of play, and the iPad died at an alarming rate, too.

The eye animations are cute, and impressed the kids, when they worked, which was roughly 50% of the time. The app also quit randomly much too often, and even had to be reinstalled once, because it just hung and even an iPad forced restart wouldnt get it going again.

Its possible this experience will improve exponentially, as they work out the kinks, but right now the battery-hogging, bug-heavy app, combined with hit-or-miss interaction (and more battery eating) on the Furby itself, make this hard to recommend, despite a few impressive elements. It just seems like the sort of thing most kids will play with for a few hours when new in the first flush of excitement, and then it will be left gathering dust on a shelf, while they move on to more reliable apps that don't require toys and tech support from mom and dad to enjoy.

I like that is so tiny it can launch off your hand and fly or roll it indoors. I don't like the battery life. You get about five minutes of play time per charge. I like the appearance of the drone. It's very cute and comes with stickers.

Overall it's entertaining, but the battery life needs to improve before it's worth more than three stars.

reviewText:
This is actually my fourth Fortress Maximus. I have the original, Brave Maximus from the Japanese Robots in Disguise and now two of the Titans Return Fortress Maximus. My first is from Hasbro direct and is the SDCC version that comes with the giant sword and special packaging. Now Amazon has sent me the regular version of Fort Max to review. It's exactly the same as the SDCC one save for the lack of the sword, so I feel pretty confident in saying it just depends on if you want to pay the extra $30 for the sword. Some TF fans will feel the sword is worth it and others won't. Just note you can find both directly from Hasbro and these are the only differences.

The Titans Return Fort Max is a wonderful tribute to the original G1 Headmasters version. It looks extremely similar but the colors are a little brighter (although that could be from age on my G1 Fort Max), and the figure is far more poseable. Of course, you still get city, fortress and Giant Robot mode (several feet tall!) and Fort Max's head becomes Cerebos who is a headmaster of his own, although HIS head is no longer Galen or Spike Witwicky. It's now called Emissary, which is a weird choice, but I'm sure older TF fans pushing 40 or more will call Cerebros' head by either of its original names.

The figure is a fantastic centerpiece for any TF collection. Size-wise he's on par with the Metroplex remake although I do feel Fort Max is the more impressive of the two. Fort Max feels like he's a super poseable G1 figure rather than a modern Hasbro TF, which is awesome for nostalgia reasons. About the only thing I could ask for with this version is a smaller "Warden" style fort max to fit the current IDW comic series.

Although you might have sticker shock as first since Fortress Maximus costs $150, he is WELL worth it. This is the cityformer we've all longed for since Hasbro/Takara first started putting them out. Now I can't wait for the eventual Trypticon (and hopefully Scorponok/Black Zarack) remakes. The bottom line is that Fortress Maximus is a fantastic TF and just edges out the Takara Galavatron headmaster as my favorite first party TF of 2016 (Masterpiece Shockwave rounds out the top 3). If you're a TF fan, you probably don't need this review, or ANY review - you're going to purchase this because you already know how fantastic it is. All of the new headmasters from the Titans Return series have been terrific but this is certainly going to be the best of them. Get yourself a Fort Max before he's no longer sold.
summary: Easily the best Headmaster release ever.

After enjoying the MCX so much, I wasn't sure if I should buy the MSR, the CP Pro, or jump straight to the Blade 400, which will be my next heli. I almost went with a CP Pro since the price is close but you get a good 6 channel radio with the CP. Thing is, you get a better 6 channel transmitter with the Blade 400, so the MSR BNF still seemed like the most cost effective stepping stone.

At first, I thought I made a mistake because the MSR was much more unpredictable than the MCX, and I thought the problem was partly the imprecise basic transmitter. But after some practice, most of the the unpredictability was due to me learning single-rotor flight characteristics. The basic radio is definitely too vague and clunky for the MSR, but it is adequate.

I find the MSR a little frustrating because it can (and often does) go way too fast for indoors, but at a mere 0.8 ounces plus 0.2 for the battery, any wind blows it away. It's a great little performer without a reliable venue.

Great: Maneuverability, speed, overall durability, single rotor, sounds angry, extra tail rotor and mixing flybar, comes with two batteries (uses one at a time) and a great 4-battery charger with a wall plug.

Frustrating: Unstable in a light wind, too sporty for the basic transmitter (precision control is much better in the low rate mode, but then it lacks the control throw to move any faster than an MCX), flight time per battery is shorter than the MCX even with the 120mAh battery.

The MSR's surprising, MCX-like durability was definitely the best reason to choose it as an intro to single rotor flying.

reviewText:
I haven't shot a Super Soaker in years, so I was pretty excited to try this one out.  The design is cool, and it feels sturdy without being heavy.  Doesn't feel like its going to crack if you drop it on the driveway.  One big bummer was the lack of a trigger.  The Soaker is fired by pumping the barrel.  The green area on the underside of the barrel acts like a pump shotgun.  You pull out to 'load' then you pump it back to fire.  It decreases accuracy, but the streams are pretty thick.  My 4-year-old niece is pretty tough, and she tried playing with it, but just wasn't big enough or strong enough to aim and pump the gun.  She was kinda able to fire it straight up into the air, holding the barrel close to her face.

I counted shots when totally full.  I think it was 61 shots with the single stream, or if you slide a switch, the crossbow arms pop out and it fires three shots - about 45 times on a full tank.

Overall, its missing that satisfying trigger-pull, but it will soak whoever you're chasing around, as long as you're tall and strong enough to reach both the stock and the barrel.

Pros:
- Sturdy design
- Strong blast; thick streams of water
- Approx. 60 shots on a full tank with single stream, 45 with the crossbow arms extended
- Easy to fill and fires until fairly empty
- Cool effect flipping a switch and having the crossbow arms pop out

Cons:
- No trigger
- Recommended ages 6 and up should be followed; too hard for small children to pump

reviewText: Taking inspiration from films like the ultraviolent neo-classic gangster flick Reservoir Dogs, Ca$h & Guns is the game of what happens after the heist -- when the gangsters start fighting over the haul. What really sets this game apart is the 6 toy guns that come in every box. Everyone gets one. Each turn, 5 bills are revealed. They are each worth from $5,000 to $20,000. This is the cash the gangsters are going to fight over. Each player then chooses a "Bullet" card. (This determines the order of shooting.) Everyone points their guns at their intended target. At this point, if you "lose your nerve," that is, if too many guns are pointing at you, you can "duck out." That means you knock your little plastic piece of its stand, and you grab a "Shame" marker. Players then shoot. This means showing their Bullet card. "Bang bang bang!" shoots first. Then comes the "Bang!" cards. Anyone who gets shot takes a wound piece. Get shot 3 times, and you're done. The remaining players divvy up the cash evenly. Any cash that can't be divided up evenly (no change can be made) is added to next turn's pot. The game lasts eight turns. If you aren't dead by then, the player with the most cash wins. (You lose $5K for each Shame token.) The real fun comes when you're pointing the guns at each other. While they are made of orange foam, there is a certain suspension of disbelief that really puts you into the "movie." It's even more fun when you start throwing out your favorite one-liners. (Gangster-style profanity is known to fly!) There are a few variations that add to the mix: super powers and an undercover cop. They bring a little more longevity to the game. Admittedly, the game is largely brainless, and thrives off the heist-movie thrills. It's definitely categorized as a "filler" game. Still, it's great fun and comes highly recommended. Also check out King of Tokyo. You may also enjoy THE Book of Word Games: Parlett's Guide to 150 Great and Quick-to-Learn Word Games for game nights.

reviewText:
This is a Velocity Toys Baja off-road truck. It is 1:10 scale, 15.5" x 9.5" x 6.5". The body is lightweight and is removable. The car has a working suspension front and rear. The tires are soft and have a knobby tread and get good traction. It's fun to drive and has good power.

It uses a 7.4V battery that's really two 3.7V batteries put together. It uses a USB charger that has an indicator that changes from red to green when it's done charging. The remote has a steering wheel and a trigger and uses four AA batteries (that are not included).

The only thing about it that I thought could be better is the steering. It doesn't turn very sharply and sometimes it takes a couple of tries to get around the corner. Now that I'm more practiced I can get it around a sharp corner if I accelerate and spin the rear tires.

This would be a good choice for younger kids as it isn't overly fast and could be driven around inside on a rainy day if you have room.

reviewText:
My son and I first heard of Little Bits at a local Makers Fair.  One of the tables was run by a self-described Little Bits Evangelist and he had several interesting projects he created with these things.  We left the Fair intrigued by these products.

Son is very interested in electronics.  We had him set up with numerous Snap Circuits kits as well as other DIY project kits.  He's comfortable putting together interesting circuit designs.  This did seem like a natural fit for him...looking like it's part LEGO, part electronics, all fun.  And indeed, with this set he did do some interesting projects that were included with the kit.  He had a lot of fun designing his own satellite dish and understanding how parabolas work (for context, he's a precocious 11).

All in all, it does seem like a very open ended continuation of learning about circuits.  My kid can build certain circuits from scratch, but now with Little Bits he takes pre-made circuits and puts them all together into larger projects.  However, my complaint is twofold...

First, the target audience seems unclear to me.  The LEGO-like nature of this product along with the kid-friendly instructions for the projects make me think this is something aimed at older pre-teen kids, but the actual use of them seems to imply an even older audience.  Not that I don't think a product should push the envelope for kids - it should.  But there do seem to be a limited number of modules in this kit which seems to have an inherent limit as to what you can make with it.

Which leads me to my second criticism.  If this is aimed as a learning tool/product for kids, well, the price point is kind of up there.  This product seems to give a limited number of modules which cannot really be combined in all possible combinations, at a price that makes it risky to purchase for a kid who may exhaust the potential of the kit relatively quickly.  Certainly one can buy other kits, or even other modules ala carte, but those aren't inexpensive either.  I think the price point really does limit the willingness of a parent to take a chance on this.

Reviewing the Little Bits website, I see that Little Bits are also used by some adults to create demonstration prototypes (for, say, a startup company), and that it seems to me is its strongest market niche.  Adults with a strong background in design would certainly find it easy and convenient to have a supply of ready-made snap-together circuits to create something.  I'm just not sure if kids are really going to get lasting value out of Little Bits without a large (and, frankly, expensive) inventory of modules.

Overall I do appreciate the concept and I think the innovation of small pre-built snap-together circuit modules is compelling.  I just wish the price point was set so as to make it accessible to more kids, if indeed kids are the target audience.

reviewText:
The Fisher-Price Little People Animal Friends Farm Toy has always been a wonderful toy that helps foster a childs imagination.  The most current version may be one of the best  because it is far more compact and portable than previous versions, and the silo portion of the barns structure is attached rather than being a separate piece.

The two halves of the barn are hinged together and close securely.  Importantly, it is not difficult for little ones to open the barn when they are ready to play farmer.  When closed, the barn is approximately 8 deep and 13  wide; when fully opened it is approximately 5 deep and 24 wide.  The height of the barn at the silos peak is about 13 .  A handle makes this toy easy for a child to carry when it is closed.  Other pieces included with the Fisher-Price Little People Animal Friends Farm Toy are a hay bale, a farmer, a cow, a goat, a sheep, a horse, a pig and a chicken.

Using a small switch located on the underside of the barn, the sound effects on the Fisher-Price Little People Animal Friends Farm Toy barn can be turned on or off.  To activate the different sounds or songs, a child must open the doors to the stable.

Like all Fisher-Price toys, the Fisher-Price Little People Animal Friends Farm Toy is nicely finished and sturdy.  The hard plastic barn has no rough edges.  It should be durable.  The figures included with the barn are a stiff, but not hard plastic.  None has any visible seams or rough edges.

The previous version of the Fisher-Price Little People Animal Friends Farm Toy was one of my grandsons favorite toys; he played with it until he was almost four.  I am sure his little sister will enjoy the new Fisher-Price Little People Animal Friends Farm Toy when she visits Grandma.  This is an excellent choice as a toy for your little one.  It fosters imagination and creativity in your child; it is one that will provide many hours of fun.

reviewText:
Ah, the Blitz. My second favorite (Buster gets the top spot, I had a gripe with Blitz's armaments being mostly disposable in nature) of the original SEED "Fab Five" gets the second release slot. And let me say that Bandai engineering has done a wonder on it, as many custom Gunpla builders may agree. Keeps the stock SEED RM frame runners so building this is pretty straightforward and like the other five, but the True fun part is the Trikeros Shield System. I also took quite a fancy to the slider mechanism in the shoulders for the Mirage Colloid dispensers, and the Gleipner Anchor was a very interesting piece. I was disappointed in the range of motion in the verniers, and like the others it has problems keeping its skirt armor in place, as well as the ankle guards occasionally sliding into the way of the joint and blocking movement, but nothing that can cost it a star.

In all, a faithful build that will look fantastic with the others, and should you be considering a base kit for a custom project, this one is a great pick.

Final Verdict - As long a you have space to store it the Radio Flyer Triple Play is the ideal wagon. It offers storage for parent and child alike - my only wish... that I wish it had come out sooner! 5 Stars

The T.S. Shure Wooden Magnets Alphabet Letter set is fantastic. I have a metal sheet on the wall of my game room and these are perfect for sitting on the floor with the grandkids learning letters and even to a small degree, spelling words. It works well even for an 18 month old (with supervision) as he can pick up the items and arrange them on the wall - the magnets hold very well.

The Letters are made of wood and each piece has a picture on it that begins with that letter.  For instance, Q has a quail, R has a rooster, and Z has a zebra.  If you are willing to invest in a couple of sets as I am, you can use the magnetic letters to form simple words.  With a single set, you can form words provided there are no letter duplications.

I have a few of the T.S. Shure products and am very impressed by their quality and attention to detail.

I got the Barbie Digital Makeover Mirror for my 9 year old daughter because she really wants to wear makeup but we think she's still too young. We thought this might be a way she could experiment with makeup without putting on real makeup.

Putting the mirror together was a snap, literally. The two pieces snap together very easily, and it's  a pretty sturdy stand for your iPad. The software downloaded quickly and the Bluetooth paired with the iPad easily. Then my daughter went through the "setup" on the app, and I don't know if she was just impatient and skipped over it really quickly or if the app was just buggy, but it took us a good 30 minutes to get it working from that point. It was starting to get really frustrating, but we finally started over, went through the whole setup, and everything seemed to work okay.

I will say, since this relies on the camera on the iPad, and we had an iPad 2 with a not-so-great front camera, we had to be in an area with pretty good amount of light for it to recognize her face. The little lights on around the iPad provide hardly any real light to light your face.

Once she got it working, she had a lot of fun playing with it. You can save photos to the iPad with your makeup, so you can share them with your friends, etc. Overall she really enjoyed playing with the mirror. I think this would be great for girls aged 5-8, my daughter (9) likes it, but probably not as much as younger girls would.

reviewText: All in all, you get everything you need to start a humble pot garden.  This set comes with the 3 pots, the pot holder, some soil and organic seeds, and a little trowel.  The directions are easy to follow to get this started, and the seeds they provide are fast sprouters.  We saw little plants (the basil) shoot up in just 2 or 3 days.  My daughters were so excited to check their plants everyday and water them.  We've been growing the plants for over a month now and the basil is doing great, the sunflowers are growing, and the zinnias are moving slow, but getting there.  If I had one complaint, and this is as a gardener, I worry about how well the plants will continue to grow as the pots have no hole(s) at the bottom for water drainage.  But so far, so good.  The plants have had little care (water once a day and set in the sun) and are still thriving.  This set makes my kids excited about growing plants and makes them more aware of their world.

reviewText:
Overall this is a good toy. My only concern is that my kids don't play with it for long at a time, but they do come back to it. I got this for my 1 year old to start walking with and my 3.5 year old keeps playing with it too. My 1 year old is just starting to walk and a little unsteady so she likes to hold on to anything near by. I figured this would be good for her, she could push it around and be a little more stable. That works great! She loves walking around with it, but gets bored quickly and moves on to something else. Let's look closer:

Pros:
*Versatility. You can leave the  back wheels off completely and lay it on the ground, or connect them as a walker or a ride on. Once that is done you can lock the back wheels to keep them still or unlock to allow it to roll around. I have used it all of these ways and found uses in each case.
*Easy to switch. FINALLY!!!! A toy that goes from one mode to another without making you scream! There are two large plastic screws in the back of the legs that easily unscrew to move them together or apart depending on which mode you want.
*Off switch. A TRUE off switch, not one of those "auto off" things that still makes noise if you sneeze too hard. It goes completely off if you want it to.
*Volume control. Soft is very soft and I can completely tune it out, and loud is loud enough to not ignore but not too loud to be annoying over time.
*Amount of things to do. There are a bunch of buttons to press, things to turn, etc. Everything triggers noises or lights or both so there is instant feedback for your child. The wheel and horn are a favorite in this house and it makes the music start so they love it.

Cons:
*Screws. OK, so it does easily go from one mode to another, but there are other screws in the initial assembly that are simply terrible! They are such a soft metal that they start to strip out as you are putting it together. I have assembled TONS of products over the years and am that person friends call over to do stuff like that for them. I know how to pick the right screwdriver for the job, and that didn't help. The amount of force needed for that handle on the top almost ensures the screws will strip out on you. I even tried one with the power tools on the lowest setting and same issue.
*Weight limit. There is a weight limit for the kids to ride on it. My 3.5 year old is just over it so I am constantly telling her to get off it. I can see it start to sag a little big when she is on it. I don't think it would break, but I am not willing to take the risk anyway.
*Bored quickly. While both of my kids keep coming back this thing, hence the 4 stars, they are also just as quickly leaving it alone. I wish it had more of a interactive game mode to keep them over there playing with it.

I would recommend it as there are plenty of pros and my kids do keep playing with it, but keep in mind that they probably won't play with it long and there is a weight limit so the toy will become obsolete after a time. I am not sure why, but my 1 year old keeps trying to crawl under the thing and then gets stuck. I wonder if anybody else has kids that do that? I wonder why? Anyway, It's the quality you would expect from VTech and pretty easy to assemble even with the bad screws. It doesn't take up that much space in the house, so it's worth a try in my opinion.
summary: Versatile, fun, but can get bored quickly.

reviewText:
I like this gadget enough that I've now given it as a baby shower gift more than once -- and had people return the competing product that had been on their registry once they realize how much better this one is. Here's why:

1) If the baby stops breathing, the Oma+ vibrates to startle the baby into breathing again. For the kinds of apnea events young infants have, this is often enough. The alarm then only goes off if the baby still isn't breathing a few seconds after the vibration. This feature is awesome for two reasons -- it means the baby is likely to start breathing again more quickly, and it means fewer alarms in the night with panicked parents racing to check in on a baby who has resumed breathing again after being startled by the alarm.

2) Because the Oma+ is clipped onto the baby's diaper, it works no matter where in the house the baby is sleeping. With the devices with sensors that go under the crib mattress, not only do they only work when the baby is sleeping in the crib, but they can cause the alarm to go off if the baby rolls to one side of the crib or even if you pick the baby off without resting the alarm first.

3) It's a lot more portable and easy to use on the go -- very little setup needed at all.

So all in all, it's easier to use and with fewer False alarms. Win win!
summary: So much better than most of the competitor products on the market

Love the minifigures, can't fathom the thinking behind the design of the set. You've got two exterior walls with a few EXCEEDINGLY MINOR play features (a collapse, and a tree that falls over), a paltry piece count in the mid 400s, and 5 (very desirable, but merely five nonetheless) minifigs, all for the astoundingly inflated price of $60. In fact, this may be the worse piece-to-dollar ratio of any midsize product Lego has issued -- certainly, it's close to it.

I'll probably still buy it for the figures (you're averaging about $12 a fig, which is pretty close to Ebay for them), but on the whole its just a waste of money. Hugely disappointed at Lego for this dog of a set.

reviewText:
Purchased this breadboard as a hobbyist expanding my knowledge in electronics.

The board itself is nicely sized (large), and allows for pretty decent sized circuits to be constructed.  Basically, it is 4 standard breadboards side by side, with an additional bus strip run horizontally on the top, all connected to a solid backing.  4 binding posts allow for additional external components to be connected.  It looks like it should last quite a while if treated well.

The jumper wires are of a very wide length of sizes, and allow for easy color coding when working in complex circuit prototyping.  The box the come in (clear instead of the blue shown) allowed for easy organizing of the different sizes.

Overall, it's a pretty good combo, and reasonably priced for the size of board you get.  Other than that, it's not too complicated of an item, so there's not really much else to say.  2 Thumbs up!

I confess that for the moment I only own three of these figures, so in case another one turns out to be better, I'll update this review.  For now, though, I'm more than convinced that this one is, indeed, the best figure in these series.

As everyone here says, of course, ignore the first picture here.  I don't know why Amazon keeps that picture around.  Not only the second picture is far more accurate to the looks of the actual figure, but the first one is detrimental to the sales for people who only look at the article on a list without actually clicking on the link.

In any case, if you're reading this, you're not one of those people, and you're most likely already convinced, but let me praise this figure anyway: it's amazing.  The likeness to Cesar Romero is so great you'd swear someone actually made a tiny homunculus clone of Cesar and covered it in some plastic product like in that House of Wax movie.

The articulation is great.  Joker has at least better articulation than Batman and Catwoman from this series, and he can totally do the splits.  JCVD would be proud.  Like all the other figures, it comes with a base and a collectible card (get all the cards together in order to form a picture of the Batcave!).  Otherwise, no accessories.  A shame, but it doesn't take of the awesomeness of this figure.

Now I just hope there's a series two of these figures.  There are too many characters from the TV series I'd love to own.

reviewText: Generations Starscream one of the best ever! I do own most deluxe class Starscream transformers done and I can honestly say this is another great Strascream that would be at the top of the list for all transformer fans to get. I will admit in cybertyronian jet fighter mode I think it would look better with a body section piece between the cockpit and back section,but I also understand with the way the jet fighter mode is gives it more of the cybertronian look as well which is still very cool. Starscream comes with spinning assault cannons which can combine for one large weapon or seperate for individual cannons. The assault cannons attach securely in the hands in robot mode and underneath each wing in cybertronian jet fighter mode. The Decepticon air warrior has awesome detail and articulation throughout both modes with all joints being constructed very well. The poseability is outstanding with great stability for creating cool battle scenes or displaying where you please. The durability is excellent as well with quality ball-joint construction and a solid build in either robot or jet fighter mode. The transformation level is intermediate meaning if you have plenty of experience with transformers there is mid-level difficulty. If you are a parent buying for a child of 5-6 they might need some assistance in the transformation process. All parts fit together very securely during the transformation process for a solid transformer all around. To start off rotate the wings forward as you rotate the forearm's around so the fingers are to the back. Next the feet rotate in as the red pieces of shoulder armor beside the head piece rotate up. Now the arms along with the back piece rotate back then forward as the head piece is rotated around. The head piece rotates down as the back section piece now rotates back out forming a v-shape. Next the back section piece rotates straight up to be aligned behind the cockpit section. Make sure the red armor pieces are above the grey pieces in the middle or the legs won't be able to connect right underneath. The forearm's then rotate around once more as the hands rotate down against the arm piece. Now the entire arm pieces will rotate underneath in place between the wings. On the next part the legs will rotate back underneath the wings and connect securely to the pegs underneath the tail section. The nosecone now rotates out from underneath and Starscream is ready for flight! This is one of the better Starscream deluxe class transformers around and is one of the elite figures in the Fall of Cybertron Generations line. Bottom line Fall of Cybertron Generations Deluxe Starscream is a well-made,high quality,10 out of 10 transformer all fans and collectors wiil enjoy. I highly recommend Generations Deluxe Class Starscream to all transformer fans and collectors out there. Starscream Rocks and Transformers Rule!!!

reviewText:
This game is fun and not too hard to play, though as others have said the rulebook is long, a little intimidating, and can take awhile to get through the first time.  I have played Munchkin, but never Castle Panic.  This game is cooperative in that the players are working toward a common goal.  At the same time, however, the players are looking out for themselves, a dichotomy that can cause difficulty in winning the game.

The players' castle is at the center of the board and must be defended from the monsters which attack from 6 different areas around the castle. The monsters move closer each turn while the players attempt to kill the monsters using their cards.  Of course, the cooperative goal is to defend the castle and defeat the monsters while the  players' individual goal is to get the most points from defeating monsters.  You have to balance the team goal with the individual effort and cooperate enough to win.

I like that you can play this solo.  In fact, it may be more enjoyable and easier to win playing solo.  My 9 year old daughter enjoyed this game.  My 5 year old son liked it and wanted to play, but could not on his own.  He liked playing alongside one of his parents.  Overall, this game is fun and worth playing.

reviewText:
I am torn in reviewing this toy.  Here's why:  The toy is definitely well-made, will not come apart, will not break unless subjected to massive violence.  It definitely builds motor skills, hand-eye-coordination, and even thinking skills--as deciding which colors should be up or down or evenly matched in height requires some intricate choice and physical application.  So, the toy is a great toy!

But . . .

You are basically giving your child a miniature of Thor's hammer.  Not a hollow plastic hammer, mind you.  No, no.  This is a toddler weapon the great god of thunder would approve of.  Two solid wooden pieces held together very well.  The head of the hammer is sculpted to allow attacks from many interesting angles.  Great for the toy.  Not so great if your little one might decide to go "a-viking" during a playgroup, family get-together, or school function.

Like the mighty Mjolner, this hammer throws well, flies fast and far, and can kill the mightiest of trolls.  Or televisions.  Or PC's.  Or Grandma.

So . . . the only reason I take a star off is because of the deadly weapon that comes with this awesome toy.  Maybe it should have been fastened by a cable to the toy, Melissa & Doug?  It's not cool that parents have to do this thinking for you.  But we love Grandma.  Having our toddler turned Thor send her to the hospital is not our idea of fun.

If your child is meek and kind and dependably non-violent, go for it.  GREAT TOY!  If your little one may just be a conqueror of lands reincarnated into this tiny body, please beware the hammer!

reviewText:
I am the parent of 2 preschool aged children, and they both love interactive toys. So of course, we were very excited about Cody the Smart Cub! He is absolutely adorable and snuggly, with a plush body and a bright, cheerful appearance. He has several interactive features that teach things like counting, colors, singing songs, and so much more.

Cody tells lots of fun stories, and even encourages kids to "play" with him by asking them to complete tasks like "Find my tummy" or "Give me a high 5". When a child successfully completes these tasks, they receive tons of cheers and applause. This is a wonderful confidence builder for little ones!

What we really love the most is the fact that Cody can be personalized by plugging the included USB into a computer or tablet. When you visit VTech's Learning Lounge, you can add more stories, music, and activities to Cody's extensive capabilities, and you can even personalize this toy for your child. We added our son's name, his favorite colors and snacks, as well as tons of his favorite music and stories. This makes play time so much more personal, and little ones love hearing their names being said by their plush pal.

I also love the fact that the time and date can be programmed into the toy. This means a child will get appropriate greetings, like "Good morning", "Good afternoon" and "Goodnight". A child can also receive birthday wishes and Holiday wishes on the appropriate days.

The only downside? The USB cable is a bit short, which makes downloading additional materials a little more challenging. It's still simple to achieve, but I would have preferred a few more inches of wiggle room.

Overall, I would definitely recommend Cody the Smart Cub. He is absolutely adorable, and definitely keeps young children engaged while they learn and play!

I will avoid explaining all the details of this game as other reviewers have done that.  I will explain what I found fun about the game as opposed to classic risk.

I played this game with my friend and his 12 year old son.  We all learned together.  It isn't like classic risk where you develop long term plans.  You have until the Clara lands on the 11th Doctor to dominate as much of the board as you can.  Clara went from the first doctor to the second doctor as soon as the first player started his turn.  After two rounds, Clara almost every time.  She was on the 8th Doctor in no time.  We figured she would hit the 11th doctor quickly so we all made a mad dash to unleash bonus troops & powers so we could maximize our chances of winning before it was too late.  Well, then we hit a crazy lull where Clara cards didn't appear for quite some time.  By this time the 12 year old player had gained South America and my friend I were scattered with little chance of establishing ground within a few turns.

I look forward to playing this again.  I think I can do better now that the game will last longer than it initially seemed like it would.  More players in the game would also be more fun for opportunities to EXTERMINATE rivals and take bonus troop cards or mission cards.

reviewText:
Grandma gave this board game to my kiddos because she's aware of their Paw Patrol obsession.  While the game is OK, it seems to be missing something...especially in the clarity of the directions.

It comes with cardboard game pieces, one of each of the 6 main pups.  There are several cardboard badges for each pup.  There's also a cardboard spinner, as well as the game board.

The premise is simple enough, though I do agree the directions aren't the most clear.  You spin the arrow and move to the corresponding color.  You collect the pup badge for whatever color you landed on (once you have a red, you don't get another one next time you're on red).  If you pass over a ladder shortcut, you take the shortcut if you've already collected that pup's badge.  If you haven't, no shortcut.  The one exception is your pup's ladder (your playing piece).  You take his or her ladder whether you've collected the badge or not. Whoever gets to the end first wins.

This game is basically Candy Land mixed with Chutes and Ladders, but shorter and with Paw Patrol characters.  It's cute, and if your kiddo is super into Paw Patrol, it might be a good purchase.  Otherwise I'd say you can skip it and just go with Candy Land!

My 11 year old was super excited to pick out and purchase this using his Amazon gift card. He assembled it himself in about 3-4 hours. I let him complete the assembly independently and he didn't ask for assistance at all although he probably should have as he ended up using random screws in various areas of the assembly. He did mention that many of the screws look alike and it was difficult to tell the difference between the screws.

He meticulously laid out all of the parts and screws and gathered up the tools he would need before beginning to build. He watched several YouTube videos to both inform his purchase and learn more about the robotic arm and general information about building.

He successfully built the arm although part of the base of the arm is a tad loose (I attributed this to using screws that were too short). Since there is a cover plate that holds the entire base together, the overall function of the arm isn't hindered by this.

My son has had a good time trying to lift things with the arm although it doesnt lift mass amounts of weight. As a parent, I was most impressed at his ability to stick with this project through to the end (even with the oversight with the screws). Hes proud of his finished product and has not only a display piece, but something functional that he built himself to show for his efforts.

I would recommend this item for anyone interested in robotics. Its a good entry level project, as all of the steps are laid out for you to follow. Just make sure you sort out the screws before you start building :)

Pros:  this house is really a cute house. Most of the windows open - either outwards or they slide up. The little balcony and front porch are perfect for some outdoor critter fun!  The spiral staircase is a nice touch. The opening in the side of the house provides access for the rooms in the front of the house.
Cons:  The rooms are pretty small. Neither the master bathroom nor cozy kitchen sets fit in one room in the house.  The furniture has to be split up, which works ok for my 4 year old. The rugs that come with each set have to be folded to fit right.
Overall, I am pleased with the purchase and would make the decision to purchase again. The house is quaint and has provided hours of fun and play for our daughter. The house seems to be sturdy and not flimsy like some of the other reviewers have mentioned. If you could purchase for less than $100, I would change my review to 5 stars.  We have four furniture sets and room for two or three more.
Note:  This house is significantly smaller than a loving family dollhouse. The rooms in that house would be much too large and furniture too chunky for the critter families.
summary: Detailed and Quaint...perfect starter Critter house!

reviewText:
OVERVIEW: "The Royal Road to Card Magic" by Jean Hugard and Frederick Braue is a classic text book that continues to be recommended by many as the place to begin a serious journey into card magic, as an ideal course for learning all the fundamentals of card magic. But it can be difficult to learn something from printed text alone, and it can really be of benefit to see a trick being performed and taught on video, and that's where these DVDs come in.

WHAT YOU GET: This product is a set of four DVDs that was first published in 2005. It comes in a single DVD case that houses all four DVDs. With many hours of run time, the videos go through all the chapters of Hugard & Braue's book, with magician Rudy Hunter carefully explaining all the sleights and moves, and the effects that can be performed with them. The video features baroque music with the menus, which heightens the overall feel of the classic magic within.

CONTENTS: The DVD is arranged according to the book, and the main topics covered are as follows:
DVD 1: Overhand Shuffle, Riffle Shuffle, Flourishes, The Glide, The Glimpse
DVD 2: The Key Card, The Palm, The Backslip, OverHand Shuffle 2
DVD 3: False Shuffles & Cuts, Double Lift & Turnover, The Pass, Misc. Flourishes, The Reverses
DVD 4: Hindu Shuffle & Controls, Classic Force, Top & Bottom Changes, Arrangements, Platform Tricks
For convenience, all the material contained on the DVD is listed on the back of the case, which is a very helpful reference and overview.

THE TEACHING: Rudy Hunter doesn't have the dynamic or lively persona of the typical overly-exuberant in-your-face street magician, but he is a professional, and this is a great demonstration of classic close-up card magic that is performed very smoothly and cleanly. For example, he mentions that in his own magic career, he must have performed the Ambitious Card Routine about 250,000 times while doing restaurant and similar work, so he has a wealth of experience. His friendly and personable style works well for teaching, and he does a good job in explaining how things work, and he does have his own sense of humour which helps keep things interesting. Multiple camera angles are used to ensure that it's easy to follow-along. The instruction is concise, and Rudy doesn't waste his words, so a lot is packed in a short amount of time; you can always re-watch sections if you need to, and there's no sense things are dragging.  While books are excellent, being able to see the effect performed is tremendously helpful, and this works very well either in combination with the book, or even independently from it.  Rudy also gives his own take on the sleights that he teaches, and there's a number of personal tips and ideas that he shares based on his own experience with magic, which I found helpful. In short, Rudy is a good teacher who speaks clearly and carefully, and if you're looking for a good teaching resource to use, this is certainly a great place to start.

BONUS DECK: This deluxe edition of the Royal Road video set also comes with a bonus decks of trick playing cards.  This aren't as high quality as typical Bicycle cards printed by USPCC, so there's no real advantage in getting the deluxe version.  In reality this deck is just an added bonus, since it's really the video that makes this a worthwhile buy.

RECOMMENDATION: Many new magicians make the mistake of wanting to progress to difficult tricks or routines, and it is important to lay the foundation by grasping the basic mechanics and fundamentals of card magic, which will hold you in good stead life long. The Royal Road to Card Magic covers all these basic, important and versatile sleights.  As such it provides a more thorough education in the fundamentals of card magic than the crash course videos by Ellusionist, which are more focused on street magic and learning a small selection of tricks.  The Royal Road to Card Magic is geared to complete beginners, and what I like about how it is set up is that it first explains the techniques needed for mastering a sleight, but then goes on to include one or more routines that employ that sleight. Working your way through the Royal Road course will give you a systematic and complete education in card magic, and give you many tricks to work with. Rudy Hunter does an excellent job in this particular version, and his slow and deliberate explanation makes his teaching easy to follow, especially for beginners. This is an excellent learning tool for people starting out in card magic! - BoardGameGeek reviewer EndersGame
summary: Great video companion for Hugard's classic book on the fundamentals of card magic

reviewText: Everything old is new again, with the Electric Inferno by KNex, a USA-based company that specializes in construction toy systems. My son has been an avid consumer of their projects for the past 4 years building, it seems, their entire product line. This model is a huge improvement over older versions (he built several back in 2013 see 1st pic). All the major elements of roller coaster design the lift hill, dive drop, corkscrews, loops and rolls - are stronger and feature less sway while the car(s) are in motion. This is due to a vastly improved structural design that includes better positioning of the supporting pieces. For instance, the Electric Inferno features an integrated support system of the green flexi rods that anchors the tower to the base as well as to the ascending and descending track on either side, a design element not seen in the 2013 model. More crucially, the heavy, battery-operated motor is now located at ground level instead of at the top of the structure. These small changes bring unprecedented stability to the model eliminating the top-heavy sway, chain snags and stuck cars that dogged older versions. Although this model only comes with one car, he was able to add three more (from other kits) without experiencing mechanical failure/malfunction. Design innovation and excitement is built into the KNex brand. One STEAM-based suggestion: a schematic with the roller coaster elements identified and annotated (kinetic motion, acceleration, torque) would position this as an engineering project with fun built into the equation.

reviewText:
This is honestly one of those things that you don't truly appreciate until you have it in hand and it's on your shelf next to the other figures from previous & corresponding lines. The prototype photos like many don't this justice. This queen in particular is from the Aliens: Genocide comic series and she is absolutely mammoth in size, the sculpt and articulated points all make it worth the hundred dollar mark. She's even bigger than McFarlane's first deluxe queen, which still has a special place in my collection. The color and paint application is more of a saturated, fleshy red as opposed to the the more ghoulish translucent blue on the original queen.

There is some assembly required with the six organic spikes protruding from her back, and it comes with two inner mouth extensions; one short and one long. It also comes with a base to support two metal rods (one short & one long, depending on how low or high you have this beast posed) and support hook. This is such a solid action figure, articulated in all the right spots and aesthetically striking to look at when displayed. The thing I love about NECA is they simply know what they're doing with their action figures, especially their aliens. I can't wait for them to bust out an AVP queen in this scale, with the dark black and spiked ridges along the crest and seeing chains dangling off of her after being freed from her incubator would be cool to see. At least, that'd be nice to look forward to in the future.

reviewText:
This gift's arrival was perfectly timed.  As my children and I walked to school the morning before Kanoodle Genius came, my 10 y.o. had mentioned wanting puzzles  not the picture kind  for her upcoming birthday.  She was thrilled to try it out that afternoon!

Kanoodle Genius is rated for users ages 8 to adult.  So far my 8, 10, 12, 14, and 16 year old children have tried it out and  loved it. That is no easy feat for this mix of boys and girls.  They are unique individuals.  Being a mom to seven I truly appreciated how both the instructions and puzzle pieces all fit neatly into the 3.5 x 5 game case.  That makes it so simple to store away in our home and even pack for use on trips.  Educational Insights offers both 2-D and 3-D puzzles in this game.  It is nice to have one game with varying levels of challenge for the user. For my younger children, setting up the 3-D puzzles proved to be a challenge in and of itself.  I have witnessed my children all huddled around this game playing cooperatively without fighting.  That is definitely a bonus in our house.  A few of my children are visual-spatial learners, so I enjoyed watching them challenge their brains while having fun.  I am a frugal shopper and love that this game will hold my children's interest for so many years down the line.  The playing pieces are small, so as always use caution if you have little ones around.

Parents, when your kids aren't around grab this game and try it out.  I bet you will like it.  I did and I don't generally enjoy puzzle games.  Oh, and if your instruction book wears out from all the use, Educational Insights offers a free downloadable set of product instructions on their website.
summary: A fun puzzle game for both kids and adults

reviewText: We bought this shopping cart for our granddaughter's 1st birthday.  I read the reviews and noted the comments about the wheels falling off, but decided to take a chance.  Unfortunately, as soon as I assembled the cart and tried it out, one of the wheels immediately came apart.  Instead of trying some of the "fixes" suggested by other reviewers, I called Little Tikes and explained the problem.  They attributed the problem to imperfect plastic molding and said they would send out a replacement kit (new axels, wheels, washers, caps, etc.) to resolve the problem. The game is simple.  Each child takes turns at sliding swords into the openings on the side of the barrel.  The game is set up for four people to play with each person having a different color of sword. Instead of walking the plank, they came up with their own tasks, such as having to hop around the table on one foot while saying, 'ARGH! I['m a pirate, I'm a pirate!"  It was hilarious to watch them enjoy this toy so much!

The kids had fun playing with the toy after dinner most nights and I'm sure they will enjoy it now that we are home.

reviewText:
I'm a Lego veteran, but somehow I've never run into K'NEX before.  I'm quite impressed.  This is an Amazon exclusive and good fun for Roller Coaster fans as well as people (like me) who just enjoys 3-D puzzles.  You need a bit of space to put it together on.  I used an old library table which placed it at a perfect height.

First, make sure you have all the parts.  If there are any missing you can contact the company for replacements.  There's 500 parts (if you are lucky and have them all).  There's a nice web site with downloadable instructions for the Crossfire Chaos Roller Coaster-- in case you lose the originals-- and instructions for a second Coaster called the Torpedo Twist. There's social features that aimed at parents and kids. There is also help with building available on the site in case you get really stuck. I haven't tried to construct the second one yet.

I really didn't expect that the moderate sized box I received would end up being a 3 foot tall Roller Coaster. The open nature of the structure felt a bit odd because I'm used to building with walls like Legos.  It took me a bit over 3 hours to put it together.  The parts fit together well and the car fits well on the tracks and runs easily.  However, don't fool yourself.  The fun is in the construction not necessarily playing with it afterwards.

Recommended for kids 9 up to at least 59.

reviewText:
Farts.  That's really about all you need to know here, but I will be a bit more long-winded (pun intended) for those that want a better whiff of what this toy is all about...

This is one of those toys that kids might like a lot but parents may find a bit too crude.  Basically its a van with a sink & toilet in the back that when pressed make any number of gross sound effects - flatulence, burps, vomiting, pooping, flushing, flies buzzing (presumably drawn by the aforementioned bodily wastes), etc.  When the van is rolled across the floor, the rear wheels activate sound effects which indicate that this van is fart-powered (oh the never ending fart sounds with this van).  It also has a really loud horn and appears to be carrying a bunch of gassy animals through a busy city.  It comes with one little animal, the "slobby saint bernard", and OF COURSE additional critters can be purchased and collected.

From a practical perspective, the van is very durably made and should withstand whatever punishment a youngster might give it.  The day-glow orange and green on white color scheme is bright and appealing.

Butt it really boils down to this question - how gross do you want go?  If you or your kids love scatalogical humor, this will be an odiferous dream come True.  If you're not prudish but don't think the epitome of fun is bathroom humor, you might be like me with mixed feelings about it.  If you are more of the straight-laced type and want your kids to be discreet about farting in public or just talking about farting in public, avoid this one like a dirty bathroom at the local gas station.  Oh, and did I mention is has a lot of fart noises?

reviewText: This drone is awesome for a beginner or intermediate pilot. It has similar features to a full size drone in that it does have GPS, Return to Home, Follow Me, compass lock etc. Simple, simple, simple to fly. And if you get in trouble you flip a switch and it hovers. If you lose orientation you flip another switch and it comes back to you. Awesome. A few tips. 1. Make SURE you have at least 6 GPS connections. This can take up to 5 minutes after you insert the battery. If you only have four... the return to home feature doesn't work. Trust me on this one. Found it out the hard way this morning as the drone floated away from us. At least we had a spare set of props :-). 2. Follow the instructions every time you change a battery for Compass Lock. 3. Keep spare batteries with you. The transmitter will burn through four AA batteries in about 30 minutes. Use rechargeables and take spares. Bottom line - I highly recommend this for a starter drone. The picture/video quality is amazing for such an inexpensive system. We have flown this in our small driveway, at a park, and at a private flying field and in our living room without GPS. It is that stable. Just to prove how easy it is to fly and how stable I am including a video of my 10 year old flying it. This was only the third time she had it in the air so good for kids or adults. I will cut down a video of the drone video and post it when I can. Pros: Easy to fly, great video, good features comparable to drones that are a lot more expensive Cons: No rechargeable LIPO option for transmitter. Short flight time (batteries last about 5 minutes based on what I am seeing). Getting the blades turned on and off is a real pain. You have to move the sticks to the bottom corners then "mess with them" to get it to kick in. Would be a lot easier with a switch or something. Sometimes you simply cant get it to turn off so you end up having to move your hand under the drone with the blades spinning, pick it up, and disconnect the battery. Not very safe. But the blades don't hurt if they hit you.

My 11 year old has Autism and in the past he did not like playing the Find It Games that we had. He did not like them to the degree that I passed them on to friends for the their children. It has been several years since we tried to play one so I decided to see if he might like them now. I am very glad that I did!  He loves it!!!

We have both had a lot of fun with this game. There are many different ways that you can play this Find It Game. You could even make up your own questions or rules. One thing that I like about this set as compared to the others is that some of the questions cause those playing to think as they go. An example is, "Find something larger than .....". This question allows the person playing to decide what the other person needs to look for. This is perfect for my child that is on the spectrum. I think that this is one of the things that pulled him into the game. He likes that he can choose what others need to look for.  :)

I would highly recommend this for everyone!  Of course it is great for kids. But I also think it would be good for elderly people.

I purchased this at a discount in exchange for an honest review of the product. I am selective in what I review, and I will always give an honest opinion.

There are two ways to play this game; 2D and 3D.  The 3D is more fun and challenging.

My 5 year old son can do the more basic 3D pyramids. He has mild case of autism and he can concentrate on things when he likes a particular activity.  He play with it for hours and even slept with it under the pillow the first day we got it. There are more difficult puzzles for grown-ups.  It is not impossibly hard but has a quite entertainment value.

Not for the very little ones as the smaller pieces can be chokers.  And don't lose the booklet.

I love it and I do recommend it for those who love thinking games.

My son has spent countless hours playing with his wooden railway. He can design his own track and pick the pieces he wants to add and remove to play with. He carries on a monologue between the trains and their activities. There is no comparison between the wooden railways and the Tarckmaster sets.
Again, this is a very nice Trackmaster set, especially if your child likes to watch their trains go around a track, but I would rather spend my money on something that allows my child to interact and have some imaginative play.

reviewText: I am the type of person that enjoys family bonding time during the holidays, especially when we don't see some of our family on a regular basis. I also love to laugh and play a whole family involved game when we get together. Balderdash and many of these types of games just make me belly laugh and nothing makes me happier than to fill our home with laughter and family memories. We hosted Thanksgiving at our home this year and I was looking for a game that everybody could play, including the men (who sometimes try to get out of playing the family games). I came across this Thanksgiving themed box of questions and thought that this would be a fun way involve the whole family and keep the spirit of Thanksgiving alive with the themed questions. There are 82 question cards and it says for age 6 and up. While this is not a game that will make you belly laugh (it may at times), many of the questions are more thought provoking about Thanksgiving. Some question examples are: Thank someone at the table for something that will surprise them, Do you sleep in after the big feast or get up early to shop the sales on Black Friday, What are male turkeys called, What are female turkeys called, Have you ever worked in a soup kitchen or served others on Thanksgiving, What is your family motto, etc... These cards are round and have a picture of a pumpkin pie on the back of each one. The box is sturdy and has a Thanksgiving themed motif on the outside. I really enjoyed this game and will bring it along next year to the festivities. It is inexpensive and is a nice themed game for family bonding. Melissa & Doug also makes several other games like this one that are themed for other holidays or different types of get togethers. This is a nice conversation piece to place on the table and I would recommend this game to anyone that is looking for something to involve the whole family on Thanksgiving. I had a little craft set up for the little ones that they were able to do while we were playing this. You don't need to sit around a game board to do this, so it is very functional and you can quit at any time.

reviewText:
This is a nicely put together crystal crowing kit, far superior to the Ravensburger kit I reviewed a few months back.  First, you do need to remember that crystal growing is more or less like watching metaphorical paint dry.  You mix the solution and then hurry up and wait.  In other words, it is well suited for kids with longer attention spans.  Make sure this isn't your only activity for the day!  Second, note that while the kit includes much of what you need (pipette, chemicals, beakers, chemicals), you will also need jars to actually grow the crystals.  These are not included!  So if you are gifting this, you might want to pick up some canning jars to gift along with it, or the parents of the gift receiver will be scrambling to empty out jelly jars.  If I gave this as a gift, I would certainly also gift a bunch of empty glass jars to make life easier on the parents of the gift receiver.

The actually kit is laid out nicely, and the chemicals and plaster are all in nicely sealed bags.  My other crystal kit from Ravensburger was full of plaster dust, so I am glad that Thames and Kosmos saw fit to properly seal all of the bags in the kit.  The colorful manual explains the science and the safety behind experimenting and walks kids through what they can do on their own and what requires parental involvement.  The crystals are beautiful and certainly a fun reward for the experiments.  It's a nice kit and recommended.

reviewText:
Scrabble Twist is a fun pass 'n' play electronic game that is great for 2-4 players.

Scrabble Twist has hard plastic wand design that fits comfortably in an adult's hands, but is simple enough to also be handled by a 7 year old.  The device takes 3 AA batteries, but you have to use a screwdriver to take the battery panel off.  There is no on/off switch, the device automatically goes to sleep if nothing is pressed for 30 seconds.  The wand itself is rather simple. There are five circular buttons on the face that have blue LED backlighting.  One red cap houses a speaker, and the other red cap can be twisted about 45 degrees in either direction.

To turn it the device, just twist the red cap.  A menu is illuminated on the five blue circles.  You use the twisting motion to cycle through the options, and hit any blue circle to select the displayed option.  If you flip the wand it recognizes the orientation and automatically turns the letters right-side-up. There are three games to choose from:

SOLO:  5 random letters appear in the blue circles.  You must press the circles in order to spell 3 to 5 letter words, and then twist the cap to lock in your word.  If its a valid word, you get a friendly chime.  If its not a real word in the Scrabble dictionary, you get a bad noise and an X briefly pops up in each circle.  There is a third pop noise if you repeat a word.  You score 3 points for a 3-letter word, 5 for a 4-letter word, and 7 for a 5-letter word.  The game can be set for 45, or 60, or 75 seconds.  Once your time is up, your score is displayed on the blue circles.

TURBO:  Same as solo, except after your turn is up, your score is displayed and you pass the wand to the next player.  Each player gets the same 5 letters to work with. Once everyone is done, the wand tells you that P3, or whoever, was the winner.  You can set the wand for 2-8 players.

PARTY:  This is also for 2-8 players.  The same 5 letters are used throughout the game.  P1 starts and has to create a single 3 to 5 letter word and has 15 seconds to do so.  That person calls out the word as they twist to lock it in.  The wand is passed to the next player, who must create a valid word and pass the wand on.  If a player cannot form a new valid word within the time limit, they are knocked out.  The game ends when one member is left.

In the master menu settings, you can adjust the games from Easy to Medium to Hard.  The changes basically alter the amount of time you get for each game.  The default setting of Medium grants each player 60 seconds in SOLO or TURBO time.  Its probably the best balanced time allotment for most players.

Overall, the game is a lot of fun for people of all ages.  I just have a few small complaints.  First, there is no option to save your high scores in SOLO mode in order to compete with yourself over time.  My second complaint is that the volume levels are difficult to control.  There are 4 volume settings buried in the main menu: Low, Med, High, Mute.  Playing the game on mute is a major challenge because the only way you know you are running out of time is to listen to the ticking noise that continuously speeds up for the last 15 seconds of a round.  If you set the volume to Low, its still pretty loud for quieter environments.  I brought it to the office one day to show my co-workers and we couldn't play a game because even on the low setting it was loud and distracting to nearby workers.  I would have liked to have seen an extra low volume setting for this purpose.  Also, I appreciate the smooth, clean design that does not include switches or buttons beyond the 5 circle letter buttons, but I would have liked to have seen a physical volume dial on the device.  If you have a game going and the phone rings, the game has to just cycle all the way to the end with the loud ticking clock noise before it can shut off.  This can produce 30 loud, embarrassing seconds you have to deal with.  Finally, hitting the blue circle buttons isn't that bad, but it does take some physical pressure to get your inputs to register.  For an adult its not really a problem, but for an 8 year old with small hands, it can become a frustrating limitation preventing them from achieving a very high score.

Even with those complaints, though, Im only knocking Scrabble Twist down one star.  Its a fun, inexpensive game that is great for parties when people have short attention spans.  When you are playing with 2-4 people, they only have to wait 60 seconds per person before they get a shot and everyone stays involved.  If you play with 8 people, the last person has to wait 8-10 minutes and may wander off before their turn comes around.  If you keep that in mind, though, I think youll be happy with your Scrabble Twist purchase.

reviewText:
I bought mine at a local comic book shop. This is a great figure of the Iron Man 3 Mark 2 War Machine armor. Though this suit doesn't actually appear in the movie, the armor was still used but painted in the Iron Patriot colors.

For accessories it comes with a Hall of Armor display base, which can also be used for the Marvel Legends figures if you want. We also get an alternate mask-less head with Don Cheadle's face. Unfortunately it doesn't come with an extra pair of hands, but it does comes with an articulated shoulder cannon which can be plugged behind the right shoulder.

Articulation: ball-hinge head, shoulders, and hips; rotation at upper biceps, forearms, wrists, upper thighs, and ankles; ball-jointed torso; single-hinge elbows and ankles; double-jointed knees; and ankles also roll side-to-side. The shoulder pads also hinge up and down. These allow you to get many nice poses with the figure. The rolling action of the ankles definitely help the pose-ability too.

The only complaint I have is that it has really loose hip joints. I like the articulation on them though, but's it's very loose. So loose that it can be hard to stand. In fact one of the shoulder pads broke off on mine because it fell off a dresser. I had to super glue it back on. I hear others saying this too, so I don't think it's just mine, although it might not be the case for everyone. You just have to be careful to center it right so the weight is balanced.

Overall it's a great figure in my opinion. Looks great next to the Mark 42 from Marvel Select. If you're an Iron Man and War Machine fan, I would recommend this.

This product is the cheapest one with its theme, and also has way more features compared with another product that costs $30 more. With that in mind, I ordered this Digger scooter.

Below the mirror there is a panel of instrument-shaped buttons to press.  I wrongly assumed that the panel has several activities, or at least that each button would cause a different effect when pressed.  Turns out that regardless of which button the baby presses, the next song or sound plays.  Except for two little pop up babies,it has no interesting activities to keep baby occupied.

My daughters face lights up when I sit her in front of this toy, but within a few minutes, she's tired of it.  Besides for the toy being boring, the brightly flashing lights and obnoxious music are annoying (even for babies I think!). Come on Fisher Price, it's the 21st century.  There are great kids songs out there.  The least they could have done is added a few more songs, so they don't repeat as often.

This toy is the perfect height for a sitting baby, and there aren't too many of those.  It's a pity Fisher Price didn't put more thought into the design.  I don't expect too much from a toy.  If it keeps my daughter entertained for 15 minutes I consider it a success.  Unfortunately this toy failed.

Apple comes in an extravagant dress, and easily gets my vote for best dressed. Raven and Cupid both had pretty outfits, but Apple White takes the cake and then some. It's not as bright as the stock picture shows, yet is still stunning, mass produced or not. She has several layers on the lower section of her dress, with transparent white and gold patterns on the first, then a champagne layer with black and gold patterns, then a transparent section with gold flakes, and finally red on the bottom. If there were any complaints about the price of these dolls, trust me when I say that this is one where the price is justified. The rest of her outfit is equally beautiful, with pearl gloves, red bows at the elbows and a corsage on the left wrist. Apple has a large red necklace with small bows and other designs carved into it, and she has a plain white and gold sparkle top with white fur around the shoulders, and a golden belt with pearls that go around the hips. Finally, her shoes are black and red with large bows, and she sports large golden earrings, though I can't quite make out the design.

The standard Ever After/Monster High articulation is here. Her head, shoulders, elbows, wrists, upper legs and knees. Accessory-wise, she comes with the usual Ever After High stuff: stand, purse and mask. As with the other dolls my daughter has, the mask can fit in her hand just fine, but it can't be held up next to her face. It's no big deal, although they should have done something to fix this. The best you're going to get is having it displayed as shown in the stock image above.

This doll is an absolute home run, and if this is one of the early dolls, I can't imagine how they improve later on with different variations of the character, or any of the others for that matter.

reviewText:
It's a full featured play kitchen that makes good use of the space it occupies and has proven engaging for my daughter to play with. From washing her plush dolls in the washing machine to general cooking and baking cookies. That's the good part.

Assembly takes a long time and will test your patience for peeping at too small pictures and tolerance for defects along the way. Some of the assembly pictures were incorrect and I found it helpful to download the PDF from the manufacturer's website so I could zoom in on certain assembly steps.

The box was delivered by UPS intact but the styrofoam was broken all over the place inside, carry on we thought and found more scuffs and scratches the minute we unpacked the box; most of them were on back edges or sides that would be inside facing so we decided to continue with assembly. But the main counter piece literally had a glob of color matched "glue" on the outer edge to fill a defect, it was sticky and off color once you take a closer look at it.

By this point, we're already 70% done so one must decide to accept and continue, call kidkraft to get replacements and leave a 70% finished kitchen just hanging around, or breakdown pack up and return the whole thing. Not a decision you want to make 2 hours into assembly at 10 PM at night. Up our tolerance for defects it went; repeating our mantra that kids will beat the thing up eventually anyways.

Another hour or so later and we were done! Two days later, an inside piece of the oven knob or range snaps off when my 4 year old was playing with it. Luckily, nothing fell out of place and it doesn't seem to affect the set but one must wonder and question how well this will last over the years of repeated play.

In summary; good design and play features but assembly could have been better thought out, packaging was deficient for parcel delivery, sloppy QA on pieces, and overall questionable material quality.
summary: Full featured but shoddy QA control, cheap materials, and scuffs in transit

reviewText:
We got four of these - Monster Opto, Monster Mindstein, Monster Gump, and Give Him A Squeeze. One for each grandchild. The balls were different colors for each Monster, (and Mindstein's look like brains!), so the kids could play together but keep track of whose balls were whose.

We played target games, (get it in the basket and stuff like that), rather than shooting at each other. But, there's no harm if someone is hit because the balls are soft, (harder than Nerf and softer than ping pong), and don't have much force behind them.

The balls really do fly up to 20 feet and it's even possible to aim them pretty well, so target games aren't frustrating.

At first we were really disappointed because two of the monsters didn't work. If you squeezed it the ball just sort of fell out. Well, there's a trick here. The balls have a little bit of a rim around the "equator". You have to push the ball into the monster until you feel a slight positive "snap". If you don't push the ball in all of the way it won't POP out, it will just roll out. Once we figured that out and once the balls got broken in a little bit, all of the Monsters worked fine.

For what it's worth, our players were four, six, six and nine years old. None of them had any trouble inserting the balls or getting the balls to POP out. A gentle firm squeeze was all they needed.

We're usually reluctant to buy novelty stuff on spec, but the bottom line is that these were a great success and have kept up their play value. A nice find.

The jaw is still hinged, but it will not stay open. It feels almost like there is a spring that makes it immediately shut. It's really a shame because it just makes it look less realistic and cheapens the appearance. Overall this is still a unique and cool prop, I just wish it was made with the same production values as last year.
