reviewText:
So I was having trouble deciding between this one and the green, less of a whipped tail version by this same company as an upcoming surprise for a long week away from home for my kiddo who's recently fallen in love with The Land Before Time. All we have are my old JP dinos from when I was a kid from the original movie, but they regrettably never made a "long neck" :-). My toddler seemed to prefer this one over the green one from Safari, and so we chose this guy based on reviews saying it was sturdy, and not too big (this needs to fit in a carry on), etc.

I've included some photos - one thing I was surprised about was the uh, elimination hole of some sort? I guess? I don't know, I included a photo. The lighting was kinda crappy, but it looks like it was done very intentionally with how precise it is and the paint job. Not sure if that's just ours or what, but I didn't see that on any reviews and made me laugh a bit. I can see how others might find it off putting though.

This is my first purchase from this company and i bought another dino from a competing company which tends to be more expensive but gets very high reviews (carnivore in the photos is from that company) and I included the carnivore in photos for size/quality comparison, and I'd say quality wise they are quite similar, surprisingly.

This model is solid hard rubber material with wrinkles, not just detail painted on. The whip tail seems like it will take some rough play before snapping (if ever). I mean you'd have to really twist and bend to break this guy. His neck has all those extra folds, but is still round - I felt like other photos made it seem like the neck was more flat and less round, but not so. Like others have said, the paint job is detailed and nice and for the price point of about $10, you can't beat it. I personally find the green one by this company more attractive and desirable as it seems to be larger than this one, but this guy is a great addition to our collection. He's more of a medium size dino than a large one though. I definitely recommend him!

There are three items* SOMEONE should warn parents about before they buy them. This is one of them. I only wish someone had told ME years ago...

Yes, this game is cute and easy to play. Yes, it's famous. And yes, it's probably educational.

But be warned - it is THE most boring game in the universe. After ten minutes you will find yourself in a stupor. You'll look at the board and begin trying to calculate how much time it will take for the game to END. Soon you'll feel the urge to throw your chair through the window...not the loving-family-ambience you were expecting.

AND EVERY TIME YOU THINK THE GAME IS JUST ABOUT OVER, YOUR KID FALLS DOWN A CHUTE AND HAS TO START OVER ALMOST AT THE BEGINNING. You will find yourself lying to your children, telling them a "2" means "Move 4", and secretly scribbling over the chutes at midnight with a fat-tipped indelible black marker while spouting gibberish and drooling.

Let your kids play this at pre-school. Give it to the grandparents. JUST DO NOT ALLOW THIS GAME IN YOUR HOUSE IF YOU VALUE YOUR SANITY.

*the other two are Candy Land and the book "The Little Engine That Could"

reviewText:
Bright colors and a huggable body, as well as an assortment of accessories, make Adora Mixxie Pony 15" Plush and 11 Interchangeable Parts Including Unicorn Headband/Tutu/Necklace a fun toy.  This ponys turquoise body, dotted with pale blue hearts, contrasts nicely with his hot pink mane and tail; two hot pink legs printed with little white stars have purple-and-white gingham hooves have white stars scattered on them; and two black-and-white striped legs have tangerine hooves.  His two lime green ears and his lighter turquoise muzzle provide additional visual interest.  The ponys smile and nostrils are embroidered onto his muzzle; his smile is made of tan thread and his nostrils, brown thread.  Adora Mixxie Ponys warm brown eyes and eyelashes are appliqud onto the head; heart-shaped pupils make his expression very appealing.

The Adora Mixxie Pony is constructed well.  The short nap of the velour-like fabric is soft and touchable.  Seams are securely sewn; I could find no rough areas or places where there thread ends protruded from the ponys seams.  Weighing about 1 lb., Adora Mixxie Pony is easy for little ones to carry from place to place.

The accessories included with the Adora Mixxie Pony include two striped ribbon leg bands; a removable, lavender glittery, unicorn headband; a lavender necklace with a pink flower pendant; a hot pink tutu; and a white-dotted, lime green pony tail bow.  These add extra fun for little ones who may like to dress up their stuffed animals and dolls.

Although the legs, attached to the ponys body by buttons, are removeable, it is extremely difficult to do so.  As an adult, I struggled; my granddaughter found it impossible.  While this may be a negative for some, because the toy is meant for younger children I did not lower my rating.  Further, changing the legs around does not significantly alter this toys appearance or appeal and should not have an impact on its rating.  For little ones who love stuffed animals, especially horses and ponies, the Adora Mixxie Pony 15" Plush and 11 Interchangeable Parts Including Unicorn Headband/Tutu/Necklace will be a winner!

This is Killer Croc from Batman: Arkham Origins. Its a very nice, big action figure from DC Collectibles. It measures about 10.25 inches tall and is quite hefty. The sculpting and painting look good, with scales and spikes on his skin and back. He doesn't come with any accessories.

Articulation:
-Ball-jointed head
-Ball-hinged shoulders, wrists, and knees
-Swivel biceps and waist
-Single-hinge elbows
-Ab-crunch
-Hips hinge in and out, forward and backwards
-Ankles hinge and roll
The ankles on my figure were very tight, so be careful with the joints when trying to move him. I used a hairdryer for about 20 sec on the ankles to help free them. Once they move it has a good range of motion.

Overall this is a great figure for the price, which is $24.99 if you get it for MSRP. Good price for the size. He goes great with the other Arkham figures from the line. Definitely recommended.

I bought the bouncehouse about 3 weeks ago and have used it about four times.  I have been very happy with it.  My daughter is 3 1/2 years old, which is a perfect age for it.  I read all the product reviews before purchasing it, and they had a significant impact on my decision.  Interestly, the first thing my wife said once it was blown up, is that it was smaller than she thought it was going to be.  I had read the reviews beforehand (my wife hadn't) and so I knew others had the same initial impression, and I had also knew the measurements and sized it out.  Its not huge, but big enough for small children, and we've had an eleven year old in it having fun.  I like that the kids can bounce, climb, slide, and use the hoop.  I wanted to go slightly bigger, but I didn't see a bigger one from this manufacturer.  The quality is good enough.  My neighbor rents commercial ones several times per year and those can take a lot of rough-housing, but he was a twelve-year-old boy with friends.

It blows up extremely quickly.  They say you can store it in the box it comes in, but I don't see how.  I bought a bin that is larger, wider, and taller than the box it came in, and I still struggle to get it in there.  The cord is pretty long, but it would be nice if it were even longer.  The stakes they provide are plastic.  I drive a metal stake first, then insert the plastic ones, otherwise they may not last long if your ground is rough like mine.  I also lay a plastic tarp under the bouncehouse to protect the bottom, but it also helps prevent grass, etc from entering the bouncehouse as when the kids get off the slide, they step on the tarp instead of on grass.  If this company makes a bigger one, I would buy it and will probably need to eventually.  In closing, the neighbor kids are over more often now, which says a lot about how much they like it.

Our kids absolutely love this gun! It fits in their hands (4 year old and 7 year old) perfectly. The rubber "bullet" shoots out with a loud sound that makes each shot exciting. Yet the only thing that keeps this from being a perfect 5-star item is that the bullet gets stuck with too much regularity (like 25% of the time). When this happens, you have to manually remove the bullet and replace it. It's not horrible, but it does impede play and regularly require adult intervention. reviewText:
I think Hasbro is the latest owner of the rights to publish Twixt in English. Yet Hasbro choose to not publish Twixt. Something is wrong with the system. Does Hasbro get to decide that Americans cannot play Twixt?

GRAPH PAPER SUBSTITUTE:
You can play on graph paper. Use pencil to outline 23x23 atomic squares, giving you one overall outer square. Each of the four outer edges thus has a length of 24 corner-points. The corner-points are all that matter in Twixt, and they are called "holes".

GOAL:
The goal of player 1, red, is to build an unbroken chain of his red links to connect the north & south edges of the board. The goal of player 2, blue, is to link the east & west edges with his blue links. No link can be built to cross through any other link; thus only one player can ultimately succeed and win.
No player is allowed to place a peg into any of the four outermost corner holes.

LINKS EXPLAINED:
A link consists of two pegs connected by one bridge, all of the same color. A peg can support an unlimited number of bridges in different directions. The exact length of a bridge must be like a knight move in chess, the two pegs must be in holes with that alignment.

PLAYER TURNS:
Each turn consists of...
1. Place one of your pegs into a hole.
2. Remove any of your old bridges (rare, but sometimes important).
3. Build any new bridges you want, although the new bridges must use the new peg you played.

STRATEGIES:
[A] Vortexes are crucial in Twixt. For example, imagine you place a peg so that there are 3 holes between the new peg and an old peg of yours (called a "beam" shape). Now on your next turn you have two holes wherein you can place a peg and suddenly build 2 bridges, making one long powerful linkage. Neutralizing your opponent's votexes is a surprisingly deep challenge, as is preparing vortexes that your opponent cannot neutralize.
[B] The building of bridges too early can lead to disaster. I feel like defense is the best offense in Twixt, and a powerful offense it is.
[C] Your ideas will evolve about how close to place your peg to the opponent's peg.

TWO PROBLEMS WITH GRAPH PAPER:
[A] The rules allow you to remove any of your old bridges, but of course erasing ink and even colored pencil lines on paper is messy or impossible.
[B] Occasionally the hand & eye simply draw in the wrong place by obvious stupid mistake, and again we have the messy erasure problem.

FUN:
Twixt is one of those rare abstract strategy games is based on an elegant idea, has very simple rules, has great visuals, and where the strategies begin to become clear quickly after the first game. Yet the strategies run deep too (the better player will win).
The strategies in Twixt are of a fun sort, something that many abstract strategy games cannot claim as strongly.

SUBSTITUTE GAME?:
** Ponte del Diavolo: Supposedly perhaps intended to be Twixt with extra gadgets or doodads added, perhaps to avoid patent infringement (just a wild guess)? I have never played it (I own a physical Twixt game).

OTHER GREAT GAMES:
These each have their own very interesting elegant fundamental idea.

Quoridor: A game your non-game-playing wife can like, yet not simplistic. Strategies emerge after first game. Thrilling surprises occur during the game. Simply get your pawn onto any square in the opponent's home/back row. The opponent will harass you by using some turns to place a fence rather than move his pawn (you do the same, of course). Crucial is that it is illegal for either player to build a chain of fences that would make winning impossible; this rule has surprising effects. Nice visuals. A wonderful game.

Kamisado: You must move your one piece that matches the symbol (or hat color) of the square to which the opponent's just now moved his piece to. Pieces can move forward only (columns or diagonals), and cannot move sideways nor backwards. Goal is to get any one of your pieces onto the home/back row of the opponent. Great game, yet I was surprised that this was the most popular of several games during a long group holiday visit by our extended family. People lined up to play. One game lasts 10-16 minutes.

Khet: The coolest idea, you maneuver mirrors to direct a laser to kill the opponent's pharoh.

Quarto: A very good game, but not quite great. Games are short and sweet. Non-game-players can enjoy playing a couple quick games of Quarto. No player owns any pieces (like how in chess one player owns the white pieces), and no player is ever "losing". Instead the game suddenly ends with a winner. Try to make 4-in-a-row of any dimension: height, shape, color, density. Nicely interactive because you must play the piece that your opponent gives you at the end of his turn.
summary: Hasbro Should Publish Twixt, or Release It

reviewText: Were you good at Tetris?  Are you "Geometrically Advanced"?  Do you like fast paced games? Ubongo is for you!  This is a great board game for fast, intense, brain teasing fun!  Basically, the game is played with small boards that have a variety of choices for the puzzle pieces and you fit them to the squares in the puzzle. The first to fit the puzzle with the pieces yells, "UBONGO!!"  VERY easy to learn when you start to play. The instructions are simple and clear, there is no frustrating "what the heck are they talking about?" moments.  There is a cool way to score using "jewels", small plastic pieces.  It can be frustrating at first, this is a game for people who are good with shapes, if you aren't be patient.  Usually there is that one person who is great at these puzzles (my girlfriend is a ringer!) but once you catch on, it becomes a lot easier to play.  The one complaint is that there are a lot of pieces to this game.  However, the makers know this and give you bags and ways to keep things neat and separated.  Absolutely, if you like good and interesting party games that really do use your visual senses and logic, Ubongo is a wonderful choice....just don't lose the pieces.

reviewText:
Deadpool. One crazy guy, that made a huge splash outside of the comic world with a movie that was a huge success. People in the know have loved Deadpool for years. For me, he was in and out of comics that I read. I knew who he was. I knew he had a loud mouth and great jokes that could rival Spider-Man. It wasn't until more recently that I started to get the collected volumes to really delve into the character. And boy does this not disappoint.
Now we have the figure. Part of the X-Men series, since he wants to be an X-Men over almost anything else. What do we get with this figure? First and foremost, we get a fantastic figure. We get some nice new body parts. The forearms and the shins are both covered in armor. He has a great head sculpt that gives a wonderful expression. And he comes with a few costume accessories that really add to the outfit, including the belt, shoulder holster for his katana blades, and leg holster for his gun. So, with such a great figure, how can we top that? Add in more accessories than I have ever seen come with one figure, and more than some waves have had over all of the figures combined. Let's take a look at what we get.
First off, a knife. I am sure if Deadpool is using a knife, he is out of options... like cutting off his own hand to get away. There is a sheath along the outside of his left leg to keep it nice and close by.
Next up is a pair of guns. They look like they are Desert Eagles. A little small if they are, but fairly well done. They both have a holster, one on the hip, and one on the thigh. Yay for storage for your guns!!!!
Next up, the pair of Katana blades. Can't be Deadpool with out going into a gun fight wielding a pair of swords. They look great. They were nice and straight out of the box, and fit nicely into the sheaths running down his back.
Then we get a little crazy. A rocket launcher with punching fist. This is the same rocket launcher we got with The Punisher, but without the boxing glove. Thankfully, if you want a more serious tone, the boxing glove is removable. The rocket launcher pegs into the hole in his back.
We get a couple of extra weapons. One is a repaint of the shotgun that came with The Punisher. This time around, it is a much better silver color. The other gun is a futuristic rifle. It makes me think of the Kree storyline where Deadpool was pretending to work with them while he was actually working on destroying them.  These guns are extra, and do not have a place to be stored on Deadpool.  I am thinking some straps need to be added, because Deadpool needs to go into battle with every weapon that is not tied down.
Finally we get an alternate head. We need an unmasked head, because how else is he going to eat that taco he also comes with? The head looks horribly great. He is no doubt a burn victim of some sort. The smile is well done, and shows he cannot be kept down by that ugly face.
This figure is great. No wonder it took me so long to get my hands on. Everyone and their brother wanted this figure. It was an additional figure to the wave, so it did not come with a BAF part. Instead they filled every part of the box with some kind of death instrument. What fun!!!
summary: One of the best figures EVER!

reviewText:
My son got the leappad from his grandmother for his birthday.  He's had it for one week, and he's totally in love.  It's wonderful for holding his attention and keeping him occupied (rest time is never a fight anymore, and he's always got something to do when we run errands).  The educational value is pretty good as far as electronic toys go.  He's learning to write and draw better, and his reading is improving too.  He has such a fun time taking his own pictures and videos as well.  And the cool value is important too - he thinks he's such a big shot because he has his own "ipad"!

My only gripe about the leappad is that it eats batteries.  We've had it for a week and I've already put 3 sets of batteries in it.  It would be nice if it had a rechargeable battery like the nintendo ds (or the real ipad!) so I wasn't constantly feeding it batteries.  That's really my only complaint though, and it's a pretty minor one at that.  If batteries is the price I pay for a happy quiet child when I need one, I'm glad to supply batteries - I just buy them in bulk.

Overall, great toy.  Pricey, and eats batteries, but worth it.

reviewText:
My boys love Jake and the Neverland Pirates and it is show that we have nothing for - no books or toys.  Now that they are getting more into board games I love that Wonder Forge has created a game featuring their favorite pirates gang and its honestly a game I don't mind either!

Setting up the game is easy - just snap in the two tree and the hammock with the included rubber bands.  Then place Hook and his 12 treasures on the hammock.  Then 2-4 players take turns moving around the board game with the goal of removing the most treasure pieces and not knocking off Hook.  There is no Start or Finish, just whoever knocks Hook off.  Each player spins to see how many moves they make and then depending on what you land on is what you do.  Land on a Treasure chest, remove that type of treasure, Land on a colored "X" removed a treasure of that color, and it you land on a Tool you have to remove a treasure using a specific tool.  Yes the tools are pretty cool and make the game challenging.  There is a shovel, sword, tweezers, and fishing hook.  Oh and if you spin the Broken Bride, any player on a bridge piece loses a treasure piece to Tick Tock Croc who is sitting patiently under Hook's hammock.  The game is over when Hook falls or all treasure pieces removed.

This is a board game unlike others we have played and its fun for the whole family.  We are practicing decision making especially with this game as my boys have learned not to just grab any piece!

He loves sharks, boats, and building, so 3 out of 5 isn't bad.  This has kept him entertained for quite awhile.  He did get frustrated when he couldn't use all of the pieces at one time.  His frustration was compounded by his mom's because that means there are always loose pieces.  There isn't an internal storage system the way it is with some other milti-piece toys.

My daughter was also concerned when her lovely son made the shark eat the captain.  We were grateful that there is a slit in the rubbery belly that made it easier to rescue the captain, but they expressed concern that it was necessary.  All boys, no matter the age, will make the shark eat the captain and/or the diver.  He also brought the shark to us when he couldn't get the oyster and two propellers out of the shark's belly.  The oyster is a bit tight.

This is a wonderful toy for imaginative children.  Having a way to store all of the pieces together would make it better for parents.  Oh yes, I need to comment that it would be easy to wrap this box, although it's definitely not frustration-free packaging.  So many toys like this are in open front boxes making wrapping difficult if not impossible.  This one has a small opening in the clear plastic so you can try out moving the shark's fin and making its mouth open.  Thank you, Matchbox, for that.

reviewText:
This game was a lot of fun, has a lot of re-play value and is well-suited for young kids AND adults alike. (Seriously...what adult doesn't LOVE the Charlie Brown Halloween Special!?) I've purchased themed games before and usually their game-play elements are very basic in nature. (Think "Candyland"). However, I was pleasantly surprised that this game had more to it that just your typical *be-the-first-to-get-the-to-end* kind of thing.

The object IS to the be the first to return to the pumpkin patch, BUT you have to have at least 5 pieces of candy AND to be in your character's costume to do so. (At first, the costuming part seems kinda pointless, but it keeps you from getting bored with the trick-or-treating aspect because chances are, you will be going around the board more than a few times.)

You start out in plain clothes in the pumpkin patch. You then move to the outer board where you go "trick-or-treating". This is where you have to collect a minimum of five "Candy" Trick-or-Treat cards AND land on your character's costumed space to get in costume. However, it could take several rounds to land on that one space, all the while you're collecting "Trick-or-Treat" cards by landing on "Trick-or-Treat" spaces carefully placed in front of various house illustrations. (My daughter showed lots of enthusiasm yelling "TRICK-OR-TREAT" everytime she landed on one of these spaces...so that was just a bonus.) :)

Trick-or-Treat cards may be either "Candy" cards, "Rocks" cards or "Quarters" cards. If you draw a "Rocks" card, you lose one candy card from your stash. (If your total "Candy" card stash drops below 5, then now you have to go around again until you have at least 5 before you can head back to the Pumpkin Patch.) If you draw a "Quarters" card, you take a candy card from any other player AND get another turn. There's ONE "Invitation" card, and if you're lucky enough to draw that card, you don't have to have the 5 pieces of candy to return to the pumpkin patch. (You DO still have to have your costume on though.) Once you land on you character's corresponding costume space, you them change your playing piece to your character in costume. (Or you could just add the little playing piece to your stash if you choose.)

So it's quite fun to play, and just when you think it's getting a little monotonous, all of a sudden someone's luck will drastically change and the race back to the pumpkin patch begins. My 5-year old daughter had a LOT of fun playing this, and it's also the first board game where she was actually interested enough to learn the rules and play through to the end properly.

There's a Peanuts Christmas game as well, and it has similarities to how this one plays, but it's different enough to warrant owning as well. So I would recommend that game to anyone that enjoys this game.

I even went as far as picking up some little, PVC Peanuts figures on eBay to use instead of the cardboard playing pieces....because, well...I'm a nerd that way. :p

All in all, the best part of this game is that it gets you in that holiday mood, which is (in my humble opinion) a HUGE success because that was the entire purpose of the Peanut's holiday specials! So to the designers, BRAVO! Also, it was a great low price! :)
summary: Excellent game that captures the feel of the cartoon!

reviewText:
Pro's:
1)  RC car is great for my 7 y/o.  Bought it for his birthday.  Its quick, fun, and tears through most anything he hits.  Drives very fast on the driveway and road.  Hits the unmowed lawn with speed and maintains it throughout.  Up and down ditches like a champ.  Through mulched beds with ease.  He drives it through the forest in the back yard over hills and dirt bike ramps with ease too.
2) For a 7 y/o it took a few runs to get used to the skid steer, but that was expected.
3) OUTSTANDING customer service.  His left wheels started to 'stick' causing the car to not drive straight when commanded.  This happened w/in 3 months of purchase.  Emailed Kidzlane, and they took care of it with ease!  Very impressed with their desire to maintain good customer relations!  Thanks Kidzlane!

Cons:
1) Easy to flip.  If he drives to hard into a steep hill, or hits reverse on both wheels when going full speed forward, the vehicle will flip.  No biggie, but it scratches the roof.
2) Battery installation is difficult, requiring a screwdriver (provided).  Understand it's needed to keep watertight battery compartment, but I would think a quick latch system would work.
3) Battery life can be less than desired.  Quick solution was to purchase additional batteries for hours of fun.

Overall - this car is a beast for it's price, and my boy is loving every minute of it.  Kidzlane has been outstanding in their service.  Highly recommend purchasing this if you are considering an inexpensive RC car for your child.

Update, Dec 2015. I can't praise the Customer service of Kidzlane enough!  Our toy broke again, a plastic gear in the wheels stripped.  Kidzlane replaced for free!  If you like amazing Customer service - Go with these guys!
summary: Great product for a 7 y/o. Great customer service.  100% satisfied.

reviewText:
I recently received the Zoomer Dino Jester for free from BzzAgent to try out and review.
 First impression was the toy seemed to be well made and attention grabbing. When handled it does not seem to be flimsy or have parts that feel weak. The colors are cool and its design is cool.
We fully read the instructions and charged for one hour as directed before trying it out. At first he seemed cool running around and making noises. But when we tried to change his mode or take control of him nothing worked. I then tried charging longer and this made him almost complete useless. I used different batteries in the controller, let him set over night, etc. But could not get him to work. I emailed Spinmaster and they promptly responded with some suggestions and an 800 #. The suggestions did not work, so we called and got excellent customer service who actually went and got one of their own and played along with us. They got him working.
After finally having a working unit we got to try him out. This is quite a cool controlled vehicle. The burps and cow noises made everyone laugh, except our dogs who ran from him. I love patrol mode and make him charge me and shaking his tail until he is mad is hilarious. The balance gyro in this toy is actually quite advanced. He rolls around with ease. Keeping him in the mode you want still is an issue, but he is fun enough to ignore.
Follow up: Only charge for one hour - overcharging messes it up. To change mode he must be only on his wheels, will not change if tail is on the ground. And Spinmaster customer service is really that great service for the customer.
summary: Cool RC vehicle that you do not have to always control

reviewText:
This game is so poorly designed and annoying it will be going to Goodwill very soon. Where to begin with the issues...

The Timer - You slap the red button in the middle to start the timer. Each person has 10 seconds to think of a word, push the letter and push the red timer button again to begin the 10 seconds for the next player. Couple of issues here...
1 - The timer is LOUD! I mean REALLY LOUD and ANNOYING. Because of the volume of the timer this is incredibly distracting to both kids and adults. To the point that nobody would play more than twice and that was with a lot of coaxing.
2 - There is no way to turn the timer off. When you are done with the round it just keeps ticking until 10 seconds is up. Because it's so loud, 10 seconds seems like an eternity.

The Rules - When you are done with a round (having chosen a word for every letter) and there is more than one player still "alive", you are supposed to keep going, now thinking of words that begin with 2 of the letters. Really? There are so many better ways to have a tie breaker or continue the game. This is really illogical given the very limited amount of letters.

Missing Letters - The game is missing the letters Q, Qu (as in many games offer a Qu), U, V, X, Y, Z. How creative is that? You can't use Yellow, Venture, Zebra, Uncle and many others that were said but couldn't be used because the letter isn't there.

Packaging - The game comes with a very small deck of cards (with 4 topics per card - don't get me started...) and the Tapple disc. To store the game you get a box. A box that opens on the side. There is no place to put the cards so they don't just slide all over the place. The Tapple disc will also be sliding around the box with the cards, bending and otherwise damaging the cards. They don't even give you a baggie to put your cards in.

Oh, and it takes batteries... No real reason for the batteries but, yeah, it takes batteries.

I could go on but I think this makes the point. At the end of the day, nobody wanted to play this game, it's frustrating as H@!! and is a mess waiting to happen. We will be packing the little cards in a baggie and dropping this off at the charity shop the first chance I get.

Oh, and I find it comical that the company calls themselves "Educational Insights."  The only educational thing this product does is teach kids to wait patiently and then learn to deal with the disappointment of a junky toy.

PERFECT!!! Finding learning devices for my two year old can be a chore sometimes because he has a younger brother who just loves to chew on EVERYthing. Well, that's to be expected since he's teething. So, when I found these, I immediately jumped on ordering them for multiple reasons.

1) They consist of a variety of different objects. Some that my two year old doesn't know quite yet so he gets to learn something new.
2) They are foam! I have had bad luck with magnets of the "reinforced cardboard" type. His younger brother can grab these and gnaw to his heart's delight and they remain intact which leads me to...
3) The magnet covers the whole back. It's thin magnetic backing instead of a some tiny nubby square or circle being glued onto the back. It pretty much eliminates that particular choking danger. Obviously, kids being kids, you should ALWAYS keep an eye on them because god knows what they're going to try to shove up their nose or what new object they think might taste good - but the backing on these has not worn off, peeled off, or come apart as of yet and my boys have been playing with/chewing on them for about two months now.

Lastly, if your tub is of metal making, they can play with them during bath time. It's a great distraction from when I'm trying to get behind their ears. :-)

I highly recommend this - they work on the fridge, your filing cabinet, a kid's magnetic board, the bath tub - they'll even just line them up on the floor. Great learning toy that has withstood the destructive hands of children.

reviewText: First off, let's get the most important part out of the way: THIS IS THE BASE BLASTER. NO MAGAZINES/CLIPS, NO DARTS, NO STOCK, NO BARREL, AND NO BATTERIES. ALL SOLD SEPARATELY. With that out of the way, the blaster itself is fairly decent. It's a semi-auto, clip-fed blaster; firing 1 round with each trigger pull. More or less a Stryfe with more rail attachment points. It is notably front-heavy, as the battery case is in the gray foregrip, with the motors above that, and having a much longer front-end compared to a Stryfe, making it harder to single-wield if you don't have the arm strength. Moreso if you kit it out with accessories and a barrel (or two, if using barrels that allow another barrel to be attached). It is compatible with almost every detachable Nerf stock, Nerf barrel, Nerf rail, and Nerf clip accessory, from the old Raider stock and Longstrike barrel to the Firefly dart magazine or Raider 35-round drum. However, the only darts it can fire are the new Elite darts (and similar Chinese copies). Older dart head types will not work in the clip or with the motors (suction darts get stuck in the rubber passthrough inside the gun). Rapid fire is not recommended; as you do need to allow the motors to reach full rev again after each shot; otherwise, it'll quickly cut down the ranges of additional fired darts. Fortunately, this doesn't take long. Initial revv'ing up does take a few seconds though. There is one notable issue with the blaster itself; scopes are practically useless on this blaster; the top rail is too high and the forward top rail is blocked by the carrying handle in the back. Why I gave it 5 stars: Because it's the base blaster, which is all I needed. I already have plenty of Nerf accessories I can use or reuse with this blaster, many of them as good as, if not better than, the Modulus remakes, and it's cost-competitive (as a Prime member) and more common than old Stryfes (hard to find on local shelves and often about the same price after shipping costs). Not to mention, it performs better than a basic and unmodded Stryfe despite a few setbacks (mainly weight and scope use). This definitely isn't the blaster version to buy if you're looking for a brand new blaster as a gift; you would be better served getting the Modulus starter pack and just buy a set of batteries. Lithium AAs work well if you want a bit more kick than regular AAs. Nerf N-Strike Modulus ECS-10 Blaster

reviewText:
This is an OK build (*but see my addendum on the decals below). Not surprisingly, the other recent review's comments are about how much better the 1/350 model is, rather than how semi-good this one is. But not everyone has space for a 3' model, never mind the hefty price tag, leaving this 1/1000 version an ambivalently best choice for the casual hobbyist.

 -- on the one hand, extraordinary attention is given to tiny details of the various versions of Enterprise: the first pilot, the second pilot, the "Mirror" version, and of course the standard version which graced the remaining 77 episodes. Heck, you can make it the Constellation, the Defiant, or even the Exeter (from "the Omega Glory"; I had to look it up).

-- You can choose whether to have vents or orbs on back of the nacelles [both being correct, of course], not to mention points on the front. Those who have studied "The Cage" footage in detail will appreciate that the decal set includes those minor differences, not to mention the slightly larger command dome. And the engine nacelles feature one clear plastic dome inside another, allowing the modeler to paint the inside one [to create translucent color]. The Botany Bay is a nice addition.

On the other, the assembly does feel a bit cheap. The fit is not always very good, the size is rather small at 11-1/2 inches. Though made to snap together, I found it necessary to scrape & trim with a razor to get some parts together; even then, some parts still needed glue, and some never came together very well under any circumstance [e.g., gapping between the top & bottom halves of the saucer]. Assembling the stand as instructed results in a starship ready to fall off, so it's better to just ram the steel pin into the bottom of the ship. The one remarkably good part of the assembly is that the nacelles do not sag.

Level 2 or no, it would take a remarkably talented modelist to get this model to look anything like the photo on the outside of the box. I can't help comparing this to the AMT model that I built several times, decades ago. That model had its own problems [see "The Trouble With Tribbles", where the model outside the K-7 clearly displays the AMT nacelle sag], but was more aesthetically pleasing, even with [or partly because of] the debated grid lines. This version is like having a so-so car with a really fantastic wrap job. The parts and decals speak to the obsessive detailist, while the so-so fit speaks of one happy with anything that's in the ballpark.

Still, it made my son happy, and me more appreciative of what rewards await me in the 1/350.

Addendum: The real fun of this model is in the decals; buying several allows one to create a small fleet, complete with proper registration numbers. Those decals do get tiny indeed -- having a magnifying glass on a stand will be essential -- but they add subtlety and interest, and indeed distract me from my complaints about the so-so fit. The opportunity to make [for example] the mirror-universe "I.S.S Enterprise" (complete with spiked-planet logos) brought back the excitement that was missing from the snap-together assembly, and I am raising my earlier three-star rating to four
summary: You get what you pays for, and you don't complain

reviewText:
My daughter is a bit younger than the recommended age range for this set (12 months as opposed to 18 months).  Of course, her playtime is always well supervised, and I did not feel that this toy was in any way a danger.  The pieces are large, and it's very engaging even for someone so young.  Although she's at that stage where she wants to be constantly in motion, this Klip Klop Stable set from Fisher-Price actually prompted her to sit down and play for an extended period (and even longer when I sat with her and played alongside her).

Because her older sister (five years) is a big fan of Disney Princesses, this playset fit right in with our other toys.  My five-year-old expressed limited interest in the stable set on her own (she prefers dolls that she can dress up), but what this toy did accomplish was quite amazing.  Because my older daughter loves princesses, this playset allowed her the chance to calmly play with her younger sister with something that was interesting and somewhat engaging for both of them.  I've long been looking for a toy that both girls could enjoy, or at least something that would interest the older girl in playing with her younger sibling.  In that respect, this Klip Klop Stable was a great success and a popular addition to the girls' room.

My younger daughter likes the sounds that the horses make and mainly just likes holding the pieces and moving them around a little, while her older sister simply likes horses and princesses, making this set "cool" just on the surface.  It's really a nice combination of elements to engage a fairly wide age range for young girls.  As it happens, Rapunzel is my older daughter's favorite princess of the moment, and she was thrilled that this set came with her included (along with Aurora who is not as popular or as recognizable in our house).  Of course, in a perfect world the most popular princesses - Ariel and Belle - would be included as well, but at least they're available separately in case we absolutely need to have them (which will probably be the case if this remains a popular toy for the next month or two).

Essentially, if you have a girl - or a couple of girls - between the ages of 1 and 5, there's a lot to like about this set.  And it might even encourage your kids to play together, which is a definite plus.
summary: Encourages my daughters to play together

reviewText:
The box features the new 2013 LEGO Star Wars design which features a green background to complement the Yoda figure in the top right of the box. The box advertises a poster inside and shows the mini-figures with details of the set's features on the back.

Initially I was a little hesitant, to buy this, when this set first came out because it looked like just another rework of an old set from 2008  however, there real improvements in this set in my opinion. It may look, just about similar on the outside, but the construction has been greatly developed. This one is very well designed and sturdy set. It includes a little handle that you can grab to pick it up (or hang it from a shelf, but it is strong enough that you can easily grab it from the bottom or top and it will stay together.

On opening the box, you will find 10 bags in total. 9 of the bags include the set pieces and are numbered 1-9. The 10th bag includes two sets of instructions, a piece of cardboard (to place the set on as you build and work on it); there are a sheet of stickers, and a poster. The building instructions here are detailed. They give you a good general overview of what you will be building from each bag of Lego.

The good:

- The redesign is so much better in terms of stability
-It is great to have the side turrets back
-The red clone trooper was a great additional mini-figure
-The weapon storage, in the back was a nice touch

The build was fun without being too difficult, there is so much playable value here, when it is done, and you do not have to worry about pieces coming loose when you pick it up. Is there anything that set lacks? Well there could have been more clone troops included, in what in essence is a troop carrier - that said Lego had done a sterling job on this set.

reviewText:
My Garrus has finally arrived! YES! I have made a list of pros and cons that should help any on the fence buyers. Here goes!

Pros+
+Garrus is built like a brick. He is dense and able to stand some punishment.
+Garrus, like all the Mass Effect Play Arts figures has great articulation. I believe around twenty or so points. His legs are ratchet jointed, his shoulders are butterfly, like every other ME Play Arts. In short Garrus has the male Shepard build, tweaked for Turian amrour.
+Garrus looks just like Garrus( in game ). All the detail is nicely done.
+Garrus has not a loose joint to be found.
+Finally Garrus has an epic sniper, and a pretty great assult rifle. A spare set of hands but that it for his items.(same as All ME Play Arts)

Cons-
-Garrus from a distance looks great, up close he looks less then steller. His paint ap. for his face is shoddy.
-Top heavy does not even BEGIN to describe Garrus. He is almost unable to stand.
-His feet, though accurate to the game can't support his weight. Ouch.
-Like the other figures his hands have a hard time being switched out.
-Garrus is missing his HUGE scar on his face, it looks like it was just painted over, seeing as how the damage to his face is kind of there.
All in all Garrus is a good buy. Not perfect, none of the figures have been, but he is one of the best. His detail is nicely applied and whats better he is STRONG. I can not stress enough though that Garrus looks pretty rough around the face. If that bothers you wait until the price goes down. If you can over-look it, BUY HIM NOW! He looks great with my Femshep, Tali and Ash.

reviewText:
Smokescreen was one of the standout "new" Autobots that appeared in season 2 of the original show. I decided to start a mini-collection of Universe/Classics/Generations figures (to go with the IGear's unofficial PP01 Mini Masterpiece Optimus Prime) and this guy looked pretty good in pictures online, so he was my first pick.

In person, at first I thought his colors were a bit garish (especially after the first transformation into robot mode). Now that I look at him more, it's not too bad...they could have made him more uniform (see below) but what's here sort of fits in with the classic style.

Besides that, the mold has some problems. The front wheels were too high and stuck in the wells out of the box. His head is attached to a spring but doesn't peg onto anything once you get it out, so it's pretty loose. I could overlook some of these things if he were easy to get into a cool pose, but he's not. The aforementioned head isn't on a balljoint and is angled downward, so having his legs anything but straight will make him look down (yes, you can move his chest up to compensate but then there will be an ugly gap in his torso). His arms are a bit short but look good, outside of the door "wings" getting in the way because of the tires on his shoulders (the wings tend to pop off during transformation, and you can leave them off if you want). The biggest problem is with the legs - the hip parts don't rotate out much, and there is a swivel, but it's below the knee rather than at the thigh. It's hard to plant his feet flat, and even if you do, he tends to topple over due to all the weight above the waist. The best pose I could get him into is a sort of lean/turn to the side. Back in car mode, it's hard getting the panels on the sides of the hood to fit without leaving gaps. I got the wheels to sit flat and turn together, but it only works if other parts of the car aren't tight.

The Henkei (Japanese) version has a more uniform color scheme (light blues and more whites, and chrome missiles/gun) but is otherwise the same toy. Henkei TFs are always more expensive though, sometimes 3-4 times the cost of a Hasbro version. Personally, I like the colors on the Hasbro version more. I might paint the windows all grey (plus the rear "windows" that are just blue paint now), along with the usual painting tricks (blacklining, dry-brushing) to bring out the details in the gray parts.

This is the first of the new figures I'm getting into, the second being Sunstreaker. He's got a balljointed head and a more uniform color scheme, and while Smokescreen is decent, I'm hoping I'll like the next figure more.

reviewText:
Taking in her full body look, I am digging the design features.  She is wearing a hoodie that has ears on top.  Of course she is wearing her black mask as well.  To go with the black mask, she also has a black winged backpack.  She has on gauntlets of yellow and finishing off her arms are really well detailed black-gloved hands.  She has one open hand and one grasping hand.

She is wearing black pants that are on the snug side, but not skin tight.  She finishes off her look with a pair of yellow combat boots.

She has such a beautiful face.  It is a bit smoother than the beauty look of Monster High or Barbie Dolls.  Her eyes and eyebrows are painted on with a line of perfection.  She does not have any extra makeup over a bit of pink lip gloss.

Her backpack is a solid piece that has great detailing all it's own.  She has the requisite bat wings along with details of zippers and a pocket.

Her gauntlets are removable.  As you would expect from the makers of Monster High, Mattel did really good with the body parts, allowing for the hands to be pulled off to remove the gauntlets.  The only thing I don't like about the gauntlets is that they cover some really good forearm detail.  This girl has some muscle, and the forearms are great.  Take a peek under that sleeve, and you can see Batgirl has a pair of concealed weapons.  She has good muscle tone going on all over the place.

In the store, and in the box, it is a bit hard to tell, but side by side, there is a fairly large discrepancy between DC Super Hero Girls and Monster High.  It is clear that Mattel went with whole new bodies for this line.  It is a bummer for the people out there with a large number of MH dolls.  Sorry, your DC Girls will not be borrowing anything from your MH girls.

reviewText:
Dark Horse Deluxe and Gentle Giant have teamed up to bring us fans of HBOs Game of Thrones action figures. I anticipate that people will be annoyed and or pissed that these figures are in a static pose and have no articulation. There was a rather negative reaction to Mezcos Breaking Bad Walter White action figure having no articulation and I suspect there will be some displeased buyers who aren't expecting a figure in a static pose. I don't mind because I am keeping my in their box.

Daenerys Targaryen is my favorite figure of this first wave of Game of Thrones figures. This looks a lot like Emilia Clarke who plays Daeny on the show. I like that you can pick any one of the three Dragon eggs to place in her hands. Again this figure/series by Dark Horse Deluxe and Gentle Giant do not have any kind of articulation. The box that the Dragon eggs come in can be opened and closed, but thats the only articulation be found here. It is a bit disappointing that these figures are not articulated, a simple neck articulation and arm articulation at the shoulders would have been nice, but oh well. Im still pleased with this figure, the great sculpt, the great paint apps, accessories and the base really make this figure great. Any fan of the show should grab these while they can. Theyre not available on Amazon until February the 7th, but I got mine from Entertainment Earth already, and for a few dollars cheaper. This figure come HIGHLY APPROVED.

reviewText:
Just to be clear, right from outset  the title of this game says it all!  You definitely need to be a Movie Buff to play this, and you need to be really good at remembering actors, their roles, and specific quotes from the movies.  I love movies, so I figured I would love this game.  But Im not all that great at coming up with names and quotes on my own.

Heres how this game works:  Everyone is dealt 10 cards from a huge pile of cards.  Most of the cards read, Movie, Actor, Role, or Quote.  The player going first can play any one of these four, and then name the movie, actor, role, or quote they're referencing.  The next player then plays off on the actor or film, adding another actor, role, or quote.  This goes on until the players cant think of anything else to add, or until someone plays one of the Strategy Cards, which allow you to switch things up.  For example, if I started with a Movie card and named the film War of the Worlds, and then the second player put down an Actor card and named Tom Cruise, the third player could put down a Reverse Angle strategy card, which would allow him to take the game in another direction.  This player could then play another Movie card and name the film, Mission Impossible, which means the play switches to this new film (also starring Tom Cruise).  The object of the game is to get rid of all the cards in your hand  the first one to do so wins.

Its really not hard at all to get the hang of playing this.  What IS hard is coming up with actors and character names and direct quotes (unless thats your thing).  Had this game included a Director card, I might have had more luck (for some reason I remember directors more than I do actors and their character names).

This can be a fun game  and you can adjust the rules to fit the people playing.  But its a little pricey for a box of cards that contain no information on them at all.  This is not a trivia game, even though thats how its being marketed.  There are no questions and no answers.  Its up to the players to come up with everything (and up to the players to determine whether the names and titles and quotes are correct!).

Bottom line, this is pretty much a game that works or not depending on whos playing.  And you could probably play it on your own, without any cards at all.  Would I pay $25 for this set of cards?  No, I would not.  The box is cute, though!

reviewText:
This METAKOO pocket quadcopter is SO COOL!  Its very small, in fact, its smaller than my thumb. However, its big on fun. Also, its really easy to fly. I wouldn't recommend using this inside, until you've mastered the controls. You'll just keep bouncing it against the walls, and eventually break it. My buddy and me took my big quadcopter and this one to a large empty parking lot down by the river. For a novice, this is the perfect quadcopter to learn the controls for several reasons. First, it has intelligent height. The big problem I have with the large quadcopters, is that they can shoot up in the air 40 feet or more within a few seconds, and start to get away from you. (My one quadcopter is living in the top of a large pine tree, for that reason.) This minicopter won't do that. Maybe it'll fly 6-8 feet high, but not much higher than that. The elevation is very easy to control. I was also able to fly it low enough, that my cat could chase it. Another thing about the controls I like, is that it maneuvers fairly easily, though sometimes these things seem to have a mind of their own. I like flying these at night, since they have little LED red/blue lights, above each foot. So, they're easy to spot. Just now, I was outback flying it in the dark, and it went over to my neighbor's yard, then out to the alley, then back to my yard, then crashed against another neighbor's garage door. Down at the river, I noticed when it took off, it was going 25 yards away from the controller, but still was connected to the signal.

You've love the ease of operation. There's an ON/OFF switch on the copter, and another ON/OFF switch on the controller. Turn them both on, flip up the switch between the two joy sticks, and you're flying. The controller takes two AAA batteries, but the copter has a built in lithium battery you charge with the included charger. Aerodynamically, I have no idea how or why this thing flies, or how it remains level, or knows how to keep steady at a reasonable height. Maybe the spinning propellers act as gyroscopes, but that's just a guess. I can promise you, you'll love playing with this. To learn, I'd definitely go someplace with some space, like a parking lot, or a large mowed field.  Except for the size, it's a lot like flying a larger quadcopter.

The Ravensburger Smartscope is a fun and inventive way to allow children to view objects microscopically.  It's especially helpful for younger children because they often don't understand how to close one eye and look through a microscope with the open eye. Also, more than one person can view the enlarged images at the same time so no one is saying, "My turn, I want to look now" and "No, I'm not done looking yet".

The assembly instructions that come with the kit are mostly pictures and they are not at all clear. However, better instructions can be obtained online by using the available QR code.  One we watched the online video, it was a snap to assemble.  I have an old Galaxy S3 phone that the kids play with and they use it with the Smartscope and it works very well.  One nice thing is that they can take a photo of the enlarged images if they'd like to.  They have used it to look at various insects, salt, leaves, and even dirt.

The Smartscope requires 3 AAA batteries which are not included, so be sure to have the batteries on hand or you'll have some very disappointed kids.

reviewText:
This was a fun family game!  Each card has an "easy" and a "hard" side.  We found that it was more even if the adults did the hard side while the kids (mine are age 9 and 11) did the easy.  My children are both whizzes at math, and my daughter loves puzzles, and they did really well at this!!  While you get rewarded for being the fastest, everyone gets to pull a random gem out of a bag at the end of each round.  Gems are worth different point amounts based on their color.  So even if you're not the fastest every time, depending on what you pick out of the bag, you still have a shot at winning the game!

Basically, you're doing puzzles with tetris-like pieces.  Everyone gets a set of pieces ( no 2 pieces are the same).  You get your card with the shape you're filling in with your pieces.  Someone rolls the dice- each card has multiple piece combinations you can use, and the dice tells you which shapes (3 on easy side, 4 on hard) you're going to use.  Flip the timer and go!

reviewText:
This figure was a real disappointment.  The figure itself looks like it was made from past pieces of Hans, but more on that later.
The action feature is terrible. The "quick draw" or "punch" is a step up from Arena escape Padme, granted, because you can put him in more than one than one pose.  But the only way I can get the action to work, is to hold him by his upper body- and what good is that?!.  They REALLY should have designed it like the Zam Wesell figure
As for the actual design of the figure- this was a major letdown.  For the most part, he looks like a custom figure made out of Bespin Han(although I imagine the customs would do a better job)
The vest looks just like his jacket- with a few modifications...it's even the same color!  The legs are terrible.  They are not smooth at all, and look like last-minute rush jobs(just look behind the holster and above right boot- who has a knee like that?)
His left hand looks just like cantina Han, with again, a slight modification.  I'm not pleased with the way his right arm hangs so loose when not in "quick draw" mode, and I don't know if it's just mine, but his face is just soooo shiny.
Han and the blaster had a few problems.  The first being lining them up.  In non "quick-draw" mode, he looks fine, but when you pull the arm up, the head and gun don't exactly match up.  Also, I'm nit picky and I like the blasters to fit in the holsters like cantina and Bespin Han's did.  This one didn't fit 100%
On the bright side, the face is a good rendition of Harrison Ford, and this is probably the best version of his blaster yet- being color coordinated.  The suction cup- grenades are a nice accessory, although looking at other Star Wars Saga figures, I did expects him to come with more items.
Endor Raid Han Solo has seven points of articulation(not including his right shoulder, which you can't move freely without the "quick draw" feature): Hips, right wrist, right elbow, waist, left shoulder, and neck.

reviewText:
Wow, how disappointing!  I was really looking forward to this game, but was disappointed from the start.  The technology falls short:
1.  The black and grey letter images are not very easy to read.  How about a little color and more definition?  The displays remind me of the first attempts at electronic devices.
2.  You can only read the letters if you are looking directly down on them from above.  This makes it nearly impossible to watch others as they play.
3.  Right answers and repeat answers are noted with an audible beep.  Correct answers darken, but sometimes you can't tell the difference between correct combinations and repeated combinations.  There should be more distinct responses for the two results. If color were added, repeat answers could turn red, correct answers could flash green.
4.  Larger tiles would be helpful for older eyes.
5.  As with other reviews, some valid combinations never scored, the game needed to be reset frequently, and words that don't exist scored.
6.  I wish there were more multiple player options.

I guess this sounds more like an enhancement request for Scrabble, than a review for potential buyers! I hope they read this because I will definitely snap up a new, improved version!

reviewText: Mechanical toys like this usually creep me out, but this little guy is surprisingly cute!  My 3 year old LOVES "feeding" him with the bottle and the sounds he makes are adorable -- either little slurping sounds, a tiny (polite, almost!) little baby burp, different little coo-ing sounds (one of which has the intonation of "I love you!"), etc. -- and sometimes he moves his little feet like he's being tickled.  If you feed him for a little bit and then stop, he makes a really cute little snoring sound, so my daughter says "Mommy! I was able to get the baby to sleep!" ha!  For those of you thinking this is only a "girl's toy" (as if there were such a thing!), please take note that my HUSBAND was dying to try it and I found him rocking and feeding the little bear too!  I think this would be a great "new baby" gift for the new big sister (or brother) -- so the older sibling can "feed" her new toy while her parents are caring for the newest addition to the family.  I bought him for ten bucks and thought that was a fair price.  I wouldn't pay twenty though - so just put it in your cart and wait until it goes down.  Oh gosh, he is so cute that maybe I would have even paid twenty. :)  He's much softer than I expected too.

reviewText:
Awesome figure. Incredible sculpt, detailed paint work, and solid accessories.

One of the coolest things about this figure is his costume design. It's littered with question marks, with the main attraction actually being on the figure's back. There's a large, sculpted, yellow question mark, and it looks awesome. So much so that this is one figure you may actually consider displaying from the back. It really does look that cool.

Articulation isn't great though. His arms and head are fine. Very good actually. But past that it's pretty limited. The way the articulation is sculpted into the figure looks great, and he stands OK on his own, but only really in one leg position. A base helps if you really wanna pose this figure around.

His accessories are great. Only two of them but what's here is cool. I like the translucent cane, and the hat is removable. It falls off his head fairly easy though, but once posed it's likely not gonna go anywhere.

Overall a very cool Riddler figure, and the head sculpt (and sculpt all around) is really the main selling point here. Overall he just looks great. But don't expect to get a ton of articulation out of him. You can still get cool poses just because his arm articulation is really good, and there's fun stuff you can do with the cane if you get creative, but don't expect to get him to stand outside of a flat standing pose. At least not without a base.

EDIT: Hand broke off when trying to get the staff out of it, applying very little force. Dropped score to 3 stars from 5. Tired of broken figures!!!

reviewText:
This toy is disapointing.

First of all, this toy looks very little like the Megatron that was in the movie. It is stubby and stocky and presents none of the lethal intent the movie character does. The vehicle mode only slightly looks like the vehicle from the movie, and the transformation is much harder than it should be considering the results.

In robot mode this toy is hard to pose and unstable when standing. The feet do not support the toy except in a very narrow range of poses. The toys hands are useless and do not even look like hands, they cannot hold any of the other toys weapons or anything else. The "Chain whip" is kind of neat, and a nice nod to the original Transformer's cartoon character, but was not featured in the movie. His hand supposedly combine to form a "Fusion Cannon" but it looks nothing like the movie version. Also, the gun doesn't stay open without holding it open. The arms have a lot of kibble in the form of the "nose" of the plane, which serves no purpose in robot mode. The lights and sound gimmick it only OK. The Scream kind of make sense for this toy, but the yellow lights do not (blue lights for the ice, maybe?). The lights and sound gimmick add weight and bulk to what should be a fairly thin figure.

In Vehicle mode, the legs fold under the wings, making them look blocked up instead of like wings. Also the "tail" of the aircraft doesn't really lock into place and can flop around if touched. If the tail flops it tends to knock the legs free from their pegs on the wings. The wings are meant to unfold automatically, but this never fully worked on my toy. They unfold, but never fully without me having to push them down until the gear locks (there is a visible white gear on the wing hinges). Also the head is completely visible while in vehicle mode. The arms form the front of the plane, but again do not lock together well and come apart easily.

All in all this toy suffers from a lot of the same problems many other movie transformer toys suffer from. The character was designed for the movie first with no thought to how the toy would work, and the toy suffered from it.

reviewText: Here's a game that offers serious strategic play with a simple set of rules, and some nice "wild card" action thrown in for variety. Players start with a row of pegs (called flags) between them. They then take turns placing cards on their side of the flags. They can place any card by any flag, never more than 3 cards at any one flag. All cards are played face up. Players capture a flag by having a combination of 3 cards on their side that beats the opponent's combination on the other side. There are different kinds of combinations -- 3 of a color, assortment of 3 random cards, 3 of a rank, etc. Certain kinds of combinations will always beat other kinds of combinations. Between the same kind of combination, a win is decided by rank or arithmetically. A win means you capture that flag. If a player captures 3 adjacent flags, or any 5 flags, he wins. If you've made it this far, you'll see that the game is rather like Poker with multiple hands and face-up play. Add to the mix Tactics cards. These include leaders like Darius and Alexander which are wild cards -- they can be played as any rank, any color. Other Tactics include Deserter (your opponent loses any card of your choice) or Traitor (you can steal any of your opponent's cards). Gameplay is straightforward. But strategically you need to exercise a lot of foresight. You can't simply drop cards into your formation without thinking about your opponent's (hidden) hand. You also have to take into account the strategic importance of each flag. Remember, capturing 3 adjacent flags means victory. So there are "lines of force" in the game that aren't immediately apparent. The Tactics cards mix up play somewhat, but their effect isn't extreme. They don't radically shift the game, but they can often help to mitigate an awful hand or to add a slight advantage. Highly recommended for card game lovers. Those who enjoy military strategy games will probably enjoy this as well -- the flags certainly create the sense of a strategic front. But players looking for hardcore military action may be disappointed. Really, this is an excellent card game with military trappings. Also check out Glory to Rome. If you like strategic word-game play, you might enjoy THE Book of Word Games: Parlett's Guide to 150 Great and Quick-to-Learn Word Games.

reviewText: This is a really hard review for me because I love Legos and MegaBloks, and it's been years since I was disappointed with a set. But here I am. Let me start by saying that if you're a Trekkie and want a fun little ship to sit on your shelf, desk, or wherever, you can go ahead and click "Buy". There isn't anything deal-breaking in my disappointment if you were otherwise already persuaded to purchase. For everybody else, you're with me. First and foremost, these bricks feel cheap. For years Mega Blocks has been moving toward Lego in quality, and I even helped my girls assemble their Mega Bloks Monster High Draculaura's Birthday Party the other day, which shares *many* pieces with this set, just in purple and green. Whether it's the grey dye they used or a different acrylic batch, these just don't feel up to par - especially the flat-topped pieces. This will be the first Mega Bloks set that I won't be including in our brick bin. Second, this is the first set I've had in years from either brand that was missing pieces. I was missing one of the 4-pip wings (there was an extra 3-pip wing, and I checked everywhere to ensure I hadn't misused something). I suppose when you're dealing with millions of bricks this is inevitable, but still disappointing. And third, but to me most important, this just isn't a particularly well-designed kit. Rather than looking like a purposefully-designed and polished bricked Battle Cruiser, it looks like what a high school Lego club would cobble together from other sets. There are weird overlaps and underlaps, the flat bricks across the display base should be rounded and instead stick jarringly out, and the whole thing just looks a little goofy (see my from-above customer photo). I don't know if Mattel grabbed the license and rushed this to market to cash in on the movie, or if they let the interns design this one, but it's well below the quality of design I expect from them (the CoD UH-60 was so good). So despite how it hurts me to do this, I'm slapping this set with a 3-star rating. Its bricks are too cheap to mix with our block collection and it's too goofy to stand on its own. It'll have its Trekkie fanbase, and for them there are no amount of flaws that will dissuade purchase. For the rest of us, we know Mega Bloks can do better.

reviewText:
My son got this as a gift for his 5th birthday. I was skeptical because it looked like it could be messy and there is a warning on the Lunar Lava that it can stain, so I didn't want to use it on a wooden surface. I decided to let him give it a try on our laminate table in the kitchen.

The toy consists of several components: a "spaceship" which serves as a storage unit for all the other pieces and which can be used as a toy for flying around your completed Martians, a rolling pin, a chunky pair of tweezers, a blunt plastic knife, a cookie-cutter-like circle, three containers of Meteor Mud (playdoh-like substance), three bottles of Lunar Lava (the substance that makes the Martians), and 14 mix-and-match half-molds (7 heads and 7 bottoms).

To make a Martian, you first create a mold by using the spaceship, Meteor Mud and two half-molds. This part is pretty cool because the child can come up with numerous different combinations for a complete mold by combining different heads and bottoms. Once the mold is made, you then fill it with Lunar Lava. The child can use one solid color or mix any or all of the three colors that come with this kit. Then you make a "lid" for the mold using more Meteor Mud, the rolling pin and the circular cookie cutter. You seal the lid on the mold and wait 3-5 minutes for the Lunar Lava to cure.

I gave my son our kitchen timer and showed him how to set it for 5 minutes as we found that 3 minutes was really not long enough for the Lunar Lava to properly set up. Once time is up, you peel off the lid and remove the Martian. It's kind of a slimy substance once it sets up, which is perfect Martian material! Because there are three containers of Meteor Mud, you can continue making new molds and more Martians while the first one cures.

Once the Martian is ready, you remove it from the mold and can use the knife and tweezers to cut off any Lunar Lava that may have spilled over the edge of the mold, or you can dissect the Martian -- "blood" (Lunar Lava on the inside that hasn't completely set up yet) oozes out! You can also put the Martians inside the domes on the spaceship and pretend to fly them around. They will eventually dry out if you don't keep them in the domes or other air-tight container. The Meteor Mud can be used over and over and over again and can be used like traditional playdoh in addition to making molds. The Lunar Lava will run out once you've made a whole lot of Martians. If your child uses this toy as often as mine does, it may be worth getting a couple of refills. I do wish they sold JUST Lunar Lava refills because so far I've only found Lunar Lava/Meteor Mud combo refills and we really don't need more Meteor Mud.

A couple of tips: The Lunar Lava bottles come with attached lids. Cut off the part that attaches the lid to the bottle because it really gets in the way when trying to fill the molds. Also, get a timer ready so you can accurately gauge how long it will take for the Lunar Lava to cure. It really would be nice if the toy came with its own hourglass-like timer but we made do by using our own digital kitchen timer.

This toy helps foster creativity and is great for developing fine motor skills and finger strength. My 7-yr-old daughter has also really enjoyed playing with it and it has actually worked well for both kids to play at the same time because they can each be making their own Martian without getting in each other's way.

There is a little bit of clean-up involved, but no more so than regular playdoh. I've found that if you let the Meteor Mud or Lunar Lava completely dry (even on clothes) it easily crumbles and cleans up much more easily than trying to wipe it up when it's still wet.

All-in-all, I am completely thrilled with this toy! Anything that holds my son's attention for more than ten minutes is a winner in this house and he has spent hours with this one!

reviewText:
This game is positioned oddly. The complexity of the game play makes me agree with the rating of 7+, but the theme and topic are attractive to a much younger audience. While my 5 (almost 6) year old loved seeing the animals, ghost, and electronic chest, my 10 year old found it far too childish (to say nothing of my 14 year old!).

The back story is that you are trying to solve a mystery about who stolen a ring, and there is a time limit; you must solve it before the clock tolls six. There are eight suspects whose pictures are on eight cards. You go from room to room (loosely determined by a roll of the die) and press buttons on a chest to search the room, talk to the animal, feed the animal (who, in return, tells you a clue), attempt magic, or try to open a chest. These need to be done in a specific order and it gets a bit confusing if you perform the same function on the same room multiple times (e.g. you search the room several turns later.) There is a complicated process by which keys and food are accumulated. There is a ghost that adds a randomizing element.

We found many things unclear: how many actions can one take per turn? When do you try magic? How come there are these doors in the game that never need to be opened to win? Can you just accumulate one key? Once used, does it go away or go back in the pile? What is the significance of the cat card?

Even though we didn't know what we were doing, the game seemed to work OK. After feeding an animal, we are told the thief is not short and that this eliminates two of the suspects. (sure enough, the pictures of the eight suspects shows two short ones.) This goes on several times, until the pool of suspects is reduced to one. The thing is, the game tells you too much. A 7+ year old will simply find the challenge of identifying the two short ones (or ones with hats, or ones with long sleeves) simplistic.

So this goes on and on. Periodically the clock sounds, going from noon towards six. Just as we received the last clue and narrowed the field down to one suspect, coincidently(?) it struck six and we were forced to reveal our guess. It seemed a bit contrived that these happened together and I wonder if it is just programmed to be sure you win every round. Add to this the looseness of the rules (you can move a number of rooms, from 0 to the number rolled on the die, each turn in any direction. A single player has a good deal of latitude as to which of the eight rooms to be in any given turn and the group as a whole has even more so.) There is such little strategy involved, it wasn't engaging.

A small thing: The stolen ring is put into the chest which houses the electronics, but it is unclear why. The chest doesn't lock until the mystery is solved, nor does anything happen when you solve the mystery. The ring goes in the box when the game starts, and out of the box when you put the game away. It is a small thing but kind of emphasizes that that whole games seems a bit contrived and random.

In summary, the actions needed to play the game are complex (press which buttons in which order), but the clues and actual mystery are simplistic. The aesthetic is appealing to young children but the complexity excludes them from enjoying the game. Overall it seemed no one enjoyed the game and it is unlikely anyone will ask to play again.
summary: Complicated, narrow age range, unclear instructions

reviewText:
So far my favorite Alex kit is the bug set, but this comes in second.
The pros and cons are below.

PROS
-each kit is individually wrapped with the needed items in it, so you just grab one of the six and you're good to go, no sorting out the different pieces (a big deal if you have an impatient toddler)
-no glue is necessary, all parts are either stickers or use the bendy pipe cleaners to secure items
-creatures are very cute
-fine motor skills not necessary, these are easy enough for 3 year olds and up to manage.
-simple instructions (visual not text) that even my four year old can understand
-cardboard backing is very sturdy
-bright colors and interesting textures

CONS:
-the sticker sheet has rather small stickers to pull off, and they tear easy.  An adult needs to hand the stickers to the kid.
-the stickers aren't repositional, which would be helpful in some cases
-these sets are a bit simpler than Alex's critter/bug set, so they only take about 10 minutes tops per kit.  Possibly great for distracted kids.

All in all, these are a great way to entertain a child without needing scissors or glue-minimal mess!  Beats playdough!

For me personally; I think the bloated, swollen Well Walker was perhaps the best zombie in season 2 of AMC's The Walking Dead (not including Walker Shane; who is still missing from your line, Funko!). He looked just so putrid and disgusting, like he'd really been down in that well for quite some time.  Not only was he a memorable ghoul; but there was also a little black humor built around him; something fairly unusual for the series.  And of course he also had one of the best gross-outs, when, after all the hardwork of hauling him up out of the well; his rotting, bloated body, made heavy and gelatinous in the well water, rips apart; spilling his lower half and most of his blackened guts right back into the well they had been trying to get him out of in the first place.
So naturally, Funko took a memorable walker and transformed him into a memorable POP.  He looks great, from his swollen, narrowed eyes to his grabby little hands to his broad, flat feet.
But, what really makes this guy stand out from most other POPs is his action feature! Just like in the show, this grisly ghoul can be pulled apart (with far less gruesome results, naturally).  It's not every POP that features cool abilities such as this one; so it's nice Funko went the extra mile and delivered a fantastic toy.
So, you have choices and options here. You can display him as whole and solid, torn in half or somewhere in between.  He also looks pretty greatin the box, if you're inclined to keep him in there as I am.
Grab this walker quick and add him to your herd!
