reviewText:
This was my first Kubros figure -- and as a Trekkie (not quite a bonafide Trekker, I must admit), it was the perfect one to delve into.

It is the perfect gift for your favorite Trek fan. Not only is the 8-bit look retro cool, the whole product from start to finish is fantastic. First off, the PACKAGING ROCKS. The box is highly collectible, with one side panel a photo of Leonard Nimoy as Spock, but every step of opening it is a designer's delight. The top opens kind of like a snack box, with a pull-away strip that exposes a tab so you can close the box. Open the flaps and the side flaps are Mega Bloks Spock's eyes/face in glossy print. A delightful detail! The inner flaps and entire inner box is printed with all the various Kubros figures as line art. AND, each plastic bag inside containing the bricks and pieces are all printed with the same art. Love it.

Now, for the figure itself. With 133 pieces, and it standing 5" tops, this is a fairly quick build, with a couple of exceptions. Following the instructions, you build the head first, then the body, then legs and arms/hands. My biggest qualm is building the head, early on in the instructions. There is a point in Step 2 of building the head where the only connection point of two constructed parts is a single 1x1 flat segment. This makes building onto what you have so far very difficult as the connection keeps disconnecting, causing parts to fly. (Pro tip: look for the neck piece and go ahead and snap that in -- it will stabilize as you build.) Other than that, building is easy to follow and quick.

Finished, he looks fantastic. Though the arms are poseable at the shoulders, this construct isn't meant for much play. Pose-and-go is more the thing. Moving the arms too much will make them fall apart. The head can also turn, so you can get the Vulcan sign higher up if you'd like.

Overall, a great collectible Kubros to celebrate Star Trek's 50th anniversary! Very pleased with the entire presentation.

reviewText:
My wife and I bought the Carcassonne big box some time ago. It sat on our shelf awhile because every time I looked at the rules, I thought that there was no way I'd figure them out. I was wrong.

Carcassonne is a beautiful, and simple tile laying game. The components are very nice, and the artwork really appeals to me. Complete maps really look great.

We first started playing the game with the River mini expansion, to set a prescribed start area for the board, and without utilizing farmers. (Farmers are the most difficult to try and score, but they're really not hard to score.)

Since our first play, we've added a few other expansions, and farmers. We love this game!

Game dynamic gets crazy when you start adding more players. Everyone will be competing over everything, and some things you were hoping to complete will become nearly impossible thanks to others playing a crazy tile placement.

All that said, the game never feels mean spirited, and even if you get screwed out of one scoring opportunity, you pretty much always have a chance to score.

We love this game. 5/5

reviewText:
This is a fun and creative craft for girls 9 years old and maybe up as far as early teens (the package says 8 years old to start, but you can judge how "handy" and patient your own eight year old is. I wouldn't do it at an 8 year old's birthday party (although it is a great party idea for anyone in the older range--girls spend time creating something together and then have an original "party favor" to take home). The bracelets are colorful and not too difficult to make, as long as you have a little patience.

There is not a typical "instruction sheet" but instead a fashion booklet/magazine with a number of different articles and young fashion tips. In this booklet (beginning on page 12) you will find the instructions for this craft. Everything else--the yarn plus 7 hard 1/2" width bracelets and 13 soft, thin rubber ones (like people used to wear as reminder bracelets) is altogether in one bag. From a parent's point of view, I found it easy to "master" and demonstrate the craft, particularly after looking it over first and watching the video. There was minimal frustration as long as the girls realized it wasn't going to be "fast". Very motivational. The kit has supplies for 20 bracelets, but 13 are thin rubber ones so you might prefer to plan on 7 hard plastic bracelets and let each girl have one or two of the rubber ones. It has the makings of a good "party craft", like a sleepover activity and something good to take home.

Girls often would like to make jewelry but craft stores can be overwhelming (even at my age). Having everything all in one kit--and so many possible designs--is so convenient and makes everything easier.  I gave it 5 stars because I love the idea that a girl could make these bracelets at home, be introduced to the fun and creativity of jewelry design, and do it together with a friend, a group (small or large) or even a sibling or parent. The website has a video demonstration (again, good for a party) and some more design ideas as well.

reviewText:
This game is best for 3 to 4 year olds. It would help if an adult or a patient older sibling can help facilitate the gameplay. There are variations, but it's basically a way to practice taking turns while getting familiarized with colors and shapes. The bugaboos of the game are that the dice have a joker which allows you to pick any piece, and the white on the colored die means you have to skip your turn - it's important to learn skipping turns too.

It is fun to see a child react delightfully after getting the pieces, but kids 5 and up would be bored. Also, there are 40 pieces to pick up. That's at least 40 rolls total, so it can get long. Due to the simplicity of the game, maybe the gameboard should have contained smaller number of pieces to match a younger child's attention span.

The board itself is made of cardboard like those jigsaw puzzles contained within a cardboard frame and backing. I can see the board getting beaten up if not cared for. The game can be played by one like solitaire, but that's 40 dice roll for one child and can be a tough task to complete.

For at least 2 preschoolers, this is a fun game. I recommend minimal supervision, or you can join in the gameplay if you want.
summary: Best for preschoolers learning shapes, colors and taking turns.

reviewText:
As the other reviewers noted, this is a sturdy set. I purchased it a while back for my baby, who shall be two in late December. This isn't her favorite set (Winnie the Pooh still holds that record), but she does enjoy the animals, and she absolutely adores the car (definitely the favorite item in the set). She's still not much of a builder, but when I (or my husband) take the initiative and start taking out pieces to build things, she quickly toddles over to imitate to the best of her abilities. She sometimes has difficulties assembling the legos, but at her age, it is to be expected. Still, the bright colors of the legos (and enthusiasm from the family) keep her trying until she succeeds at "connecting" one-three pieces. She's not building zoos, at present, but considering that these Duplos are significantly smaller than the Megablox set that she has become quite proficient with, I'm pleased that she's getting challenged. An added bonus is that her big sister (7), who was NEVER into building toys, has finally determined that building with legos can be just as fun as playing barbies, doing science experiments, or reading, etc. Now she, too, plays with legos (but those aimed at bigger kids).

Like the other Duplo sets that I have purchased, this is of exceptional durable quality (quality that far exceeds what I have seen/experienced from the Megablox, but that is subjective), and can be easily washed in the top rack of the dishwasher, should it be necessary to clean them. As for the toy's educational value, my little one is learning the names of and sounds that a few animals make (while giggling hysterically), and she's doing basic construction (though she prefers to take apart what others in the family have assembled). She likes to wander off with the animals, so they wind up near her animal puzzles, allowing her to see/notice differences between two dimensional and three dimensional objects, and the Duplo zoo animals are sometimes used by her when she's playing with her blocks, which leads me to think of the figurines and the car in this set as not limited to the world of legos--they are being mixed by her own associations/whims with her other toys. Again though, the winning piece of this set is the car: it gets the most use by far, and she attempts to place her characters from some of the other Duplo sets inside. This (since the seat of the car has lego grooves, and the figurines have their own attachments) allow her to work at fairly intricate fine motor skills. It's easy enough for me to lock a figurine into a car, but for her it takes time and effort, which just goes to show how fascinating the car and its workings are for her. For a little one, and they do tend to be easily distracted, this one object/skill activity really retains her attention: possibly she relates to the car because it is part of her real life, but who knows.

I would certainly buy this set for another child, but I would choose it for a child ABOVE age two, just as the box recommends rather than for one who is 18-20 months old. Still, a great buy with loads of play value: I believe my little one will find this zoo increasingly interesting as her imagination and motor skill abilities flourish. So, I am pleased!
summary: Great Basic Zoo with loads of play potential

reviewText:
I have good news for parents. Hasbro's Rescue Optimus Prime Fire Station proves that someone at the toy company has been listening to the complaints of parents and grandparents. Yes, I'm talking about the packaging. While it appears to be the same old packaging that takes an adult half an hour to tear apart, this packaging differs significantly. The inner box slides easily out of the display packaging after cutting the tape on both end flaps. The inner box holds each piece securely with twine - not the expected plastic coated wire. After less than fifteen minutes, I had all the pieces out of the packaging and only two large flat pieces of cardboard, twine and one small piece of plastic to dispose of. That's a gift to parents!

Sometimes the display packaging can set a child's expectations too high and the toys are disappointing. I would give Hasbro a B+ on this product. It does NOT contain any of the full-size transformer rescue bots shown on the packaging. The display packaging also shows action figures from its other construction, rescue, and police bots sets. However, the inset drawings on the back of the box clearly indicate the pieces included with the fire station.

The durability of a toy depends - as all parents know - as much on the child as on the construction of the toy. Nevertheless, the fire station and other pieces are built to withstand rugged play. The station is made of heavy plastic and assembled with recessed metal screws. The fire station transforms from the station mode to the bot mode with the turn of a dial on the center front panel. The elevator section and the training section swivel around the back of the central panel to form a compact cube for storing.

The fire truck/rescue bot is mostly molded plastic. Only the ladder and the wheels on the fire truck are attached. The fire truck "transforms" into a rescue bot by standing it up on the back bumper. The fireman action figure fits easily into the fire truck. Its shoulders swivel and head turns. The figure can stand or sit. The third accompanying piece is the water cannon. The cannon "shoots" a piece of blue plastic shaped like water from the barrel. The water cannon is the piece most likely to break first. The bottom of the cannon has a plastic rod extending from it. The rod allows it to be mounted in several places - the front or rear of the fire truck, on top of center panel of the fire station and on top of the training section.

The electronic part of the fire station enhances rather than overwhelms it. When the red knob on the center front panel is turned, that section "transforms" between fire station and bot modes while one of twelve phrases speaks from the control center. Flashing lights and siren sounds accompany only a few of these phrases.

This set comes with a book introducing Heatwave, the rescue bot and Cody the newest fireman. The story is age appropriate for 3-to-6 year-olds. The art work enhances the plot without making the adventure too scary for the youngest reader. (I wish they had included Sparkplug, the fire station dog who plays a large part in the story,  in the play set.)

Two design elements amused me. The on/off switch is the middle slide switch inside the command center. The battery compartment hides under the map panel in the command center. Access it by removing the screw above the map.

In my opinion, the Rescue Optimus Prime Fire Station has every possibility of being a popular toy with all the 3-to-6 year-old boys for the coming holiday seasons.

reviewText:
I got this toy for my grandson, age 7, and he and his sister, age 9, took to it immediately.  They enjoyed the challenge of working the parts into their various configurations but wound up asking for adult help when they couldn't figure it out, that is all the way to the semi-truck mode, or others.

The toy comes with a sort of space vehicle that makes fun sounds when a button is depressed.  This is separate from the main figure, which is plenty complicated in and of itself. All in all, a rather engineering miracle, almost!

Plenty of possible modes to discover, manipulate the pieces into, and play with. So far it has worked flawlessly and seems durable.  They had it several weeks now.

My grandson has been known to sleep with his next to him.

High recommendation.

I think that this is a good toy for the money.  You can find them for very decent prices, especially around the holidays.  I think that it is best for a mobile child who can crawl or walk because then they have fun chasing down the balls that shoot out - sometimes the ball stay on they toy and cycle back through the chute, but sometimes they pop out and off of the toy.  If your child isn't mobile, mom and dad will be chasing down the balls.  My son enjoyed this toy the most between 12 and 18 months because that is when he learned to push the plunger down himself and would do it over and over again.  My son loved that he could make it work all on his own.  He also loved to grab the balls when they popped up, and put them back down through the chute.

It is a little bit loud, but we put painter's tape over the speaker and over a portion of the motor/fan opening and that seemed to help some.  However, it still probably won't be something that you want your child to play with while your watching your favorite show.

And yes, as others have said, your child will put everything he/she can find down the chute.  That's what kids do, though.  They learn by seeing what will fit where, and I am sure that this toy is not the only one that falls prey to such curiosity.  For the most part, I can just tip the toy over and whatever was put in slides right out.

This is a nice little set of metal tank models.  But there are some quirks and annoyances.

The Chi-Ha and Tiger are well designed and come out great.  The T-34 however, has crappy inner wheel covers which rotate freely when assembled.  A drop of super glue on each will do the trick, but come on.  I shouldn't have to do that.  Also, the model looks cool, but it doesn't look like a T34.  I mean, it really doesn't look like one.  It comes out kind of angular looking like a German tank destroyer, or something much more modern with a low turret.

The Sharman has issues too.  The main body and wheels hit it on the dot.  Nice job.  The turret, however, is just Sherman- like.  I did figure out that if you bend the bottom tab outwards on the main gun mount, it'll sit more downwards vs. the instructions and photo which make it look like an artillery piece.  But still.. the turret is a miss.

Also, these are NOT in scale to each other.  The Sherman dwarfs all the other tanks, and the Chi-Ha would be a monster, not the little jungle tank that it is.

In order of difficulty (Hardest :1):
1.  Chi-Ha 2. Sherman (rounded angles on front of body are a pain) 3. Tiger  4. T34

In order of quality/final appearance:
1. Chi-Ha  2. Tiger  3. Sherman  4. T34

Jump forward about 40 years and today Microchargers have embraced that same idea but with really small race cars that race a round a track at lightning speed.  The cars are only slightly larger than a peanut M&M, they fully charge in about 8 seconds and they race around that track at an amazing speed.

This set includes a pit stop that you use to recharge the cars as needed and enough track to build a decent sized oval race track.  There are other Microchargers sets that can be used as add-ons. The one downside is that this kit only contains one car, so you will want to buy one or more additional cars to have an interesting race. reviewText:
Confession time: I'm 37 and I have no children. I chose this Iron Man toy for me! I wanted a cool looking Iron Man Mark 42 from the film  to put in my DVD cabinet (after playing with it for a while, of course) and this popped up.  I was torn over what rating to give, 3 stars or 4.

Pros: I expect a young children under 8 would love this. He has several different voice messages, which include sound effects, that play when his chest button is pressed. Phrases such as "Systems critical; Rebooting systems now; Scanning for possible threats," etc. His eyes also light up when the messages play. A separate button to fire the missiles is on the back of the figure, but these can also be fired manually by rotating the canon on the arm. It has a range of about 3 feet.  The figure looks impressive and considering it is not a collectible, it's very accurate to the film (except for the canon), with bold coloring.  It's also big - once the bottom of the legs are attached, he's 15 inches high.  The figure also has good balance. When you put the legs in the correct position, he will stand without being held.

Cons: However, considering the price, I am very disappointed that the figure has almost no articulation. The arms do not bend at the elbows or wrists, and the legs do not bend at the knee. Even the joints at the hip only go a few degrees.  He won't "sit."  The head does turn a bit from left to right, but that is all.  The figure is very much like one of the original Star Wars figures - completely straight limbs that have limited rotation.  Further, this is not frustration free packaging, and the lack of batteries mean he won't work right out of the box. Adults should consider this before gifting this to a child.

Overall, this is a nice toy and I would recommend it for little Iron Man fans (be they boys or girls). I'm just disappointed that the price of toys continues to rise and the value for the price does not. I don't think this is worth $35, but it is comparable to similar toys and in that light is worth the purchase.
summary: It should do more at this price point

reviewText:
To start off, I truly believe Sylvion is a better game than Onirim (Haven't played Urbion nor Castellion, so I won't comment on those games) which is also a very good game.
But I am a person with limited time and I tend to appreciate shorter games that takes less time to setup, shuffle, put the cards back into the box, however, Sylvion is a game that takes about 30 minutes (40~60 minutes if played with all the expansions, which are already included in the game) to play, and not just that, Sylvion is also a game that takes up a lot of space to play too.  So if the above characteristics of the game Sylvion concerns you, then Onirim might be a better fit for you, but overall game play/design quality ALONE, Sylvion clearly is the better (but not by a whole lot) game in my opinion and experience.  So yeah, you should definitely check this game out if you are into single player games, IF you don't mind the amount of time it takes to play considering it's a filler game.

*Edit* 11/16/17
I am slightly lowering the review from 5 to 4.5 stars because of the first expansion (the second expansion is a great addition to the main game, and I don't have any complains against it), because the last 4 "Extraordinary Feats" cards out of 8 from the first expansion are just plain useless.  When you do end up drafting these cards, instead of expanding options, they only unnecessarily over-complicates the game, and the problem is because the main game forces you to stay alive and prepare to defend the next wave of elemental attacks, but these 'alternative victory condition' cards will give you like another completely different objective to fulfill on top of all the tension going on, which can be interesting in theory (and in few very rare cases, are), but for the most of time these cards are just plain useless. Of course, you could just take away all (or just the 4 'alternative victory condition' cards, plus additional 4 betrayal cards, for total of 8 cards out of 16 cards from the first expansion) the cards from the first expansion, the game still remains a brilliant game, but it is a bit disappointing that Sylvion could have been a more complete game, if all the cards in the box could have been able to utilized equally.

reviewText:
I told my wife this was a toy for my son, but who am I kidding.  This was for me.  My son is 3 1/2, he'll have no idea what to do with this for at least a couple of years.

So, do you remember the little black plastic labyrinth game with one knob on the right-hand side of the box and one in the front, and you'd try to get that shiny silver ball bearing through the maze without falling into one of the many numbered holes?  I still have mine.  I loved that game, and at 44, I still haven't managed to get it all the way through, although I've been close many times.

Well, this game is meant to be a third-dimensional version of that one.  You start by putting the little ball bearing in one of three slots, and then you rotate the ball in order to keep it on the track.  It is a challenge, and definitely in the spirit of those old-time labyrinth games.  If you can think of that famous drawing by MC Eischer; with the stairs and ledges that nonsensically go this way and that, and people walking them are upside-down while others are sideways, then you can understand the concept of this game and how to maneuver the ball bearing through the plexiglass orb.

A couple of things about the game; the numbers on the tracks are very, very hard to see.  If they had used a different color paint on the raised/recessed surfaces of the numbers, that alone would have been worth a half a star in my rating.  The other thing is (and this might actually add to the challenge) is there's so much stuff in the orb that sometimes it's easy to lose track of the ball bearing and where to go next.  If you move but a bit to see where you need to go, you might just fall off the track.

For around $15, this is an interesting test of skill and an interesting new look on the old labyrinth.  I don't think it's for kids, even six or seven, but more like nine to adult.  It's a lot of fun and I recommend it.

We're really impressed with the color and detail put into these. Sure, they're only dice but... the colors are very True to what they should be - the brown is very distinguishable from black and the purple doesn't look blue. The white on the dots is very brilliant; no problems figuring out what side is facing up even from across a long table. Also, each die has faceted corners, which means they roll a lot better than the straight edge dice.

Every single die is polished and smooth. We couldn't find any discolorations or defects.

We're very happy with this kit. A ton of dice in all different colors. Now everyone who plays gets to use their own set. And we got a nice drawstring bag to hold them when not in use.

reviewText:
Everything I love about Star Wars Lego is expressed in this one small, yet action packed set. Where should I start.

First off, the build it's self has an intricate, semi-complex feel that keeps you involved from beginning to end. I posted my dislike before of "quick builds" in my A-wing review, but the Desert Skiff is one that's fun to watch shape up.  As always, the detail in the set is perfect, and for such a small set they managed to cram in a ton of moving parts and action features. You get a movable plank, adjustable "wing" panels on the back, control levers, and just when you thought they covered it all, Lego goes the extra step and includes things not seen in the movie, like a weapons locker in the middle of the skiff and a missile on the side. Like I said before, it's details like these that make me really love Lego. I should also mention the ship is very sturdy too when built, so kids can really play with it with out worrying about it falling to pieces.

And of course how about those mini-figs? You get a great ratio of good guys to bad guys in this set, so you can really stage out some battles. A few details are off here, and just about my only complaint at all. Luke doesn't have his black gloved hand (at least he didn't in the set I got). The Death Star came with a black gloved Luke, so why is so hard to get one with the skiff. Also, as at least one other reviewer noted. Lando has no hair once you remove his guard disguise. If you want Lando to help Luke fight Boba Fett, he has to be Baldo. Oh well.

And finally, the big surprise of the set, and the frosting on the cake as far as I'm concerned, they actually managed to include the Sarlac Pit Monster in with the set, not a creature I normally think they would pull off, or even think of including, since it's basically a hole in the ground, but they did it. It's based on the ROTJ special edition monster, and looks a little too much like Audrey Two from Little Shop of Horrors, but it does look good. The instruction booklet even encourages kids to place Boba Fett inside it's mouth, which is just another fun Lego detail.

Overall, this would be a great set for the kid (or adult) who can't really afford the bigger sets, but still wants a fun to build set with nearly unlimited playability. You can't go wrong with this one.

reviewText:
Mg zaku ii 2.0 is a top example of what makes master grades so great.  This is the 20th master grade kit I've assembled and it is equal to or better than many of the kits in my display in terms of quality, design and joy of the build.

Putting zaku ii together was a fun experience.  It took about 15 hours to complete, including applying the included set of decals.  All parts fit together very well and nothing is loose when it's finished.  The model also has great balance and is very sturdy in its construction.  Movement in all the joints is smooth and there is a good range of motion at every point.  The colours look appealing out of the box and it comes with a decent amount of accessories, including a machine gun, an axe and a bazooka that can be built in 2 different ways.  Zaku ii also has simple but nice gimmicks, like moving pistons on the inner frame, a cockpit that shifts to either side in the torso and a mono-eye that moves on a separate axis than the head.

This is a great model kit in general and has everything a great model should.  I didn't get one sooner in hopes that a 3.0 version would be released to go along with my RX 78-2 3.0. Then I realized that maybe there was no need for a zaku ii 3.0 because the 2.0 version is pretty much flawless.

How awesome is a game where you literally try to squash your opponents? Well their pieces anywayyou don't actually squash people. My whole family gets a kick out of this game. Roll a die, move that many spaces and try to flip the cube shaped board so that the other players pawns get Squashed and you are the last one standing. Fun right?!

We actually ALL played this game together with only slight adjustments for my Diva. She is only 3 and a half right now but LOVES games and just HAD to play with us. She liked the part where she got to squash people LOL. I mean that was a really really fun part of the game.

The best part about Squashed, besides the squashing, is that the board is 3 dimensional and you can move it as you play. Thats right, you can move the board around while you decide which pawn you want to move, or who you want to squash next.

Also, the board is its own box! All you need to do is store the cube and you have the whole game inside it. There is a side on the cube with hinges that open up to store the pawns, the die, the Squash Pad and the rules inside. Convenient! I have said it beforeI love games that are easy to store, travel well and are durable as well as fun of course. Squashed actually meets ALL four items on my list!

reviewText:
There's a lot to be said for good, simply, children's toys, and that's exactly what the ALEX Junior Porcupine Pound and Play is.  My wife and I tend to favor simpler toys in the first place, so picking up this little porcupine was a no brainer.  Neither of us have any experience with the ALEX line of products, so, as a first time, we were a little hesitant.

Happily, the porcupine is a great little toy.  The colors painted on the wood are more lovely in person than they appear in any pictures: they're bright, vibrant, and, for lack of a better term, happy.  The wood is really smooth and well sanded, and I don't predict we'll have any problems with splintering.

My only (very small) complaint is that the screws that hold the two pieces of Mr. Porcupine together aren't covered up.  Now, they are recessed so it's not something our daughter could really get into, but I'd have really like to see them puttied and painted over.  It's a small complaint, and wouldn't prevent me from picking up this toy again.

Overall, we are really happy with the Alex Jr Porcupine Pounder.  It's a nice, durable toy that is visually appealing and is priced well.  We'll definitely be looking for more Alex Jr products in the future.

reviewText:
Like some other folks, it took me a bit of effort to connect my Sumo to my iphone (software update, a few reboots, etc), but once I got it set up it really ran just smooth as silk.

 When it comes to toys, I judge on three metrics: playability (how long until my kids forget they own it), durability, and price.  In terms of playability, this thing is still going strong.  Especially when my kids have friends over, this continues to be a go to favorite.  They love chasing around the dog, "spying" on each other, and making Sumo jump every which way.  Indeed, my only playability complaint is that the battery life -- about 15 to 20 minutes -- can put a real damper on the fun.  An exchangeable second battery would have gone a long way to getting this toy its fifth star.

 As far as I can tell, durability here is excellent.  My kids' Sumo has fallen off the deck, flown down the stairs, and been pawed at by a large dog, and it just comes back for more.  Parrot produces flying drones and they bring the durability required for that toy to this wheeled item.  It is certainly a big plus.

As for price, this is obviously an expensive toy, but well worth the money.  It is well made and I imagine something this complex must be expensive to design (especially given its excellent durability) and it can't be cheap to produce.  Whether it is worth it to a given purchaser is obviously up to the person putting down the cash, but I'd call it an all around good value for what you get.

Lots of fun and full of creative potential, this is a toy I expect my kids will be enjoying for quite some time.
summary: Great Fun, wish it had longer battery life

reviewText:
We had vacationed at a resort in San Diego, and they had a giant swan float there that the kids had a blast on.  Kids were jumping on it multiple times over the three days we were there, so we knew it was durable.  So when we saw this by the same company, and in a unicorn shape (my daughter's fave), we were so excited.  This rainbow unicorn float has not disappointed!

We went to Vail Lake resort camping grounds, which features two very large pools.  It was 93 degrees over the weekend, so this was the perfect time to try this out.  We have a blower with nozzles that we use for our camping mattresses, and it was very easy to blow this up.  I did the base first, which took about a minute.  Then I did the head, small seat poof, tail, and each wing.  I was at first concerned about the wings, so I underinflated them.  I need not have been concerned, even with the kids tugging on them, they were fine.  Even more remarkable, at one point, we turned around and when we looked back, my daughter was out of the pool, pulling my son to the other side of the pool by the unicorn horn.  And that was also no problem!.

Quality
This is high quality, thick nylon.  It's heavy, but not a burden to carry.  It feels so durable.  The construction of this is smooth all over, no rough or irritating edges.  It feels like we'll have this a long time, unlike every other pool float we've ever had.

Fun
Oh...my...gosh...this thing was so much fun for my kids and EVERYONE around the pool was eyeing it admiringly.  My kids let other kids go on with them and made some new friends.  It is every kid's dream.  It's beautiful in the water and lets you have fun many different ways.  My daughter loved putting her legs around the head most, my son liked slipping down the back so the tail was between his legs to hold him up while he kicked his legs in back to move them along.

We did keep them supervised as there was so much activity around the float.  This is a pool party fun maker.

My husband eventually sent the kids to dry off and he lounged on the float with his head against the unicorn neck.  It's wonderful.

Deflating was fairly easy, we just took the detachable nozzles from the pump and stuck them in to open the valves.  The large parts deflated super fast and the smaller ones did so with the kids sitting on them laughing.

reviewText:
I was so excited when I first saw this toy.  It looked like it came with quite a few of Manny's Tools and my son could actually take things apart and 'fix' them.  There are 9 different fixing activities: toaster, clock, camera, fan, radiator, engine, air filter, battery, and spark plug.  Most of the parts come completely off of the truck (not the engine or the spark plug).  Manny makes suggestions on what to fix, your child may receive a phone call from a client stating that their item is not working properly, or your child can choose.  The truck hood opens to fix the engine parts and the bed of the truck converts into Manny's Repair Shop.  This set comes with: Rusty (pipe wrench), Felipe (phillips head screwdriver), Squeeze (pliers), Dusty (saw), and a vise.  Once a project is completed, Manny congratulates the child on his/her accomplishment.

Here are the problems that I have discovered:  1. The wrench (Rusty) does not work very well.  You cannot move him in a circular motion given the tight spaces of the screws.  You need to constantly take him off and re-adjust.  Therefore, my son opts to use the pliers (Squeeze), but he is not coordinated enough at this age to do so. He becomes frustrated and wants me to fix the item.  2. The saw (Dusty) has no real purpose and is not interactive.  A piece of wood sits in the vice and you may freely saw the wood. No instruction is given and it doesn't really fit in with the rest of the toy. 3. Occasionally, Manny states (as he does in his show) to measure it twice and cut it once. However, this toy does not come with a tape measure. Not really sure what we are supposed to measure. It is just a random statement.  4. Where is Manny? There is a front seat that is large enough to store all the parts and still have room for a Manny doll. 5. The roof of the truck cab removes too easily.  My son tries to push the truck or lift it by the roof and it pops off. I am constantly having to put it back together.

Overall, my son (and husband) like this toy. We do not watch the show, but it is a unique toy for children who like to try and fix things on their own. reviewText:
The witch Grimelda has enchanted and changed five characters that live within an ever-shifting labyrinth. She has also trapped the magical wizard inside a book. There are two ways to play--a challenging game and a basic game--based on two sets of three specific labyrinth pieces that can be put on the board. At the beginning of each turn, a player takes one of the cardboard tiles/pieces of the labyrinth, and repositions it by sliding it in a different row than it was removed from. (Stationary pieces affixed to the board make sliding the other pieces easier.) The player then has the choice between moving along the labyrinth to any point s/he can reach, or staying put. Once you get to a character, they'll give you a task to take on--picking up an item they want, or delivering a treasure chest to another enchanted character. The reward for completing a task is typically gems, and possibly a free turn. Other ways to win coins include landing on one on the board and getting to the opposite space you started from. In the meantime, Grimelda may try to thwart you.

Although most of the playing pieces are cardboard, the "marker" playing pieces and translucent plastic gems and are a cut above the playing pieces of some board games. Nevertheless, older players may find the electronic version of Labyrinth a bit childish, due to the magical book that replaces the cards. The voices used and slow pace in which the characters speak can become a bit wearisome, but they can be interrupted if the information is already known (such as the opening introduction). I'm mostly impressed by the "magical" book because it repeats what items are being looked for if the players take too long at completing tasks. It can be easy to forget, and these reminders are helpful. However, perhaps the "book" could have been improved just slightly by it being hinged and the cover truly opening, revealing a wizard--even just a flat image--inside. This would add authenticity to the premise that he's locked within the book, and make the game a bit more fun for younger players who win and receive the prize of freeing him.

Labyrinth has a little bit of a learning curve since it's mostly graphically based, but once learned, it's easy to follow the steps of the game. And while Ravensburger says it's for two to four players, it is also easy to adapt into a one-person game as a means of developing one's strategy. This isn't quite as hard, since no one is battling against you to rearrange the maze. But it's like playing against Grimelda, and will help polish memorization skills.

reviewText:
We are big Stefan Feld fans (he's the designer of this game, and many other amazing games, just in case you didn't know). My husband and I have played this a handful of times after only having it for about 2 weeks. It's our new favorite (with loads of other games closely following). My husband is the more "nerdy" one and got me in to these Euro boardgames a few months ago. I now adore them as well...even though I am no where near as "nerdy" (lol). They are really fun! You just have to get past the learning stage which can be kind of intense.

I'll try and make this review short and concise for the less nerdy but also detailed enough that those familiar with these games can also find it useful! I really want people to give this game a try because it's really neat!!

Amerigo is a masterpiece. The board in itself is genius and allows for endless combinations (which means every game you play is almost guaranteed to be different). You have little squares (probably about 5x5) that you place together to make little islands. The point of the game is to sail around, discover islands, build on those islands, and collect victory points along the way. As with all Stefan Feld games, you have loads of options to obtain victory points.

The board and components are beautiful! You get little wooden sailboats to sail with. And, the best part, the resource generating tower. I don't know if I can fully explain this to people who don't know anything about the game but, it's really cool. You get a tower (like a wide plastic funnel on top leading down a cardboard base with a slide like bottom where the little bits slide out onto a platform) which determines which actions, and how many, you can use each turn. You use the tower after each turn and at the start of a new round. There are no dice. Still, this game has a little bit of luck due to the tower.

Just in case it's helpful....a "few" of the other games we have loved playing (mostly 2 player) are Bora Bora, Castles of Burgundy, Trajan, Rialto, London, Thurn and Taxis, Village, Seasons, Keyflower, Tzolk'in, Legacy, Smallworld, Dominion, Eminent Domain, Euphoria, Suburbia, Le Havre and Lords of Waterdeep).

NOTE: If you DO purchase, and you should, please make sure the tower is in tact correctly so it works the correct way!! We had to ensure our slide was pushed all the way back to allow the bits to fall down. (If you get the game, you'll know what I mean)

At his age (just under three years old), his fine motor skills are improving all the time. reviewText:
Fuse is a fast-paced, cooperative dice game. The players of the game have 10 minutes to diffuse a number of bombs based on the number of players, and the difficulty level. Because of the varying difficulty levels, this game has great replay-ability. I love this game because of how challenging it is. There is a lot of growth to the game. Fuse also come with an timer app which can be downloaded. The app has two different settings. The first is just a normal count-down timer and the second has a count-down timer with a sassy AI voice.

The game plays quickly. The app counts down while players pass a bag full of dice around to complete puzzles. The two puzzles (bombs) in front of them are the only ones that player gets to focus on. When it is a players turn, the player will pull the number of players out of a dice bag. If there are 4 players, then the current player will pull four dice out of a bag. Everyone will use 1 die from the dice that are pulled out and allocate it to a puzzle in front of them. Once a puzzle is completed, the player will discard it and draw another from a row of puzzle cards in the center. Once all the bombs have been diffused out of the deck before time timer goes off the group wins. If they do not complete all the bombs the ship blows up with everyone in it!

I love the fast play and the underlying hurry there is to the game. This is a game that I highly suggest. It is easy to play and teach. I also like it cause it teaches communication and cooperative play.
summary: Fast-paced, dice game that is so much fun!

reviewText:
Quick to grasp and easy to play.  Those are things you look for in a game.  However, this one also provides just the right amount of luck and the right amount of strategy.  There are those who will love this- and then a large group of people who will hate it too.

The idea is to control the most islands via land bridges, card draws, and strategic moves.  There is the element of strategy with where you place your pieces.  There is the element of luck with the cards that allow you to move.  Sometimes you'll be able to do things...other times, not so much.  So its strategically random, or randomly strategic.  The rules are easy to understand and don't require a lot of referencing back and forth.  The game play is fast, the cards and placement of tokens/bridges is intuitive and the game proceeds at a very quick pace broken into 3 rounds.  Total play time for use was under 30 mins. once we got the hang of it.

Frustration aside, I liked the game and it goes into rotation on those "quick game" nights where I don't want to fuss with a lot of setup or a lot of rules.  Be warned- this is a two player game and there isn't an option to expand or add for more players.  Keeping that in mind, it is a small package, fits nicely into a suitcase or backpack, and the components are of good quality (cards, pieces, board).

We loved it and plan to keep playing it.

reviewText:
Netossa.  She's an ally of She-Ra and she tosses nets.  Got it?  Netossa was the January 2013 figure in Mattel's Masters of the Universe Classics line and added another character to the ranks of the Great Rebellion from She-Ra: Princess of Power.  Based on the character's appearance in the Filmation cartoon more so than the original toy, Netossa is a very striking figure.  She has a beautiful color scheme and an excellent sculpt. Unfortunately, Netossa is very short packed on accessories and contains no offensive weaponry other than her cape which doubles as her net.  Here's a brief look at Netossa:

The Facts:
 Articulation: hinged ankles w/ rocking ankles, hinged knees, swivel thighs, ball jointed hips, swivel waist, ball jointed shoulders, swivel biceps, hinged elbows, swivel wrists, ball jointed head.
  Accessories: Shield, combination net/cape.

The positives:

*Netossa's color scheme is really nice.  She's predominately clothed in dark and light blues with just a touch of silver and white here and there.  Her skin is a beautiful, dark brown which looks quite lovely when pared with the cooler tones of her outfit.  While she has some similarities in color to Frosta, when you put them side by side they look just fine.

*Her costume also has some nice detail.  Her bracers and top have some nice design work on them and while I dislike the net cape as a net, I love it as a cape. It looks great and is quite sturdy.  Little details like her metallic blue fingernails also will catch your eye.

*Netossa has a gorgeous head sculpt. Her hair is very thick and nicely styled and looks very exotic when paired with her very stern yet beautiful face.

The negatives:

*The biggest issue is that Netossa just doesn't have enough accessories. First she comes with her shield. It's silver and white with a dark blue jewel. It's a nice piece on its own, but its the same shield that came with both versions of She-Ra and Frosta.  Not really a unique accessory. Her main "accessory" is supposed to be her net-cape.  While this functions fantastic as a cape,: #1. It really makes a very poor accessory as it's shaped like a cape and #2 Never before in the MOTUC line has someone's cape or armor counted as an accessory. It's a shame that Mattel couldn't come up with something cool and unique for Netossa. Even a repainted sword from Bubble Power She-Ra would have been better than no weapon.

Overall:  While Netossa was not a figure I was eagerly clamoring for, I really like how she turned out. Unfortunately, it feels like she was the victim of some cost cutting on Mattel's part. I've fixed this by giving my Netossa the really cool silver trident that came with the DC Universe Classics Black Manta figure.  This makes me so much happier with the figure, even though Mattel should have provided her with something unique of her own.  It is nice to add more numbers to the growing Great Rebellion, though.
summary: A beautiful figure that could use another accessory

My 10 year old is in love with archery.  She has a "real" youth bow, but she is only allowed to practice it outside for safety reasons.  For fun, I decided to get this Nerf set for her, because she can play with it inside (safely, of course.)

This bow is very easy to play with and use.  She loves the colors!  It's not quite the same as using a regular bow with arrows, and the accuracy is rather low.  However, this is a toy, not a serious tool, so it's more important for it to be fun, durable, and safe.  Which it is.  The darts do not have any significant power behind them, so I'm not concerned about my windows or television when she's playing around with this toy.

The foam darts are long lasting if cared for.  I like the holder on the bow for keeping the darts together, so they're not floating around her room with no place to belong.  The bow itself is a little awkward to find a place to store, but we have some hooks in my daughter's room for totes and such, which she also hangs her archery things on.

If your girls likes archery, she'll have fun with this toy.

reviewText:
A great nicely detailed little die cast of a version of the Ghostbusters Ecto1 that nobody ever expected to see. The animated cartoon one. Overall HotWheels did a great job. The die cast body is distinctly different from the movie E1 and 1A. The more hot rod mag wheels and more aggressive nose down angling give it its own distinct styling.

The only flaws with it are in some missing paint details and the roof equipment. The roof gear is by design more simplified and geometric for this design. It's animation. Somebody has to draw it every time for every frame of film. So they pare down in-needed details. This is fine. The roof gear on this car is well shaped and even has some crisp painted details. The flaw is in the unwanted parts. While the simplified gear is fine, the swirly and translucent silver plastic they cast the piece in is not. The color and consistency of the plastic used for this part is so out of place and so bad that it somewhat takes away from the car as a whole.

The other flaw is the lack of license plate printing. It's such an iconic element of the car. And all other versions have it. Such that its absence is noticeable here.
summary: A great but not quite perfect Ecto 1

reviewText:
I never write reviews but after readin the reviews for this train table, I feel it is getting a bad name.  I bought this for my son's 2nd birthday and he absolutely loves it.  It took us about 3 hours to put the whole thing together, includig the tracks, which we have never done before.  We had bought a few Thomas trains for it, but honeslty, you don't need to buy anything.  It came with several trains and cars for the road.  My son plays with this everyday.  There are so many little pieces for the table, that it gets a little overwhelming for him, so we put most of them in the drawer below.  I know that he will use them more as he gets older.  Speaking of the drawer, it is HUGE!  There is so much space to store other small toys.
Most of the complaints are about not having a lip.  but, these people are also using it as a coffee table.  Who has a lip on a coffee table?  you can't have it both ways.  No, there is no lip, but my 2 year old has yet to drop ot throw the tracks on the floor.  We have told him since the beginning that he has to play gentle and he has.  He does take the train pieces apart here and there but has learned to put them back on, so it's a game for him.  He really only takes one piece apart at a time.
Another compaint people have is that it scuffs easily.  I have to disagree with them.  As I said, it gets played with everyday and doesn't have a single mark on it.  But, when it does get marked up, I am not going to complain because it is a kids toy.  People are using it as a coffee table and then complaining it gets marks.  If you buy a regular wooden coffee table, I can almost guarantee it won't stay in perfeect condition.  We have it set up in my son's playroom where he can walk all the way around it and nothin ever bumps into it.
So, all in all, I am so glad that we purchsed this train table.  I think my son will play with this for years, especially since he has already shown interest in taking the tracks apart and putting them back.  I think if you use the train table as a train table, leave the tracks on it and don't glue them down, it will be perfect for any kid that loves trains.

reviewText:
I use this globe while homeschooling my children. It is pretty perfectly sized for little hands to hold while they look at the different countries. We have used this globe to teach perspective in how the sun, earth, and moon compare in size, and we have used it to show how the sun shines on the earth to create light during the day and darkness at night. We also have used it to talk about the different locations mentioned in books. The country borders are clearly marked on the globe, and it is easy to read. We can also easily store the globe if we need to put it away. Most often, when we do need to put it away, it's because my kids start throwing it around like a ball because it's so lightweight. It does leak every-so-slightly.

Pros
* perfect size and weight
* Countries and boarders are clearly marked
* Easy storage

Cons
* leaks ever so slightly
* kids think its a toy (not the product's fault)

reviewText:
Great 1vs1 dueling game similar to Magic or Hearthstone.  What makes this game unique is being able to play any card from your deck instead of having to draw.  Combat is done with dice which I enjoy.
The rules are very simple and easier to learn than any other game of this genre IMO.
What can be confusing is the difference between Mage Wars, Mage Wars Arena, and this game - Mage Wars Academy.
Mage Wars and MWArena are, for the most part, the same game.  Arena is the "rebranding" of the original Mage Wars which uses a board and a more tactical and complicated game in that there are a few more rules and strategies to take into consideration.
Mage Wars Academy is the "lite" version and a standalone game.  It has no board so plays more like a typical dueling game and sessions are much faster.
There are a ton of options as far as cards you can use.  It has suggested starter decks but you can customize them using a point system.  If you decide to move up to Arena you can use the cards from Academy but cannot go backwards (Arena cards will not work in Academy).  If you're an Arena player wondering if there are a good cards here you can use most of the feedback I have seen is that there are only a few worth having.  However if even if you are an Arena player you may want to consider getting Academy if want something to play with friends who you thank may find Arena too overwhelming.
As far as critiques there are a few I can offer but don't break the game at all.  1. Box is small hard to fit everything especially if you sleeve your cards. Personally I don't use the spellbooks so I made room that way.  2.  Would have been cool to include both a male/female version of the spellcasters.  Could have put them on flipside of character card.
All in all great game.  Looking forward to expansions.

reviewText: Beast Hunters Optimus Prime returns better than ever! Optimus has a more bulkier look with more armor and a cybertyronian looking truck mode with some beastly attitude. I love the neon green tint on the windows and how they gave Optimus a facial expression for better realism. Optimus comes with some cool new weapons that include his signature Star Saber and Ionic Pulse Launchers. The weapons are made with excellent quality overall. The Star Saber attaches securely in either hand while in robot mode and on the the top of the armor behind the cab in truck mode. The Ionic Pulse Launchers securely attach in either hand as well in robot mode,but can be used seperate with one stored on the back or combined with one on the top and the other on the bottom while in the hand. The Ionic Pulse Launchers attach securely to the sides of the armor in the bed of the truck while in vehicle mode. This Optimus is scaled up compared to the original powerizer version with improved poseability. The poseability is outstanding with great stability for creating cool battle scenes or displaying the Autobot leader where you please. The durability is excellent as well with secure ball joint construction and a solid overall build in robot or truck mode. All parts fit together securely during the transformation process for one quality transformer. The transformation level is intermediate meaning if you have plenty of experience with transformers there is mid-level difficulty. If you are a parent buying for a child of 5-6 they might need some assistance during the transformation process. Optimus is very versatile to be able to learn after a few times of transforming back&forth. To start off rotate the wing pieces together as one piece as the entire armor piece rotates up. The wing pieces rotate back down with the smokestacks facing straight up as the pieces then rotate inwards on each side under the middle piece. Next the front wheels on the back rotate down as the arms are positioned straight out. Next is a key part,remember to rotate the waist around 360 degrees so the wheels that you rotated down are in front of the cab area. The head piece rotates down as the arms rotate out to the side then around to the back under the armor. The armor pieces connect securely on the side to each forearm. Now the front wheels rotate up and into place along with the front grill of the truck. The legs connect together then rotate up into place to form the bed of the truck. The legs connect securely to the forearm pieces as the feet rotate up. Optimus is now ready to roll out! I also like the added attachments on the front grill that look like claw extensions to give the truck a cool animalistic touch. This is a great Optimus Prime transformer that has improved weaponary compared to the powerizer version and is more badass to be honest. Bottom line Transformers Prime Beast Hunters Voyager Optimus Prime is a well-made,high quality,10 out of 10 transformer all fans will enjoy. I highly recommend Transformers Prime Beast Hunters Voyager Optimus Prime to all transformer fans and collectors out there. Optimus Prime Rocks and Transformers Rule!!!

reviewText:
I held out from buying this version of Yahtzee but eventually gave in because I love the game so much. What an attractive set! This Folio Edition zips open to reveal a handy pocket sleeve for both the instruction manual and a Deluxe Yahtzee scorepad, with room for another scorepad or two, a loop holding a pencil with "Yahtzee" in beautiful, shiny red letters and a sturdy built-in tray lined with red felt at the bottom. Dice holder compartments are conveniently positioned below the tray's recessed roll area. The dice are a glossy cream color, nicely designed and sized with bold black pips, and rounded corners. The dice cup is just the right size for the dice, shaded a beautiful red on the outside and felt-lined black inside. The zipper handle is covered with a firm, spongy material with the "Yahtzee" logo in raised letters making the zipper easier to grasp when opening or closing the folio. A wonderful touch!

The game's portable size ensures that you can take it and play anywhere, although the Folio when closed is a bit bulky. The game description claims that the felt-lined dice cup and dice tray softens the noise the dice makes, making play quieter. This is True for the dice cup and the dice tray bottom, but the dice tray is made of a hard plastic; if the dice hit the wall of the tray, it is a bit loud, but this is only a minor complaint, and makes less noise when fewer dice are tossed in the tray or if they are tossed in more gently. When you are finished playing, the game zips closed with ease and the dice fit in the dice holder compartments, but I prefer to keep them in a small plastic zipper bag designed for dice stored in the dice cup.

The game has a classy, elegant and sophisticated look and feel; the makers did a splendid job with the Yahtzee Folio Game, it is beautiful! The sturdy design and ease of play of this edition is excellent for both Yahtzee lovers and first time players at home or anywhere you wish to play.

If you like scrabble, you will like this neat little card game.

At the beginning of the game you start out with a small deck of cards that you draw from to spell words. You score "cents" for the letters you use in spelling the words. This money you can use to buy more letter cards to add to your deck (deck building). Some of these cards have special powers that can help you get more cards or make it easier to spell words. Ultimately you are trying to wrack up enough cents to buy "fame" cards which are where the points are.

The game has rules for competitive play or cooperative play, plus some advanced rule options to make the game more interesting and challenging. If you like scrabble and card games, you will definitely like this word-spelling card game.

I am a little surprised at the number of good reviews on this thing.  First off, before you buy this know that there are companies who do it better, with higher quality plastic and much easier instructions.  So seek them out first before you spend money on this. I am suspicious of some of the reviews here, because quite frankly this is very low quality.

The minute you feel this you will know this is some pretty low end plastic, if it is plastic at all.  My daughter has a number of plastic toys that are durable and high quality, this is not one of them.  Everything feels flimsy and not quite right, including pieces that do not fit right.  Take for instance the kitchen sink handles. They just go in the hole and do not fit, they just spin. The instructions are a nightmare, the holes are not perforated, and many of the snap in parts such as panels do not work because they did not match with the panels.

I put together a Doc Mcstuffins pet vet before this, and even with a flaw or two, the quality is high and sustainable.  My wife put this together and is very handy as well, and this was a terrible experience for her. We would have thrown it back in the box and taken it back, but our daughter still wanted to keep it, so there is that.  Because it was pink she wanted it to work and have it put together.

 Be dubious and use judgement carefully if you by this.  Once it is put together, it looks nice enough, but some doors still do not close properly, and just pop open by themselves.  I say go down another road and look around and keep your money in your pocket on this one.  It is not worth it, and next year I will take my research to the next level.

reviewText:
This game comes with a stack of cards in a tin box, a poster looking thing (which we have yet to use) and a game cartridge. Basically the kids play the game cartridge and when they select a character, they do so by taking a picture of the character card they want. The character becomes animated and leaps out of the picture on the screen. Its the same process when answering challenge questions.

I was a little wary of getting a bunch of cards that I would have to keep track of, in addition to the game cartridge, but the kids really, really enjoy this hybrid card/ video game. I like that it incorporates the physical into digital learning games because the more senses they use while playing the more it stays with them. The kids love that when they take a picture of a regular card, it becomes animated on their LeapPad screen and recognizes it in their game. They have always been in love with the camera feature and I think that might add to the allure as well.

I did need to sit down with them the first couple times they played (I have a 5 yr old going into kindergarten, and a 7 year old going into 2nd grade. My 5 yr old was the one who needed help mostly) to help them when they didn't know what to do. The learning curve will probably be longer for younger kids and those who don't have experience taking pictures on devices.

They played the game in the car and, mean mom that I am, I wouldn't let them bring the cards. But my son discovered that he could play it without the cards as well because there's a little red button with three cards on it, on the capture screen, that will take you to a digital catalog of the cards for that game. The kids definitely prefer playing with the physical cards, but they'll do it the other way if they have to. So have no fear, when the cards get lost someday, the kids will still be able to play.
summary: Great way to bring the real world into a digital game

reviewText:
I have a 3 year old who is really into Legos, and a 1 year old who is getting into Duplos.  I've been looking for a mat that they could use to help keep the pieces contained, especially the small and easy to lose bits!  This is a mid sized mat with a side for regular Legos and one for Duplos.  The silicone is nice, quite heavy weight, and has no chemical smell.  The packaging is really tough to get the mat out of, so can't really be used for storing the mat.  In terms of keeping pieces contained, and stopping them from rolling away, it does a good job.  Unfortunately, it's not really any use for sticking the Lego pieces onto it.  The smaller pieces do somewhat attach to the dots, and sit flush with the mat.  The larger base pieces just sit on top and won't attach at all.  The Duplos fared better, but it's certainly not a solid base.  I wasn't expecting them to click down, but I was hopeful that it'd hold things steady at least.  If you're looking for something to properly secure items, a plastic base plate is a better bet, so we'll be using this mostly for containment (in an attempt to prevent Lego pieces from rolling away and being stepped on...ouch!)

reviewText:
All 3 of my boys loved this toy so I recently bought it as a gift for a new mom.  The stacking is fun well into and past the toddler years.  The pieces click into place so no frustrating toppling over.  The individual cups come together to make balls...5 different sizes, or as another reviewer noted, one large heavy ball (if the smaller balls are nested inside).  The kids love to stack, count, sort by color, put them together, and roll the balls all over.  Such a fun toy!

Two small things to note:

1) pulling the pieces/balls apart is difficult for the little ones.  However this also keeps them firmly together so they won't break apart when playing with them.
2) as a parent, it's a LOUD toy when used on a solid surface.  When your little one rolls the balls around over and over and over again, you might start to wonder why you bought these things.  In my opinion, worth the tradeoff for a happy child.
summary: Well loved toy by all 3 of my boys.

reviewText: Galaxy Trucker, from Czech Games, is a fun and exciting race to build the best spaceship- and not have it blow up on you!  Two to four players engage in a realtime race to build their ship, essentially constructing it out of a pile or random tiles.  This sounds easier than it is, as the tile placement must meet certain guidelines.  Players then move on to the audit stage, where everybody must make sure that everybody else's tile placement was done correctly.  Finally, you put your ship through the grinder- various events that pop up including pirates, meteor storms, and more.  If you can make it to the end, you get points based and bonuses.  Whoever has the most points wins.  This is a fun tile placement game that is a lot of fun.  It never manages, however, to rise to the level of greatness like, say, Isle of Skye, which requires more strategy.  Here, there is so much randomness that it can feel like its all over the place.  Still, there is no denying that it is a very engaging game that will have you and your friends laughing and sweating throughout.

Created to celebrate the 25th Anniversary of Segas Sonic the Hedgehog video game, this is a distinctive and colorful set. Included are three specially painted figures along with a metal coin/medallion for each. This set is a commemorative, not a toy and is priced accordingly.

Some collectibles are intended to remain boxed, and this is one of them. These are easy to identify because the box is designed to be part of the display, and the contents look better in the box than out. This box is relatively compact measuring 10 x 5 x 3 1/2 inches so its small footprint means it can easily be displayed on a shelf or desk.

This does not mean the tiny figures of Sonic, Knuckles and Tails along with the accompanying medallions cannot be removed and displayed, but like most commemorative items, to retain the pieces full value it should not be opened. The individual decides if this is a concern. Sometimes tactile concerns loom large.

For a fan, this is a nicely detailed set marking a milestone.

I love the compact nature of this game, allowing it to easily be brought along for playing with friends.

reviewText:
Fisher-Price is a brand I have known and trusted from my earliest memories and from the childhoods of my much younger brothers, but it is well on the way to being banned from my household. I can only assume that a boardroom decision was made to make all their toys louder to help them stand out on store shelves, which would be fine had they not cut corners and omitted a simple volume control switch. And this toy is loud. Too loud. Maybe dangerously loud.

The old joke about grandparents buying "the toys that make the noise" is 100% True in this case and (to their credit) my son absolutely loved it... when it made the noise. The speaker is contained in the white part of the ride-on with the musical keyboard. It does not take an expert to realize that there could potentially be some impact to baby's hearing if baby's ear was positioned by the speaker while baby pressed the keyboard keys over and over and over again. As Fisher-Price decided to save a buck on parts by not including an on-off switch or a volume control, the only way to address this concern was to unscrew the battery compartment and take the batteries out. Now baby finds it boring.

So close, and yet so far. One star.

We love family games. My daughter loves games that are word oriented. My husband loves games that are not long and easy to learn to play. This game makes all of us happy.

Essentially you are trying to find the word (or phrase)in your hand that best matches the word or phrase on the played card. The person who gets to judge the phrases or words suitability rotates through the players. You play five rounds and then the person who has had the most winning plays wins.

Part of what makes this fun is the table banter, getting to know the other players through the words and phrases they pick to play or pick to win each round. The other part of what makes this fun are the crazy little phrases or quotes on each of the cards.

So, an example might be this- the main card played that everyone has to match might be Rotten. At this point player one will pull one card from his hadn that matches this word. It might be Cruella DeVille. Player two might play the word apples. Another player might play traffic. The judge then reads everything and picks the word he thinks best matches Rotten.

This set comes with many cards. We have been playing off and on for over a year and haven't opened all of the cards. We have a family of five and play this once a week almost every week. So the party box while good for a big party will also provide you with years of fun as a family.

Well worth the money. Enjoy.

reviewText: Beginners telescopes can be problematic. Many are too childish and simplistic to see anything except a slightly larger version of what you can see with the naked eye. Others are so complex that, by the time you explain the setup and sight in the object of interest, the kids have become bored and wandered off to catch fireflies or play on their phones. In the spirit of Goldilocks, at last there is a beginners telescope that is JUST RIGHT. Sophisticated enough to give a really meaningful view of the moons surface, Lunar Telescope is simple enough that its complexities are easily mastered and in a short enough time that the budding astronomer will, hopefully, grasp the relevant concepts and still get that wonderful view of the moon. Supplemental materials that come with the scope give some tips on what to look for, and some silly games and valid history to make this the whole package to stimulate interest in the world of outer space. And, instead of seeking out stars and distant galaxies that are largely disappointing without a planetariums telescope, the focus here is on our closest neighbor  our very own moon. Tested on a ten-year-old, I can assure you that this is the intro to astronomy most parents yearn for! Set up and breakdown is easy, and the packaging is sturdy enough to store the telescope safely away for those new moon nights. Let me say, though, that if you are in a highly lighted city environment, you might want to take a drive into the country where it is dark enough to really experience the sky clearly!
summary: Just Right for a Budding Astronomer

With expansions adding new elements to the game, and the ability to but a turn limit on the game, this is a great party game.

reviewText:
I bought this as a gift for my 17yo cousin.  He is a huge fan of the Mario universe, but rarely played chess.  I feared the chess aspect might turn him off to the gift, but he absolutely loved it!

During my visit, he begged for challengers from both his siblings, his parents, and myself.  I played two games with him, and his father requested that he take my place for regular games with his son when I'm gone.  This is a first for these two, to my knowledge, and I'm excited that they could find something in common to enjoy together!

The rubber pieces themselves are very cute and easy-to-stand in their positions on the board.  The only placement issues come from when you have two large pieces next to each other, impending in each other's space slightly.  My cousin and I solved this dilemma by doing a little role-play mini-battle until one of them moved--think Princess Peach and Birda having a slapping contest.  It was very silly, but added an element of fun that chess normally lacked.

Minor issues: My cousin did note that they painted Bowser incorrectly, having Luigi as the Queen piece while Princess Daisy and Princess Peach were bishops was initially confusing, and we both struggled at first with getting the coin pawn pieces back into their correct positions in the plastic storing case.

However, the minor issues were very minor, and overall we loved this game!
summary: A Bridge Between Video Gamers and Board Gamers

reviewText:
This is a plug and play game, which means that the controller is all you need. After connecting the audio and video cables from the controller into your TV, you turn on the controller (which runs on 3 AA batteries -- not included) and start the game.

For non-serious video gamers, this is a fun toy. We bought this for my six-year-old. We don't have a game console, and he is in love with it.

It's a pretty simple game -- Spidey goes around, beats up bad guys using punches, kicks or web "shots". After the bad guys fade into oblivion, spidey has the opportunity to pick up coins (for points), hearts (for health credits) or keys (to open locked doors). With nine levels, it can keep a beginner entertained for hours. We allow our six-year-old to play this for about a half-hour at a time, no more than once a day. We're going into week 3 and he's just past level 4. He's making steady progress and the game is not frustrating for him, yet it's keeping him entertained enough that he's having a lot of fun.

There are also "secrets" that you can uncover along the way, but we've barely scratched the surface of those. At the end of each level, Spidey has to face off with an arch-criminal (hob-goblin, green goblin, the lizard, etc.) There is a "master planner" who is controlling the plot, but you don't find out who that is until the end.

Some on this list have complained about the graphics or the difficulty. This is by no means, a game for the serious gamer. This is for someone who is a young fan, or just a beginner who likes to have a little fun, but doesn't have serious gaming skills.

DURABILITY: The controller is fairly sturdy. We had looked at the Cars 2 plug and play game and didn't like it because it appeared fairly flimsy. This controller, is very similar to game console controllers on the market now. There is a directional tab on the left and three buttons on the right. there is also a "menu" button in the center at the bottom that allows you to pause the game and review a map of the maze you are currently navigating. My only concern is the wire. My son gets extremely excited when he plays and moves the controller up and down and any number of directions. As his force increases on the controller, it's possible that he might tear the wire and short the device, but we're keeping an eye on it and it doesn't appear to be a problem at the moment.

EDUCATIONAL VALUE: ummmmm......none.

FUN: As I said, for a novice fan or a non-gamer, this is a lot of fun. I've played it myself and enjoyed a few hours of entertainment. The music in the background does get a little old, but you can turn it off or turn down the volume. There is a story, which helps as you go through the game. While others found it annoying, I found it enjoyable.

....and spidey does everything that he can do in the comic books -- he's strong, climbs walls, crawls on the ceilings, slings his webs, etc... except for spider sense, he doesn't show signs of knowing his enemies are creeping up on him, but I have no idea how they would work that into this game.

GRAPHICS: Are fine. They are not stunning and not game-console quality, but they are perfectly fine, like an old arcade game.

For $20, this has provided us with several hours of entertainment and will probably last a long time. All in all, we're pretty happy with the purchase. (And as usual, anything purchased on Amazon came when expected and was in perfect shape.)
summary: Just right for young fans, plain old fun

This is the best thing money can buy! Do yourself a favor and skip the Standard and get the Advanced. For 300 more, you get better range, Glonass instead of GPS, and positioning sensors to fly indoor. When I first received my P3A, I was disappointed because the weather was bad outside and wanted to fly so bad. Fortunately, the P3A is capable of fly indoor and position itself very well. Even my 3 year son was able to fly it (I lifted off for him and only allowed him move the right joystick,my living room is pretty small also). Unless you have the extra bucks, go ahead and get the Professional.

The mobility of this aircraft is in a class of its own. It breaks immediately in the air as soon as you take your finger off from the joysticks. Other multirotors will continue to drift off, NOT this one!

FYI, If you live in the innercity like I do, you maybe experience a little bit of FPV (first person view/live video feed) interference. If you go away from the city to somewhere that is less radio towers, your video may be almost flawless. Also, that may depend on you tablet or phone. People are telling me that iPad 2+ works the best even though it works ok on my Note 4 too.

My only complaint is that DJI has set the altitude limit to 500m (YES i am aware of the FAA 400ft rule, and everyone should fly at their own risk and responsibility. Before i got my P3A, i wanted something that can go at least 1000m until i actually got mine. When i flew it up to 130m, i could barely see it in the sky. It was almost invisible. I wanted to go higher but did not want to risk losing my brand new P3A. Eventually, there will be a time where I will want to take it higher and higher (assuming that I will fly above 400ft outside of this country). So I wish DJI headquarters will change the altitude limit from 500m to 1500m.
