reviewText:
At first I was really excited to get this figure as Frieza is easily one of if not THE greatest villains in the DBZ universe and after seeing Resurrection F in theaters  I was even more hyped, then I received the figure and my excitement quickly turned to meh. I know many were extremely pleased with how  this figure turned out but I think there is one key area where Bandai missed the mark and that's on his scale and size. From most sources that I gathered and it appears to be so when watching Resurrection F that Frieza in his golden form grows in height and musculature, not by a very large margin but by enough that he's relatively the same height as Goku and slightly bulkier than his final form.

This figure is rather noticeably smaller than SSJGSSJ Goku in the same line and this wouldn't bother me as much if they had simply just re-used the same mold as Final Form Frieza that was released a few years ago because at least that would make sense from a cost saving perspective as it would give them time to work on other figures in the line that were soon to be released and it would give collectors who didn't get the chance to get an original a sort of simulacrum of the orignal BUT that's not the case. This sculpt is much more slender and much smaller in terms of bulk than the original when compared side by side and while there is a slight height increase in the new sculpt  it's not even close to where it really should be.

With all of that said they did put a lot of effort into this figure as the articulation is good, the sculpt is pretty well detailed, the paintwork and the likeness is dead on but I think that is what makes it so disappointing. If they were just going to use a new mold why not take the time and make sure to get the measurements right, to get the scale correct with the rest of the line???

While I can't say I wouldn't recommend this figure, it's probably one of the most anime accurate looking figures in the entire line, I will say that in my opinion this figure does not fit with the rest of the line in terms of size and scale and for me that isn't a deal breaker but it does definitely knock quite a few points off of his collectibility when he looks a little out of place on the shelf.
summary: He should have spent more time training.

Anyone willing to pay around $20 for this is obviously a Power Rangers fan, and at this point is probably deep in their 20's.
A fan will definitely get their money's worth, but let me clear up some confusion. People complain about the rangers not coming with a lot of accessories. Some just come with a holster and pistol- others some with a little more.
This is because these are exclusively MOVIE edition figures. The iconic six did not have their usual weapons (with the exception of Tommy).
Kimberly didn't use a bow, Adam didn't use an ax, and so on. The gadgets and/or weapons featured with the figures are the ones and only the ones they used in the movie.

The detail and proportions of the figure are pretty great, but the range of articulation is a bit limited for my tastes. They can't be posed to grab their morphers- which is an iconic pose. Having said that, this figure is only 5 inches tall so it's understandable. It's moderately durable, but the hands come off easily with handling. It's not much of an issue though because they don't fall off on their own or anything. The paint jobs are excellent and the attention to detail is phenomenal.

As a fan, this whole series was a dream come True for me. Caved and bought all six rangers.

My 4 year old loves Transformers Rescue Bots and watches them daily. He has several small Transformers but none of the Rescue Bots. When we received the Rescue Bots Beam Bots Game System to try courtesy of BzzAgent my son was thrilled!
The game system is really easy to use after you first install 4AA batteries into the bottom on the console, install 3AAA batteries into the wireless control and plug in the red and white wires into the TV.
Then your child places Optimus Prime into the console, switch the console on and then push the button on the top of the game console. Then, Optimus Prime disappears into the game system and appears on the TV.
The game loads rather quickly, which is great for impatient toddlers and allows them to choose 5 different games to play. You can also purchase additional figurines which allow them to play different games too.

You do have to make sure that the wireless control is pointed directly at the console and that there isn't interference.
I think this is a great game for young children, that is easy to play and allows them to feel like they are apart of the Rescue Bot Action.

reviewText:
[Update: my children have asked to play this game so many times, I'm going to have to bump it up to 5 stars.]

I played this with my 3 year old daughter and my (nearly) 5 year old son. The daughter didn't get much of it, but my son enjoyed it quite a bit. I did have to let him win though; I've seen these movies so many times, I knew about 90% of the answers. Still he enjoyed it quite a bit, both in regular game board mode and in casual party mode.

Game play is complicated or, if you want a positive spin, diverse, with numerous mini-games within the game, and I'm still not 100% sure how you are supposed to play out the end game. The game board needs a flat table to remain flat; we played it on a padded bench and it was hard keeping it level enough to keep the game pieces in play. As for the game pieces, they are lovely little pewter figurines; although I can see an emergency room trip should I ever accidentally step on Tinker Bell's wings.  Content is rendered for standard definition TVs; I'd have thought that we were far enough into the 21st century for all DVDs to be designed for widescreen TVs, but apparently not.

There is plenty of content, with an ample number of trivia cards, although this is not Scrabble, you are not going to get 100 full length games out of this set. Eventually, everything on the DVD will be exhausted, and this will end up at the yard sale. Still the subject matter might be the only trivia category that 4 year olds will be domain experts in.
summary: If Your Kids Have Seen the Pixar Movies A Million Times

reviewText:
Thank you Blue Orange Games for providing me with Keekee the Rocking Monkey and Spot It! Alphabet and Spot It! Numbers & Shapes, free of charge, for review on my blog Ahh~Mazing Reviews. These are my own honest opinions.

The Spot It! games are my 4-year-old son's favorites. We play these nearly every night. We received Spot It! Alphabet and Spot It! Numbers & Shapes. The games come in a tin, and consist of circle shaped cards that have letters and shapes, or numbers and shapes, depending on the game you are playing. One player turns over two cards, and the first person to find a match between the two cards wins those cards. It was surprising that no matter how much you shuffle these cards, there is always a match, no matter which two cards you draw. The person with the most cards wins the game.

It didn't take my son very long to catch on to how to play this game. He gets so excited when he finds a match, and yells, "I spot it! I spot it!" with his hands thrown up in the air.

reviewText:
This game was really fun. This is an adaptation of traditional Jenga Game - where you start with stacked wooden planks, remove one, then place it on the top of the pile. The goal of original Jenga is to not have the stack fall during your move, but make it unstable enough so that it will fall during the next person's move. With Jenga Boom - the added suspense is the platform the stack is sitting on. At some point the cord will run out, the platform will fall, thus making the stack fall. So, you aren't just trying to balance the stack, but also beat the clock.

This game, with the new twist - was really fun. We played with adults only, adults and kids (ages 5 - 7) and kids only. Every group had lots of fun. The only downside of Jenga is rebuilding the stack after each collapse, but the game is so fun you really don't mind. Jenga Boom also evens the playing field a bit when you have a physics whiz that understands contraptions playing against those of us with little to no depth perception - take that math boy!! But I digress, this game is really great for those that already know and love original Jenga as well as those who are new to the game.

The "Boom" contraption seems sturdy enough for the game to last for a while. The up side is even if the "Boom" contraption stops working, you can still play original Jenga. Definitely recommend for those that like hands on challenge games and games that are pretty easy for a number of age ranges.

reviewText:
I've been a Star Trek fan since I was born, basically...  I was born the same year that Star Trek came on the TV, and was just old enough at the time to actually pay attention (even though I couldn't speak yet!).  I fell in absolute love with the original ship, and have spent what's probably an excessive amount of my life thinking about this fictional spacecraft.

In 1979, they made a movie based upon the series, and they created a new version of the ship.  There was an in-story justification for the design changes (the ship was essentially torn down and rebuilt from the keel up, into an "almost totally new Enterprise," so that it would represent the best technology available), and a "real world" justification as well (the original creator of the Star Trek concept felt that the original design needed "updating," something which many people disagree with, frankly).

The new version of the ship, created for this 1979 movie, is what this model is of.  And this is my second-favorite ship design of all time (with the classic Enterprise being my first).  It had a much better "polish" in the construction of the model...  the model used on-screen is truly beautiful...  and it was very well-thought-through (in large part, due to the efforts of a gentleman named Andrew Probert, who later was the main designer for the "Next Generation" Enterprise as well).

There have been a number of model representations of the "the motion picture" (henceforth TMP) Enterprise over the years.  AMT (later Ertl) produced a decent kit, though with significant deviations from the "real" ship seen on-screen, and this brought about the creation of an entire cottage industry of "accurrizing" parts for this model (and for others as well, as time went on).

There have been some resin "garage kits" of the TMP Enterprise which were more accurate than the AMT kit, but these weren't perfect, either, and their quality varied wildly (some could be glued together and painted in a day and look nearly perfect, while others would require weeks of clean-up work!).  And there are special tricks and techniques required to build those anyway... it's not for the faint of heart, though the results can be spectacular.

A couple of years ago, Polar Lights released a very close to completely accurate model of the TMP Enterprise.  With minimal effort, you can make this into a near-perfect replica of what's seen on screen.  But...  it is a HUGE model, about three feet long, and fairly expensive as well.

So, Polar Lights (now a subsidiary of "Round Two") created a smaller TMP Enterprise model, and it's a beautiful piece of work.

The model is provided as a "snap fit" kit, so anyone can toss it together as a "toy-like" item.  For the most part, kids can handle it just fine, though there are a few places where even a strong adult can have trouble assembling some pieces!

If you're a more serious model-builder, however, you can (with a bit more care and patience) transform this into a smaller version of the huge 3-foot model.  The detail is VERY good, especially for a model of this size, and the model itself is quite robust when glued together (a bit more fragile when snapped, however).

There is still a bit of room for "accurizing" of the model, where some details are portrayed by decals, which ideally would be portrayed by 3-dimensional structure..  The aft end of the bridge, for instance)  I suspect that a photo-etched parts will replace these soon enough for the truly inspired modelers out there.

If you glue it together, and are good with an airbrush (and can find a good "pearlescent white" paint to paint it with), you can make this truly spectacular.  The model comes with a LOT of decals, some of which represent markings, but most of which represent "panel detailing" (something Trek fans refer to as "aztecing" because the panel detailing on the TMP ship looks like Aztec heiroglyphics).  These "Aztec panel" decals are transparent (or at least translucent)...  so the pearlescent effect of the underlying paint comes through quite easily.  This can give you a really remarkably accurate, detailed model without having to paint a million tiny panel details.  The use of this much decal covering on any model requires some specialized skills, and some materials most people aren't familiar with (such as "decal setting solutions" which soften decal material so it can conform to complex molded shapes and curves).  It's not "easy" to do this, but it's a lot easier than painting the paneling by hand, or masking it by hand and spraying thin layers of subtly different colors with an airbrush)

The end result is a very nice looking, very accurate model of the TMP Starship Enterprise.

One thing I've noticed...  virtually every Enterprise model ever made suffers from "nacelle droop" (where the twin engine nacelles eventually start to sag over time, and no longer line up with the rest of the ship).  The nacelles on this kit are very light...  so I'm hoping that the droop will be minimal.  But I'm not convinced that there will not be any.  The only way to avoid this, in my experience, is to build a mechanical structure inside (using metal plates) to reinforce the areas which tend to droop... but this would be very difficult to do on a model this small.  And the model itself is pretty light on plastic use overall...  it's almost "eggshell-like" in some areas.  So if you plan to treat a model roughly, don't expect it to last for very long!

Overall, I'm very happy with this model, and expect that I'll buy a few more (for "kit-bashing" purposes - that is, making models of other ships using parts from this) because it's relatively inexpensive.  But realize...  this is not a toy, or even a very robust model.  It's small, it's light, and it's delicate.  If you base your buying decisions on "amount of material" you might conclude that this model is overpriced.  If you base your buying decisions on QUALITY, however, you'll be happy.

reviewText:
I don't think it's a stretch to say that a quality Link figure is the Holy Grail of many a collector.  Well, consider that one checked off the bucket list, because they don't get much better than this.  I wasn't familiar with Figma prior to the release of this figure (not being much a bishoujo guy), but they're certainly on my radar now.  Everything about it is top notch, from sculpt(awesome) and paint(perfect) to the materials and articulation.  This is the first figure I've seen to have articulation in its FEET.  Even the back of Link's hood twists around to suggest 'flop' or move out of the way of the sword.

The accessories are just as good; This comes with FIVE different sets of hands, the Master Sword (Skyward Sword) and scabbard, classic Hylian shield, an 'angry' face, a different hairpiece, an energy wave deal that attaches to the sword, and an elaborate display stand with an arm.  Pretty much everything you could want.  The figure has two holes in the back for attaching the scabbard and still being supported by the stand.  Perhaps the highest attention to detail is shown by the fact that you can adjust the handle on the back of the shield so that it can be held in either the left hand (as in Skyward Sword) or in the right, as Link is canonically a southpaw with the sword. As someone already mentioned, the sword does feel delicate so a little extra care is probably well advised.

The figure is on the smallish side, I'd estimate around 5".  But what he lacks in size he makes up in soul, 'cause this thing is an attention grabber for sure.

Despite all that, I'm not quite sure it's worth $100 (really, Amazon?), because I've seen it available for MUCH less.  That's getting into the neighborhood of Hot Toys pricing absurdity.  Also, people that buy dozens of figures the second they come out to re-sell them later when demand goes up should be kicked in the face by a horse with indigestion.

Ultimately, this figure is made of pure awesome and there really isn't anything to dislike (besides the price) so I highly recommend it.  Now I just need a Twilight Princess Link to keep the ball rolling!

reviewText:
Munchkin Panic is a version of the board game 'Castle Panic', but skinned with a 'Munchkin' theme.  Characters and attacks align with the classic Munchkin art style and sense of humor.  I'd never played Castle Panic before, but do own Munchkin Fu and have played regular Munchkin before.  The rules were pretty easy to understand, and the manual is thorough.  I played with a friend who is also very experienced with board games, but had not played Castle Panic either.  The gameplay, in a nutshell, is you set up a castle and you protect it from an incoming horde of monsters.  If the castle is destroyed, or you destroy all of the monsters, its game over and the player who destroyed the most monsters wins.  Pretty basic.

The part we really loved is that we are both defending the SAME castle.  Even up to six players can be defending just one castle.  The enemies keep pouring in though.  Beyond that, maybe of the alliances and rules can be decided amongst the players.  For example, my buddy might not be able to defeat a monster on his turn, without help.  If he defeats the monster, he may receive a treasure card.  I can offer to help him, and in return he gave me the monster or the treasure.  It forces you to play together, but doesn't feel very cutthroat either.  Ultimately, we both wanted to kill ALL of the monsters before they took down our tower, so we made sacrifices for each other that we typically would not in similar board games.

Overall, it was a lot of fun.  We taught our wives how to play real quick while we took over watching the kids.  You can play the game solo as well, but I have not tried it yet.  My buddy even decided to order a copy for himself when we finished the first game!  Easy to play, family friendly, up to six players is a big plus.  Recommended.

reviewText: We've done the Shrinky Dinks Halloween Fun and had a blast putting it together. This was a great set too for me and my two kids, ages 6 and 11. We divide up the pieces, color, shrink and assemble. It is a great family project and the finished tree is a fun holiday decoration. I'm always amazed with the Shrinky Dinks because no matter how you color them, the shrinking always makes them look better. So a 6 year old and an 11 year old can both make fun ornaments. We've never had trouble with the Shrinky Dinks staying curled up. The key is to keep them in the oven long enough for them to curl and then lay flat. Another tip that was included in the Halloween fun box was to put a thin coating of baby powder on your baking sheet so that the pieces don't stick. This is easily washed off one they are cool and doesn't bake into the product. A really fun craft project for the holidays. We'll bring this one back out again next year and remember how much fun we had working on it together.

The Vtech Go GO Smart Animals Zoo Explorers playset is a great toy for kids in the recommended 1-5 year old range.  The set was easy to put together and proved to have enough activities to keep kids entertained. It comes with one animal figure which my daughter enjoyed moving around the track. The only downside to this set is that extra animal figures get to be pricey at between $10-$15 dollars apiece.

- Easy to Build
- Kids enjoy playing with this and it has a lot of "replay" potential
- Has multiple activities including music, movement, and phrases
- The multiple colors hold your kids attention
- Can function with other Go Go playsets

*** Negative Points: ***

- The individual figures get to be very expensive (they are between 1/4- 1/2 the price of the entire playset)

reviewText: Cutest game ever.  It's a counting game sort of like Hi-Ho Cherry-O, but way way cuter.  My 3 year old granddaughter will just sit and entertain herself with this by herself.  It has like 24 rubber bones (nice weight to them) that you scatter onto the board, which is an enclosed sided box that looks like a beach.  Each player has a dog bowl which is made of really heavy, heavy cardboard.  I doubt you could smash them if you jumped up and down on them, that's how heavy the cardboard is.  I digress.  It has a double spinner - you spin one of them to determine one of 3 actions to take, lose bones, pick up bones, or swipe a bone.  then spin the second spinner, which is attached to the first one, to find out how many bones to get, lose or swipe.  When all of the bones are gone from the beach, the person with the most wins.  There is a video to watch that explains it better.  The dog Shelby is adorable and she works like big tongs and is easy for little hands to grasp.  She's a nice size and works well.  It's so adorable, and it goes way faster than Hi-Ho Cherry O so you don't mind playing.

Really like this Ghost and Elite combo. It's really looks great, not as detailed as other brands. It's very lite.
Pros: Ghost
The base for the Ghost is spot on. Easily attaches to the Ghost. Maybe some electrical blue tinting next time.
Weapons rotate, boosters rotate, seat slides out to accommodate Elite.
Paint job is good. Great packaging.
Cons: Ghost
The seat only locks in at the fully out and fully in positions. Should be able to lock it in at different positions in-between.
Foot pedals to small, these are Covenant vehicles not USNC, Covenant troops all have big feet.
A bit difficult to get Elite to stay in the seat, but once in he stays in place unless you flip the Ghost over. Maybe enlarging the pommel of the seat so it can be used as clip to clip figures in seat may work. Controls are too close together.
Pros: Elite
Face sculpt looks great, Helmet really frames the face correctly. Best Elite look I've seen.
Detachable armor looks good. You can tell its not molded on to the figure, gives it more depth.
Articulation is not bad, better than most other brands. Pauldrons slide over the breast plate allowing for more poses to be achieved.
Carbine looks great. Hands are very flexible and durable. It Allows for a snug grip on the Carbine.
Cons: Elite
Armor is to bulky, bracers fall of to easily, pauldrons to bulky and loose.
Ankle joint below the knee does not articulate. It should be articulated. Mega Bloks is the only brand that articulates this joint I think.
Butt armor has to be removed in order to place Elite into the Ghost. Glad I didn't glue it on.
The angle of the wrist is off, maybe it was made this way so it can grip the Ghost controls but it doesn't look good posing with the Carbine.

All in all, Great Figure and Vehicle. It has issues but still a solid choice. It's only the first set from Mattel. Hope they Give the Covenant figures more articulation like the USNC figures and add a bit more detail. Oh ya, totally recommended.

reviewText:
This game is destined to be a classic. Proving the best games are often the simplest, the game can be enjoyed by a wide range of players including my fickle 7 year old and board-game eschewing husband.

The entire package is well thought out. It comes with a very durable reinforced cardboard tube that allows you dump the pieces in instead of having to reassemble the tower if you are in a hurry. The packaging is durable enough to lend itself to many trips and is not made of the standard cheap cardboard that most games come with.

The wooden blocks give the game a nice tactile feel and are very high quality.

Taking a page from the preschool days, you remove a block from any of the sublevels and add it to the top of the pile. The last person to move a piece without the tower falling is the winner. To begin again, use the included tower building form and stack the blocks back up.

Games last from 2-20 minutes, with each round having a unique outcome due to the nature of unstable structure.

reviewText: This toy safe is a lot of fun. Right out of the box(I liked the fact that the instructions were right on top so you can't miss them!), it will ask you to set the password after you press the activation button to open the safe(the three AAA batteries are already installed). Pick a password that only has a few syllables. If you pick a long, multi-syllabic password, the odds it will recognize it diminishes. I picked a two syllable password and had no problems. I tested it with saying the password with various inflections and also at various distances from the safe. It seems not to care about those things. It cares more about timing and tone. I also tried saying the password while the safe was in the box, which partially blocks the speaker/mic. It would not accept the password in that condition. When I took it out of the box, it accepted it. Interesting. Part of the fun(at least for me!) is seeing what it will accept and what it will reject. It says right on the outside of the box, and also in the instructions that you can reset the safe if you can't get it to accept your password, so don't worry. When I was younger, I had a toy safe that was made out of steel with a two number combination lock. The metal construction was nice, but it was very easy to crack the combination. This safe is made of sturdy plastic but it is far from easy to crack! The only way would be to open the battery compartment and reset it. Obviously, this is not a safe to put valuables in since it is just plastic, but this raises an important question: is it a good idea to give children a safe to hide things(especially, hiding stuff form the parents)? It is a recipe for disaster! So, this is loads of fun for adults and kids with adult supervision, but giving it to kids encourages them to hide stuff from adults, something these days that is not a good idea. Use with caution!

reviewText:
This kitchen is really great, but it does have some flaws in my opinion.  First, the good stuff:
1)It has everything a kid would want in a kitchen including a fridge, freezer, oven, dishwasher and microwave, all within a very small footprint.
2)The durability is great, we bought it over a year ago and it's still in perfect condition, even with constant play
3)Kidkraft customer service is excellent.  A couple of the pieces were broken upon arrival, Kidkraft shipped new parts quickly and free, so no repacking, sending back, etc.
4)It's really cute, my daughter loves the colors.  I was thinking of buying her a more modern looking kitchen, but ultimately decided to go with one I thought my daughter would prefer.  She loves the bright colors, and I don't regret getting this one.
5)The sink is removable.  Believe it or not, this is a good thing.  Most likely, at some point, your child will pour some type of food or drink into the sink, so taking it out and rinsing at the real sink is a great benefit.

Now for the things I don't like:
The burners are raised.  When I bought the kitchen I specifically wanted the version with the raised burners (the older version didn't have it).  I thought it's cuter and more realistic.  The problem with the raised burners are that dirt gets in between and under it, and it's literally impossible to clean it.  Another negative of the raised burners are that the area then can't be used as counter space for cutting food, preparing, etc.  This is my second issue with this kitchen.  It doesn't have any leftover "counter space" for playing.  Had the burners been flat, that area could have had more than one purpose.  Also, the kitchen has plenty of storage space, but you will be using the "appliances" for storage.  There are no cabinets.  My daughter still manages to cook and bake even though her kitchen is stuffed with play food, dishes, etc.
Overall, I still think it's an excellent kitchen and a great value for the price.  If you have the room for a play kitchen, it's definitely worth the space it takes up.  It's one of the most played-with items in our playroom.
summary: Excellent Overall, but look at the other Kidkraft kitchens as well

reviewText:
I have no patience for people who complain that the questions in this game are difficult.  That's the whole point.  If you want easy questions, play the board game version of "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire" rather than Trivial Pursuit.

One of the fun features of this particular version is that the events in question have happened within my lifetime, so I can actually answer a few questions by remembering the specific events of the question.  This never happens for me (born in 1978) with the original version of Trivial Pursuit (for the obvious reason that it was made just after I was born).

My critiques of this version are minor and rather nitpicky.  Honestly, I don't know why they need to create silly new names for the categories (Global View, Written Word, etc.), which just makes it more difficult to remember which colors corresponds to which category in this particular version.  I think that the original categories (or even the small adjustments that they made in later versions to include a Wild Card category) were fine.  I also don't really understand the point of the new card-holder, which is unnecessarily cumbersome and forces the two teams to trade it back and forth from team to team.  We actually just gave a loose stack of cards to each team to read and completely ignored the silly card-holder.

With these few complaints aside, we always enjoy playing this game.  There are always folks who say that they hate Trivial Pursuit and feel stupid when they play it.  They'll hate this version as much as any other version.  But for those who are interested in trivia and enjoy learning new tidbits of information, this one is solid and fun to play.

reviewText:
What a fun variation on traditional Apples to Apples! My husband, friends, family, and I have long loved the regular version of A2A, but now we want to introduce our five-year-old to games, and this seemed like the perfect start. The green cards with the adjectives on them are a wonderful way to introduce new vocabulary in a fun way so it doesn't even feel like learning. (Because, after all, the purpose of the game is to have fun, right?) The pictures on the cards are colorful and entertaining, and there are a few that kids consider just scandalous enough to be hilarious. (For example, there's one with a little boy on the potty. Only the thighs and legs are exposed, so there's no REAL nudity, but it's clear what's going on.)

I also played this with my second-through-sixth-grade creative writing students on the last day before Christmas break, since I wanted something word-related and educational but still entertaining. I thought it would earn me a half hour. They lasted well over 1 1/2 hours, and when they bell rang they were SO disappointed. It was perfect for a large age range, and the kids really bonded, which was so fun to watch. (It was only our fourth session together, and with such a large age gap many of the kids hadn't met before the trimester began, so they were quite separate before the game.)

Now that Christmas is almost here we will have family coming into town. I can't wait to play this with everyone, from our daughter to our daughter's grandparents.

P.S. For those used to the grown-up version, the main differences here are that the green cards have two adjectives on them so the judge gets to decide which one to use, the red noun/name cards have colorful -- and varied -- photographs instead of words or names, and the words and photos are PG.

reviewText: This is a very frustrating figure for Alfred Pennyworth. With the beautiful facial sculpt jobs that Mattel has done on so many other figures, particularly with the Bruce Wayne/Jim Gordon 2-pack that was released a few years back, this is NOT a likeness of Michael Caine. This is, as was stated in another review here, the "generic old man in a suit" figure. If you squint, you might possibly see some likeness, but other than that, this particular figure is necessary to your collection of THE DARK KNIGHT RISES Movie Masters figures since Mattel has decided to apply the "Build a Figure" type of sensibility to these figures as well. All of the figures of this first wave come with a piece of the famed Bat Signal that, once assembled, is actually functional and not just a nice piece of decoration. Batman and Bane come with somewhat rudimentary pieces, so naturally the figure with the least "action" to it is going to be the one that is necessary for completing this miniature functioning Bat-Signal. It's a pretty smart marketing decision, but sadly it's a pretty lame figure. The other problem is that of serious collectors vs. die-hard fans. Fans will want to crack all these figures open, assemble the Bat-Signal and watch in awe as it casts its glow on the ceiling, but that's the only way that the figure is worth anything to the fan buyer. Collectors will have a much better time with it keeping it encased since this figure is already notoriously hard to find.

I researched for hours before deciding on buying a table and chairs from Teamson. I'm so glad I went with them. I even called them to ask questions about their products and they were extremely helpful. I imagine if I had any product issues that they'd be great to deal with.

I was a tad hesitant due to the price (and only getting two chairs) but they were soooooo cute! Let me tell you... as cute as that picture is.... the real thing is even better. I was just as thrilled as my toddler. I'm so glad we bought them. They were packaged great and easy to assemble. My only potential issue is that the back of the chair is a bit heavy (this is good in that it's a quality product) but if your child leans back it could topple over. (it would not topple back with normal sitting but if the child pushes back in it, and it's on carpet and snagged, it could topple easily.) To remedy this, we have the chair designated for my toddler (at least for now as she learns how to use it well) to be backed up against her little toddler sofa chair (you could use a wall or the side of your couch, whatever). It still leaves room for her to get in and out. We also sometimes butt two of the chairs up against each other, making it into a little bench and giving her more "seat" real estate. Then, again, it's backed up to her toddler (faux) leather arm sturdy chair which serves as the back to her little wood chair/make shift bench. Hope that all makes sense.

What does that also mean though? We need to buy the remaining two chairs. Happy to do so. After all, mommy and daddy need a place to sit (gently of course - hoping it holds our weight - they seem very strong and sturdy though. Husband said it should be no problem). And, when it's time for tea parties, our girl needs the chairs for her dollies.

I want to reiterate the beauty of these products. I'm beyond happy with them. I ordered the stool for the bathroom and the toy chest, too, now that I've seen the quality. I'm waiting for those to arrive. Next week!

OH! And lastly! They make many different designs and recently came out with dinosaurs! :) I'd advise checking their website for all of the different options and then coming back to Amazon to purchase for Prime free shipping (if applies) and better pricing overall.

As to comments regarding Amazon vs Oriental Trading pricing: Absolutely compare your shipping costs when making a decision. We love our Amazon Prime perks and the 2-day shipping is great benefit when racing the clock. However, if not in a rush, Oriental Trading regularly offers free shipping and discounts on their site; you may save a buck or two. Happy shopping!

reviewText:
The big selling point for this Nerf toy is the distance and speed with which it fires its darts.  Part of this is the fact that it uses Nerf Elite darts which are different than the standard orange dart.  They are heavier at the tip and designed to travel farther.

What's in the box?
* Nerf N Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster
* 12 Elite darts
If you are very into Nerf Blasters, you will note this blaster is very much like the Recon.  The parts appear to be interchangeable. Apparently, it was revamped to fire farther.

You can remove parts of the blaster and use it as a "handgun" blaster or a larger rifle.  The stock removes, as does the barrel extension, and of course, the clip comes off.  This amounts to 4 different configurations.

It does fire as advertised and I shot at distances of 60-75 feet on a regular basis.  If you fire at a complete level angle, you probably won't get more than 40 or 50 feet in range (how much do you need? It's a Nerf!), but if you angle the shot up very slightly, you will easily make another 10 or 15 feet and typically the promised 75 feet.

Loading is easy.  You press the release button on the included clip and load it with up to 12 darts (also included).
The blaster feels well made.  You can try to use standard Nerf darts in the blaster, although they will under-perform as far as distance and may jam sometimes.  You can, however, use Elite darts in most other Nerf guns and they will work fine and may even shoot a little farther than your traditional orange Nerf dart.

The darts do travel far and fast, just keep in mind this is not a "machine gun" type blaster so you will need to pump each time you fire.
It would be nice if Nerf included more Elite darts in the package.  Twelve is too few considering the distance this fires and needing to recover the darts.

I haven't noticed any more jamming than with other blasters I have.  It does seem a little more lightweight than some similar blaster; it feels "less solid" than the Retro.  I am not sure if this will affect durability - time will tell, and I will update this review accordingly.

All in all, a lot of fun and great distance.

reviewText:
Read my review on the Starter Track and save your money...
This product has a lot of great features, which I will start with, and one major issue, GAMEPLAY, especially with expansion packs and cars. Understand that I am including expansion packs and expansion cars in my review because ANKI is the one including all the expansion possibilities in their marketing of this Starter Kit product.

Pros
- beautifully packaged
- outstanding car look and detail
- awesome car lights with varying colors
- simple track set up that is FUN fun fun!! (with a few minor tricks for risers to create multi levels)
- software is simple enough to grasp for people with experience on iPhone (first use of each expansion car required a little download update, that is fine with me)

Cons - You must be able to PLAY the game, or it is just a model kit, which is a 1 of 5 stars.
- major issues with gameplay, I repeat MAJOR. In Anki Demos on line - watch the demo with 10 if not 40 cars driving around the track flawlessly, we know that gameplay is limited to 4, with that said, lets start with a reasonable set of expectations a SIMPLE race with 2 to 4 cars... Just know that the following procedure must be repeated before each and every race, any mistake on the test laps, which I will list examples below, causes you to have to STOP and repeat all of these steps, which is too too often:
A. Each player must load the game on their phone/tablet (great) OR (not great...) back out of the failed game to return to the "room" that the host will select the players out of.
B. Place your car behind the start finish line on the track
C. On your phone/tablet select your car from the available cars, Host starts the race
D. Host begins race, and the cars take two laps around the track (attempt to anyway) to understand the shape/configuration of your track
E. Race may begin

So... knowing that is how EACH and EVERY race takes place whether you changed any racetrack configuration or not here we go...

-----we laid out a track with 2 cars and 4 cars, really made no difference in the errors, 50 % of the time, at least one of the cars could not drive around the track and stop at the start/finish line correctly which is required for most of the gameplay options (not time trial mode). Failures included but were not limited to:
1. inability to jump the ramp piece
2. cars getting confused during the test lap and literally turning around and going the wrong way
3. cars just plain driving themselves off the track then searching helplessly around the tile floor looking for the track
----- during gameplay if you cars leaves the track and this happens often, forget about putting it back o the track and trying to finish the race, whether by buggy software error, or someone shooting you off the track you are DONE most of the time, even when placed almost exactly where the car left the track the car is now disoriented and rarely will function properly for that player
----- use of the Launch Piece increases game failure rate - cars fail to jump the ramp successfully about 1/3 of the time when trying the test lap and during gameplay, this wonderful piece makes it very hard to get a race going
----- use of Big Bang - we had problems with the car Big Bang getting to the start/finish line properly, sometimes he would bang the other cars as it finished its warmup lap and tried to line itself up at the line. Bad news if you lets the race go on from this point because the cars are disoriented to the track, you must restart the race preparation procedures.

Ah, you are thinking user error:
----- Yes the cars were fully charged
----- Yes we had clean track piece
----- Yes we cleaned the tires with the tire cleaner

If Anki fixes these issues I would love to own the product. It simply, unequivacally DOES NOT WORK AS SHOW AT ALL!!!

I can be honest in saying that I had never heard of this company before trying this out, most likely because of it being a European company and only finding the company at our local Toys 'R Us.

For example the lodge has little things like logs for the fireplace, beds, tables sunglasses on the characters and so much more.

I highly recommend Pinypon to all and hope to find some great new sets to follow these!

The instructions are poorly written. That must be stated before anything else is said about this game. My gaming group found video tutorials online and learned from them. Then we test-played a couple times before playing "for realz". Others have given much details about the game so I'll just give my impressions.

If you like resource games, such as Catan, you'll most likely like Agricola. There's a huge advantage in having as many kids as possible as the farming couple. And the game is different every time it's played, at least for our group.

Be aware there is a ton of teeny, tiny pieces and that sometimes there aren't enough of certain pieces to go around so you'll have to use multipliers. The board is also rather large and you need an absolutely flat playing surface or you'll lose your itty bitty pieces. Game play typically lasts about 2 hours. It's definitely not a game to take to a place like a coffee shop or brewery, and dogs will happy tails can mess up the board. For these reasons I often have a hard time finding people to play, even among regular gamers. But, it's a fun game when the circumstances are right.

Anything that gets kids nowadays out of the house and away from the TV screen is good in my book so I would highly recommend this as a fun and entertaining toy option.

reviewText:
I have to give this OgoBild Animate it kit a mixed review. I have a 9 year old grandson who has been making videos on his own for as long as he knew such a thing existed. He mostly uses Lego backgrounds and figures for his movies. We have also worked with "flip books" in the past, so he grasps the concept of how a movie is actually created frame-by-frame. So I was excited to present this kit to my grandson when it arrived.

His reaction was less than spectacular. First, he wanted nothing to do with the "characters" that come with the kit. He thought they were too babyish. So we got out his Lego figures and backgrounds to replace the characters that come with the kit. We downloaded and installed the software. And then we both just kind of stared at the screen for awhile... what next?

Although he's used movie editing software before, this software was more difficult to figure out, and there is, of course, no paper manual to sit and read while you try things out. (Dear Manufacturer's: Bring back paper manuals!) We set up a 2nd computer so he could read the manual online while working with the software, and that helped. He got his background and Lego men all set up -- and then had to deal with the camera repeatedly falling over -- sometimes even crashing into his "scene" which, of course, ruined everything.

It took an entire afternoon -- and I mean a good 4-5 hours - to make a relatively quick "movie". My grandson felt he could have done it far quicker with his regular video editing software.

The frustration level for a 9 year old - and a pretty tech savvy 9 year old at that - was pretty high. Higher still for the grandmother who wasn't much help.

I guess if he had a tech savvy parent sitting next to him to walk him through this, he might have enjoyed it more. But as an "out of the box", kid-friendly kit? Not so much.

reviewText: This is absolutely fantastic stuff for kids to play and create with, *especially* if they're tactile-oriented. It feels awesome - soft, easy to squish, fun to mold into shapes, and generally something you want to keep your hands on because it's so rewarding, sensation-wise. You don't really need anything but your imagination and some things to shape it with - molds, plastic utensils, whatever. It holds the shape you give it quite well, and in a sense it is almost like fluffy Play-Doh. It is *not* sand, and it's not really even remotely sand-like, but I think that's a plus - it's as fun as sand, but not nearly as messy, and it feels better, too. Also, it never dries out - or, at least, it didn't dry out at all after being left open for days on end, so it's fair to say that, if it *does* dry out, it does so very, very slowly. A baggie of this might make for an excellent travel distraction, actually - it stays together pretty well, is easy to clean up, and might keep your child distracted and quiet on long trips, in which case it's effectively priceless. This kit, unlike the other one in my video, contains sand that glows in the dark, as well as glasses and a flashlight to help it do so. Is it worth the extra money? I think so, and here's why: first, it feels *exactly* like the other Sands Alive products, so there's no penalty paid for the glow feature. Second, as a rule, kids love things that glow. Third, it's not only fun to see it glowing, but it's also fun to then mess with it and notice that the "sand" underneath does "not* glow: unless you bring this out into the sun and mix it well and continuously as you super-charge it, you will effectively only get the top surface glowing, and the rest will remain "dark". You'd think this would be a bummer, but it is actually very fun in reality. The glasses and the light are not UV lasers, and so you can't really draw patterns and see them unless you hold the light *really* close to the surface and then turn it on, and turn it off before lifting it much - that process *will* create some visible designs, but they're not all that distinct. It doesn't matter, though - it's still really, really, surprisingly fun! reviewText:
I got this for my youngest little girl, but it turns out the oldest child (6 years old) wound up using it the most. This - in a nutshell -  is AWESOME! (yes, I've been watching too much of the Lego movie) I wish I had this as a kid. My oldest has been driving this thing all over the neighborhood and absolutely loves it. He comes home from school and the first thing he wants to do is hop in the Jeep. (Yes, he's a boy who doesn't mind all the pink, which I am actually quite proud of.)

Both my husband and I have been impressed with how far he can go on one battery charge. Our neighborhood has a half-mile loop with plenty of hills included, and my son has driven that with no problem. It goes off road just fine - in our back yard, on the sidewalk, on the road - all of it has not stopped this thing. What has stopped it? Well, my son likes to drive the Jeep through our sand pile. (Instead of a sand box, we have a sand pile. It just worked out easier that way for us.) Often the Jeep will do just fine, but sometimes it does get stuck and he has to get out and push. The Jeep has also had difficulty in our garage. I think the concrete there is so smooth that it can't get a grip so the tires just spin away.

The features - like the radio/Mp3 player and the overhead lights are quite cool, but since they take separate batteries, we have not really used them. Even though the Jeep has seating for two, it is very small. Unless the kids are both 3 years old and pretty skinny, they likely won't fit. At least, we've had limited success getting more than one kid in and staying safe.

Assembly was also quite easy. It took about 1.5 hours but that's only because my son insisted on helping and he's a bit slower than the typical adult. The only thing of note is that the battery takes 18 hours for the initial charge. If you're giving this as a gift and want it to be ready at the unveiling, I would assemble it and start charging it the night before.

Overall, this Jeep has been a total hit. My kids love it, the neighbor kids love coming over and playing with it. Heck, *I* would love to hop in too but alas, I don't fit.

reviewText:
Spontuneous is a fresh, clever & fun new family board game. You start by coming up with a list of words. Each word needs to be found in a song. Then once a word (trigger word) is given, the first person to come up with the lyrics that uses that words (in a phrase/line of at least 5 words) gets to roll the dice & advance. My 14 year old daughter LOVED the game. Even after our game was finished, she begged us to keep throwing out trigger words for her. She can't wait to play it with her friends. My 17 year old son is not a fan of most family games and although he did play with us, he couldn't wait to finish. He claimed that he didn't know enough songs to play. My husband & I both enjoyed it, though we did find that the 15 second allotment was hard at times. The directions weren't too complicated which was a big plus! There are challenge cards to get if you land on a certain spot. There was one penalty card which you could use if you caught someone on their cell phone! The game is designed for 4-10 players and is relatively short with games lasting about 30 minutes. It was interesting how we would all come up with different songs for each trigger word!

*I received the game for the purpose of trying out & reviewing. My thoughts & opinions are my own.

reviewText:
My three year old twins (particularly the son) LOVE Thomas, so I was super thrilled to get this track set for them to play with.  They have several of the take-n-play engines, but this was the first track set, so I was as excited as they were.

First, assembly was awful.  The directions are line drawings, and the parts aren't labeled, so it took a bit to figure out which pieces of track went where.  I had to add an additonal 10 minutes to the assembly time because the drawings aren't very detailed, and the pieces aren't labeled, so I put the side bars on backward.  The pieces aren't meant to be taken apart once snapped together, so it took me an additional 10 minutes to use a precision screwdriver to carefully seperate the pieces and assemble them correctly.  So, after a total of 20 minutes of so, the track was ready to use.  In case you don't know this already, this track will NOT stand up on it's own, it has to lean up against a wall.  We have hardwood floors and the track kept sliding down, but we moved a throw rug over by the wall and it provides traction to keep it in place.

As for the "accessories" to the track, the first piece, (not including the stop gate) is a yellow "crane" type thing that the train is supposed to swing over edge of the track as it goes by.  This works piece works, WHEN the "crane" will stay snapped in place, but it usually flies off the first or second time a train passes by.  I usually don't put it back once it falls off unless one of the twins asks me to.  The small red "bridge" stays in place, but I'm not 100% sure what the purpose of it is.  The small yellow crate that is supposed to be "slid" down the track falls off constantly, usually before the train even gets to it.  To tell you the truth, I'm not even sure where it is now, it's probably in the bottom of the toy box.  Last we have the paint shop, which is adorable and thankfully, actually works.  Even though my toddlers just turned 3, they are able to fit the "paint splash" into the area where it belongs so that Thomas can get "painted."  However, the paint only works with Thomas (who is included) so the paint wont' "stick" to the other trains.  While the paint splash works, the paint "shop" tends to fall off the track with regularity.

 As for the "track", the turns are quite sharp, and it is not unusual for a train to derail by the second switchback.  I'm also not buying the "take and play" aspect of this thing....adding a hand hold at the top does not make something "portable."  This thing is too big to be easily packed up and carried anywhere.

My twins love this track, and usually at least one of them plays with it every day. On the other hand, they just turned 3, and are quite happy letting the trains roll down the track, and don't really mind that the "accessories" don't really work.  I think a child that was a little older would get very frustrated with the parts falling off and having to replace them each time a train went down the track.  Personally, I would give this item 1 star, but since my babies do enjoy it so much, I decided to give it three stars, meaning it's "OK."  I have just started buying Thomas items for my kids, and I like the quality of the take and play engines, but this track is terrible.  I hope other take and play tracks perform better.
summary: Toddlers would rate it five stars, I'd only give it 1.

reviewText:
We own the "Cover your Assets" game by Grandpa Beck and love it, but we heard that the Skull King game was even better.

We got it, and it's quickly become a favorite. The rules took some getting used to because we'd never played a "trick" game like this before. There's a couple youtube videos that explain how it works, but it comes down to each player guessing how many hands they are going to win each round. If a player wins the exact amount they guess, they are awarded points. If not, they lose points.

What makes this so fun is chanting "Yo, Ho, Ho!" at the beginning of each round, hitting fists against the table with each word. The last hit, the players open their fists, revealing with fingers out how many "ticks" they think they can win that round. It's lots of fun and adds the Pirate-ness of the game.

It does take a little getting used to, but play a couple practice rounds after watching the youtube demos and you'll get it.

I bet some would have been worth money now, but like all teens, I sold my childhood stuff at a garage sale.  People give me gifts now and then with Charlie Brown or Snoopy on them.  Not so much these days now that I'm, well, OLD, but you get the drift.  The oldest thing I own and my most prized posession is a Snoopy bean bag doll I've had since I was 5.  So I'm a hard-core Charlie Brown guy, if there even is such a thing...
But yes - this is a nice little set.  I should empathize "little".  The figures are maybe 2 inches tall.  Tiny.  But - they look great - I've never heard of "Schleich" before, but they've done an admirable job here.  It's a cute little set - but for the price, I don't know.  You know what would really make it worth it is if it came with the tree too.  Instead, Charlie Brown is clutching his poor tree to his side in this figure.  But it would be cool if it had the tree too - I think that would really make it a "complete" set; Snoopy has his house, Charlie Brown has his tree- Merry Christmas!

reviewText:
For what it is, and for what it is trying to be, this game is perfect. IMHO, you won't find a better "pure" press-your-luck style game.

Anybody, of any age, will have fun with this. Once someone is alone in the temple, just wait until everyone is going "Ohhhhhh! ... OHHHH!" as each new treasure card is drawn. And, the theme actually does make it a cooler experience. No, you won't actually feel like you're exploring a temple, but it definitely feels like an "adventure," vs. something like Can't Stop.

The components are also very nice the card-stock is THICK and heavily coated, the little jewels are great, the tents are a nice touch (though not as durable as the rest of the pieces.) Even the box it comes in seems like it could survive the apocalypse.

The only complaint I have is that certain "rounds" can end after just a few cards being drawn (e.g., two spiders come up immediately), which is kind of a bummer especially if it's your first time playing this game with a new group, and it happens multiple times in one game. I would almost suggest slipping a few big treasure cards into the top of the deck... it's not cheating if you just want everyone to have fun! :)

Highly recommended family game.

reviewText:
We received the Air Hogs Shadow Launcher as a promotion from BzzAgent a couple of weeks ago.  This is the fourth indoor, remote-controlled helicopter that has been part of our household, and typically these have been operated by my 9-year old son.  None of the previous drones lasted more than 24 hours of play in the past, so I was certainly skeptical that this one would last very long.  It did last for a week and provided hours of entertainment.  At one point, one of the rotors broke, but we were able to fix it at first. Later, the helicopter would not lift off at all - it would pop off the tank and flop around on the floor, hence my rating of 3 stars.  I wish these toys were more durable, which is what I would expect for the $40-50 price tag.

Compared to the others, the Air Hogs Shadow Launcher was very easy to operate right from the box. We added the batteries and the copter charged in no time. My kids (9 and 5) had loads of fun driving the tank around the house and launching the helicopter.  This helicopter was much easier for my 9-year old to control compared to the other helicopters we have had. In that sense, I think the age recommendation of 8+ years is appropriate.  My 5-year old daughter and nephew were also able to figure it out pretty readily.  They had loads of fun chasing the cats with both the tank and helicopter. Compared to other helicopters, the battery life and helicopter charge on the Air Hogs seemed similar, if not a little better.

All in all, I probably would purchase this helicopter for a child under 12 over similar-sized indoor drones.  I'd rate it a 3.5 if I had the option, but chose 3 stars because ours broke.
summary: 5 stars for fun 1 star for durability

reviewText:
A fine version of a classic board game.  Upwards is much like scrabble with an added dimension -- you can put letters on top of one another to create new words.  Scoring is 2 points for each tile in a brand new word; 1 point per tile if you are going up vertically in the word (there are some other details, but that is the basic premise).  I am a huge fan of word games and I really like this one.  I find it easier to play with kids than the original scrabble.  It seems easier for lots of people to change a word than to create a new one from scratch.

Excellent value for money.  Easier to keep score than Scrabble.  Fun for a variety of ages.

I purchased this clock as an extra "throw away' clock to use at work for quick games. If it breaks or someone walks off with it, or to use around water, I didn't invest a lot of money. $20.  It's the only reason i bought this one.

Well I'm impressed. Then again it's made by DGT. It does seem 'cheap' by look and feel, but it is durable.  At 6.1 x 2.4 x 1.6 inches  it is pretty small though. This is just a count down/up timer. No frills, no extras.

Use for games, music practice, meditation, devotionals, study time, reading, speeches, when to take a break from the computer, debates or cooking.

Once the time expires, it counts up. So you know how long you've waited after the original time expires. So you could time your speeches or whatever you're working on to see how long it takes. So you could set the count down for a few seconds, and upon the buzzer, start. When you finish,whatever task, look and see how long it took you.

For just an inexpesive simple timer.  I can reccommend this one. No delays, increments, etc.  This may or may not be a good chess 'blitz' clock for you if you're a hardcore blitz player. Just counting down or counting up time control, with or without a tone at the end. Very simple.

It's a good inexpensive clock for timing your game(chess,checkers,backgammon,jenga,scrabble,boggle,etc) to keep your opponent from taking 'forever' to make a move.  <wink>
Great for other time management needs as well.

I am going to try and post pictures I took with a digital camera just pointing it down the eyepiece to show what the magnification looks like.  I was looking at chocolate milk powder last night and you could see all of the components from sugar crystals, cocoa, and the perfect little white spheres of the dried milk substance.  Very cool.  The scope is smaller than the fixed lab kind, but I would not say it is a mini or even really a toy.  This is a small lightweight battery operated microscope.  I bought it for my four year old's birthday and have not given it to him yet, but I had to try it out and am very impressed.  I will supervise his use of it as I do not think it should be thrown around or handled roughly, but it does not feel flimsy or particularly fragile.  20X magnification makes the tip of a plastic eye dropper fill the entire field of view, and the ripped edge of a piece of paper shows a weave of glossy fibers.

reviewText:
Tapple is a fast paced, easy to learn word game.  Amazon's Product Description is very thorough so I'm not going to repeat the rules.  If you enjoy word games, you'll probably enjoy Tapple. My family members who don't like word games did not want to play.

We had 7 players for our first game and I was last to play.  I was getting  more & more nervous as my letters were used. Just as it was time for my turn,  I thought of 'yogurt'. I was ready to press the letter down...only to realize that there was no 'Y' to tap. So I had to very quickly think of another food that still had a letter available. The more players there are, the harder it becomes for the last players to come up with a word. Just so you know, these 6 letters have been left off the Tapple Board: Q, U, V, X, Y, & Z.

Each of the 36 category cards is divided into four  sections for a total of 144 categories.  The blue/white side has easier categories for younger players, & the red/yellow side is more challenging for advanced play. Of course, you can come up with your own categories too. The cards are stored in a compartment on the bottom of the game.

2  AA batteries required

reviewText:
We have Lego, Megablocks, Duplo, and Brick Genius blocks (B014VTUI9S). I initially had varying degrees of success with this mat. Initially we were using this mat on carpet. The flexing of the carpet contributed to the toppling of the blocks. It really is imperative that you use this mat on a solid surface. The only exception to this is the Megablocks on the larger block side. They fit very securely so you can use them with this mat while on carpet.

The standard Lego size side has to be used a solid surface for Lego, Megablocks, and Brick Genius blocks. This mat is compatible with all brands listed. The standard sides spacing is looser than the large block side. The blocks fit and they stand up fine but they aren't as secure of a fit as the large block side.

The large block side worked best with Duplo and Megablocks. I think the Megablocks fit the most secure. The Duplo fits but it's not as tight of a fit. Both will stand up well. They don't topple.

Overall I think this is a good investment. It works well with a variety of blocks. If your kiddo is used to playing on carpet just have them put this mat on a table for the best play results.

PROS:
Rolls up for easy storage
Double sided for traditional and larger blocks

CONS:
Mat initially has a chemical odor; it dissipated over night
Doesn't work well for carpet play

I remember making friendship bracelets with colorful embroidery floss when I was a kid - back then I didn't have an instruction book or fun little kit with all of the accessories to help me, I learned from my friends and purchased individual floss colors from the craft store, and figured out as I went along how to change colors and do different designs.  These are still as fun to make as I remember, and showing my niece how to do these using the book and materials provided brought back memories of the fun I had making these when I was her age.

This kit is perfect for the beginner who has not learned how to make friendship bracelets yet.  Simple yet detailed instructions in the book help them learn a variety of methods for making the bracelets, from very simple to a bit more advanced and detailed, there are over a dozen styles covered.  Once the basic skill of making the bracelets has been mastered, kids can use their own creativity to make their bracelets any way they want - the sky is the limit. This kit includes a mini loom, 6 colors of string, 8 beads, 6 felt charms and the idea book. Everything included stores in the clear plastic compartment on the front cover, which also has a built-in ruler for measurements.

The manufacturer's recommended age is 8 and up, but keep in mind this is a somewhat slow craft and requires patience so if you know the child you plan on buying for does not excel with crafts that take time you may want to consider something else.  Overall this is a great gift, a good quality product from Melissa & Doug.  I've purchased many products from them over the years and have never been disappointed.

My first Fascinations Deluxe Jellyfish Aquarium arrived with a few cracks in the plastic tank so I returned it and received the second one a couple of days later. I'm here to report that my first cracked aquarium had a very cheesy fake sand floor with a cheesy little starfish.  The second tank didn't have anything on the bottom.  I filled the bottom of my tank with river stones and will worn shells from my shell collection.  For good measure I also tossed in a few glow in the dark fake river stones.  I am very happy with how the bottom of the tank looks.  Very natural (if you can call glow in the dark river stones natural).

I was so eager to get this tank set up that I started in on it right away.  I was careful to do everything the instructions called for except that I didn't have any distilled water and it was near midnight so I wasn't going to go out in search of it.  In truth, I didn't think it would make all that much of a difference.  Oh how wrong I could be!  For the first 24 hours our little jellies huddled together at the top of the tank like frightened school children.  The next day I emptied the tank water and replaced it with distilled water.  The jellies were reintroduced and instantly began swimming all over the tank.  There was no period of adjustment, just happy arabesques all around.

The plants ARE a bit cheesy, but for now they are staying.  I might just get a nice background and do away with their mighty plasticness.

The aquarium itself is made out of pretty cheap plastic.  If I couldn't tell that just by looking at it, the first cracked one I received made that very clear.  I suspect it will scratch easily

As another reviewer recommended, I am partial to the red and blue light setting.

It you want to love this aquarium USE DISTILLED WATER. USE DISTILLED WATER.  USE DISTILLED WATER!!!!!

I can't speak to durability since I have only owned this a short time.  I will update the review if/when any issues present themselves

In truth, 4 stars seems too little but since I reserve 5 stars for mindblowing goodness in every way, I had to go with the 4.  I do like this little "aquarium."  It is very soothing and relaxing to watch.  I would love it if they would make an even larger version.

reviewText: Compared to inns and cathedrals, this is a much much better expansion which really adds some interesting concepts to the gameplay. Here some extra city tiles are privided with symbols for trade goods like wine, wheat, cloth etc. When you build cities with these tradegoods, you get a tradegood token for each tile that has this trade good. The tradegoods are provided to the player who completes the city even if there are no knights on that city. This mechanic provides an incentive for players to complete other people's cities. At the end of the game the highest number of trade goods owned by a player for that type of trade good provides the player with 10 bonus points which make a huge difference in points and deciding the winner. There is also a pig which when placed on a farm can increase the value of city tiles of complete cities touching the farms you own. Also there is a builder introduced which when placed on roads and cities (placing a builder requires that there already exists a knight or thief on the respective city or road), provide the ability to play an extra turn if a tile is placed touching the tile with the builder on it. Some interesting new features which really make carcassone into what it should have been in the initial base set. Great expansion!

This is an AMAZING toy!!! My 3 yr old couldn't stop playing with her own screwdriver!! She sat and played with the screws for THREE HOURS straight, I have never seen her play with any single toy for that long-EVER! She was also learning, not only fine motor, but also patterning and matching(which really she already knows, but practice never hurts). We have asked her to put all the screws in the matching colors, to put the green screws in the yellow holes, etc etc.

As background, my 3yr old is very girly! She plays dress up(and dresses the dog ;-)), picks her own clothing, has loved tulle and lace since she was old enough to see it...but she also loves to play with tools. Tools aren't just for boys or tomboys, I love that too, that I can teach my daughter that she can be anything she wants, that she can play dress up, dolls, and with her screws all in the same day!!

The construction is great, solid wood, yet smooth(no chance of splinters here), the paint is done well, the colors of the screws and holes match perfectly(which should always be the case, but isn't always so). I love that the screwdriver has a secure place in the block so the entire set stays together(less chance of loosing pieces)-basically there is a rubber ring inside the screwdriver hole(its a bit difficult to get it in and out the first few times, but not impossible-even for my 3yr old).

My now 11yr old son had an entire tool bench with screws and screwdriver, yet I like this better, it is portable, has a small footprint(it can fit in the diaperbag, my purse, toybox, etc), my son's was also plastic and this wood set is far more stable, no wobbling/bending screws or bench.

I bought this for my 3yr old daughter after purchasing children's furniture that she "helped" assemble. She couldn't get enough of the screwdriver, so when I saw this, I couldn't resist.

I truly thought this would be an occasional use toy or that she would loose interest fairly quickly, however, I have 2 more daughter's coming up(my young ones are 3, 2, 1) and at this price point, that would be ok. That was definitely not the case.

I am beyond happy that this toy was available for my daughter!!

Wow!  I LIKE this CAR!  Just recently, I received this and it was one of the best things I've ever gotten in the way of car models!  As a radio controlled model, it is good.  But as an authentic model car, it is even better--it's the supercar I've always wanted to have in 1/12 scale.  This Bugatti Veyron Super Sport is dark blue and light blue, and looks just like the real car.  It worked quite well, and is made of tough plastic--seemingly sturdy.

Not only is the authenticity good on the outside, but you can also see inside the car--there's an authentic interior.  And whenever I use this car, the lights illuminate!  The real car is the fastest production car in the world, with a top speed of 258 mph.  (With the rev limiter removed the top speed is 268 mph!)  What is more, it can go from 0 - 186.4 mph in only 14.6 seconds.  Horsepower is 1200!  As far as this car's remote is concerned, it works for me.  I also really like the silver lining on the car itself--it adds nicely to the authenticity.

I added some photos that I took of the car for everyone to see.  The remote itself isn't bad looking; it is red and black and says "Gear Maxx" on it.  I really love this car; it looks WONDERFUL as a display model!  Awesome car!

reviewText: This set it fabulous, from every aspect. It's built strong and sturdy, yet is absolutely simple to put together and take apart. The trucks are strong and the wheel move flawlessly (they don't stick or wobble). The launchers are easy to use. My 3 year old loves it, but most 2 year olds could probably do it as well. One launcher makes a truck ramp over a small ramp through a ring of "fire," and the other side launches a truck through a 360-degree loop. The only bad thing about this set is on the 360 degree loop side. Because it takes more momentum for the truck to make it all the way through the loop, the launcher has to be struck with a pretty good amount of force. But like I said, my 3 year old can do it. And the beauty of this set is that it is built to withstand harder hits to get the trucks to launch further. For the price range, you won't find a similar item that is better than this one.

The Queen & I typically do not debase ourselves by settling for "canned" dragon meat, but who has the time to hunt dragons these days?  Especially with their plummeting population and breeding issues - not to mention those pesky knights leaving perfectly good dragon meat out to rot after saving damsels in distress.  Smoked dragon meat fresh off the bone is becoming harder and harder to find.

So this canned dragon meat allows me to both rule my kingdom AND have the luxury of simply walking down to the royal dining room to enjoy a meal packed with that certain special "je ne sais quoi" that only REAL dragon meet can provide.

So never again settle for "faux dragon surprise" (which is, as you know, made up of primarily Manticore, Chimera, and Hydra meat) - Entertainment Earth's Canned Dragon Meet is the only way to go!

reviewText:
I received Creationary for Christmas and have played it twice. Once with an eight-year old. and once with a group of adults (I was the youngest at 33!)

Both times we had fun playing but there are few challenges with this game. One is packaging. It needs a lid for the inner tray or maybe a deeper tray. I found that I had to use Press N Seal wrap to keep the bricks in their spots between uses, otherwise transporting or storing this game caused all the bricks to jumble together. Not a huge problem, but if you want to quickly sit down and play, having the pieces mixed together is harder to start with.

The pictures on the cards are hard to build. The 8 year old had fun building but didn't know what a lot of the pictures were meant to be-she had no idea what the Eiffel Tower was. The adults, admittedly not Lego fans, had no idea where to start building with even the "easy" pictures. They knew what the object was, but didn't know where to even start. Perhaps a beginning set of cards where the object is shown already built with bricks so people get more of an idea of where to start and are not as overwhelmed?

The bricks themselves seem, at first, to be plentiful. And, to be honest, the number is fine. However, the basic building blocks are lacking. You might be given 2 yellow 2X2, but need 8. You can mix colors, yes, but overall, I found that the basic ones are lacking. I may be adding more over time as I figure out the ones we need the most (such as more roof tiles!).

That being said, we all had a lot of fun playing and trying to guess what someone was building. It will be a game I pull out often in the future. I doubt a non-Lego lover would end up with this game as it seems to be geared towards those who already build and have an idea on how the bricks work together.
